title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄序
易曰聖人久於其道而天下
化成又曰觀乎人文以化成
天下惟我
皇明
太祖高皇帝以武功定天下所在
輒建學養士三年例一開科
===
取之迄
列聖率遵是道蓋百三十有餘年
亦旣三十有餘科矣人文之
化以久而成允有徵於易所
云者粤自先
憲宗純皇帝以成化改元固已應
其時矣今
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄序

易曰：「聖人久於其道，而天下化成。」又曰：「觀乎人文，以化成天下。」惟我皇明太祖高皇帝以武功定天下，所在輒建學養士，三年例一開科取之。迄列聖率遵是道，蓋百三十有餘年，亦旣三十有餘科矣。人文之化，以久而成，允有徵於易所云者。粤自先憲宗純皇帝以成化改元，固已應其時矣。今
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

The Book of Changes says: “The sage abides long in his Way, and the transformation of all under Heaven is accomplished.” It also says: “Observe human culture, and thereby transform all under Heaven.” Our august Ming dynasty’s Emperor Taizu Gao pacified all under Heaven through military achievement. Wherever his rule extended, he established schools to nurture scholars, instituting examinations once every three years to select them. The successive sage emperors have all followed this course. Some one hundred and thirty years and more have passed, and more than thirty examinations have already been held. The transforming influence of human culture has reached fruition through long continuance, truly bearing out what the Book of Changes says.

When the late Emperor Xianzong Chun inaugurated the Chenghua era—“Accomplished Transformation”—the name indeed accorded with its time. Now…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
皇上顧化爲已成改元弘治治不
以人文而弘邪治愈弘斯化
愈成而無替矣猗歟休哉十
有一年歲值戊午寔惟開科
之期湖廣藩臬舉行如例先
是白於巡按監察御史王恩
相與計曰夫開科以文取士
===
治之弘化之成悉有攸繫先
務尚有急於是者哉乃走使
具幣聘曰宗等以司文衡維
時巡撫右副都御史閻仲宇
撫治右副都御史黎福清戎
監察御史牟道協德一心作
興士風鎭守太監劉雅分守
punctuated: 皇上顧化爲已成，改元弘治。治不以人文而弘邪？治愈弘，斯化愈成而無替矣。猗歟休哉！十有一年，歲值戊午，寔惟開科之期。湖廣藩臬舉行如例。先是，白於巡按監察御史王恩，相與計曰：「夫開科以文取士，治之弘、化之成，悉有攸繫，先務尚有急於是者哉？」乃走使具幣，聘曰宗等以司文衡。維時，巡撫右副都御史閻仲宇、撫治右副都御史黎福、清戎監察御史牟道，協德一心，作興士風。鎭守太監劉雅、分守
translation_en:
…His Majesty, considering that cultural transformation had already been accomplished, changed the reign title to Hongzhi, “Broadening Governance.” Is governance not broadened through cultural refinement? The broader governance becomes, the more fully this transformation is accomplished, without decline. Ah, how splendid!

In the eleventh year, the year wuwu, the appointed time came to hold the examination. Huguang’s Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions conducted it according to precedent. Beforehand, they reported to the Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Wang En, and deliberated together, saying: “Holding examinations to select men through their writing has a bearing on both the broadening of governance and the accomplishment of cultural transformation. Among our foremost duties, could anything be more urgent than this?” They therefore dispatched a messenger with gifts to invite Yuezong and others to take charge of judging the compositions.

At that time, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Yan Zhongyu, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Fu, charged with pacification, and Investigating Censor Mou Dao, charged with inspecting military affairs, united in virtue and purpose to invigorate the ethos of the scholars. The Regional Command Eunuch Liu Ya and the eunuch assigned to regional defense …

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
太監李祺總兵官鎮遠侯顧
溥又相與從臾之士風益勵
而御史王恩寔監臨焉爰合
提學僉事楊春所取士覆閲
之得一千五百有竒内而提
調監試則左布政使李濬按
察使吳雄左參政梁方副使
鄭惟桓外而防範賛畫則右
布政使熊佑右參政夏祚副
使湯全陳孜顧源陳寓馮鎬
左參議胡瑞右參議陳睿夏
昂王璽僉事曹玉陳雍張鎮
危容鄭軾祝祥至凡執事咸
遴選以充三試之拔其尤者
punctuated: 太監李祺、總兵官鎮遠侯顧溥又相與從臾之，士風益勵，而御史王恩寔監臨焉。爰合提學僉事楊春所取士，覆閲之，得一千五百有竒。内而提調監試，則左布政使李濬、按察使吳雄、左參政梁方、副使鄭惟桓；外而防範賛畫，則右布政使熊佑、右參政夏祚、副使湯全、陳孜、顧源、陳寓、馮鎬、左參議胡瑞、右參議陳睿、夏昂、王璽、僉事曹玉、陳雍、張鎮、危容、鄭軾、祝祥。至凡執事，咸遴選以充。三試之，拔其尤者
translation_en:
…Grand Director Li Qi and Regional Commander Gu Pu, Marquis of Zhenyuan, likewise joined in encouraging the undertaking, further invigorating the scholars’ morale. Censor Wang En served as Supervising Official. The candidates selected by Yang Chun, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in charge of education, were then assembled and reviewed, yielding somewhat more than fifteen hundred men.

Within the examination compound, those responsible for managing and overseeing the examination were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Jun, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Wu Xiong, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Liang Fang, and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zheng Weihuan. Outside, those responsible for security and assisting with arrangements were Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Xiong You; Right Administration Vice Commissioner Xia Zuo; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Tang Quan, Chen Zi, Gu Yuan, Chen Yu, and Feng Gao; Left Administration Assistant Commissioner Hu Rui; Right Administration Assistant Commissioners Chen Rui, Xia Ang, and Wang Xi; and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Cao Yu, Chen Yong, Zhang Zhen, Wei Rong, Zheng Shi, and Zhu Xiang. All other functionaries, too, were carefully selected to fill their posts. The candidates were examined in three sessions, and the most outstanding among them were selected…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
八十五人乃刻其名氏與文
之優者為鄉試錄錄成以崇
宜序諸首竊惟湖廣南方大
藩地介乎離離也者明也萬
物皆相見南方之卦也蓋據
江漢上游漫不與他藩鄰海
徼一隅者等延袤三數千里
===
衡嶽巋然當其中中州清淑
之氣蜿蜒磅礴之所在者離
文明之象而湖藩固文明之
地哉為其士者生長文明之
地瞻文明之象養之學宮肄
習乎聖經賢傳暨凡百家子
史皆是文也優游厭飫積有
punctuated: 八十五人，乃刻其名氏與文之優者，為《鄉試錄》。錄成，以崇宜序諸首。竊惟湖廣，南方大藩，地介乎離。離也者，明也，萬物皆相見，南方之卦也。蓋據江漢上游，漫不與他藩鄰海徼一隅者等，延袤三數千里，衡嶽巋然當其中，中州清淑之氣蜿蜒磅礴之所在者。離，文明之象，而湖藩固文明之地哉！為其士者，生長文明之地，瞻文明之象，養之學宮，肄習乎聖經賢傳，暨凡百家子史，皆是文也。優游厭飫，積有
translation_en:
…eighty-five men. Their names and the finest of their compositions were then engraved for printing as the Record of the Provincial Examination. When the record was completed, I, Chongyi, was asked to place a preface at its beginning.

I humbly reflect that Huguang is a great southern province, situated in the quarter corresponding to the trigram Li. Li signifies brightness: all things become visible to one another; it is the trigram of the south. Occupying the upper reaches of the Jiang and Han rivers, the province is by no means comparable to other provinces confined to a coastal or frontier corner. It extends two or three thousand li, with Mount Heng standing majestically at its center. Here the pure and harmonious vital energies of the central lands wind their way and gather in expansive abundance. Li is the image of cultural brilliance, and surely Huguang is indeed a land of cultural brilliance!

Its scholars are born and raised in this land of cultural brilliance and behold its image. Nurtured in the schools, they study the classics of the sages and the commentaries of the worthies, together with the writings of the various masters and the histories—all of which constitute this literary culture. At leisure they immerse themselves in it and drink their fill, accumulating …

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
年歲一旦鏖戰場屋摛之筆
端鋪張之紙上衍是文之緒
餘而爲之文風簷寸晷之下
才美畢露詎不有昔人所謂
光焰萬丈長者出於其間邪
日宗等疲精殫神連校數旦
暮於是乎抜而取之務使過
===
眼而不爲日五色之迷庶幾
不負於其文矣雖然是科之
文日宗固占知其非復昔時
之文之比何則是科歲值戊
午午正離之所位是歲也非
文明之歲而何湖藩士值文
明之歲以其文見取於是科
punctuated:
年歲，一旦鏖戰場屋，摛之筆端，鋪張之紙上，衍是文之緒餘而爲之文。風簷寸晷之下，才美畢露，詎不有昔人所謂「光焰萬丈長」者出於其間邪？日宗等疲精殫神，連校數旦暮，於是乎抜而取之，務使過眼而不爲日五色之迷，庶幾不負於其文矣。
雖然，是科之文，日宗固占知其非復昔時之文之比。何則？是科歲值戊午，午正離之所位，是歲也非文明之歲而何？湖藩士值文明之歲，以其文見取於是科
translation_en:
…for years. Once they enter the fierce contest of the examination hall, they express it through their brushes and spread it across the paper, drawing upon the abundant legacy of this literary culture to compose their essays. Beneath the wind-swept eaves, within the brief allotted time, their talents and accomplishments are fully revealed. Surely among them must emerge works possessing what a writer of old called “a radiant blaze ten thousand fathoms high”? We, Rizong and the others, exhausted our mental energies, reviewing papers through successive days and nights, and selected the outstanding ones. We strove, as the papers passed before our eyes, not to be dazzled by their five colors [?], hoping thereby to do justice to their writing.
Nevertheless, Rizong is certain [?] that the writing in this examination can no longer be compared with that of earlier times. Why? This examination falls in the wuwu year, and wu corresponds precisely to the position of the trigram Li. If this is not a year of cultural brilliance, what is it? The scholars of Huguang, encountering such a year of cultural brilliance, have been selected in this examination on the strength of their writing…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其於是文則亦無愛哉矧今
皇上南面而聽天下嚮明而治其
文煥若堯重華若舜丕顯若
文王弘文之治愈有以成天
下同文之化矣爾湖藩士行
將觀光
上國與天下士會角於南宮倏
===
復見取有官守言責之寄以
其文潤
皇猷飾治具弼我
皇明文明之治於無窮則亦有無
窮之聞顧不偉歟曰宗固不
能恝然無情於是文也不能
不顒然有望於湖藩士也
punctuated: 其於是文，則亦無愛哉？矧今皇上南面而聽天下，嚮明而治，其文煥若堯，重華若舜，丕顯若文王。弘文之治，愈有以成天下同文之化矣。爾湖藩士，行將觀光上國，與天下士會角於南宮，倏復見取，有官守言責之寄，以其文潤皇猷，飾治具，弼我皇明文明之治於無窮，則亦有無窮之聞，顧不偉歟？曰宗固不能恝然無情於是文也，不能不顒然有望於湖藩士也。
translation_en:
…could they, then, have no affection for these writings? Moreover, His Majesty now faces south to hear the affairs of the realm, turning toward the light as he governs. His cultural brilliance shines like Yao’s, his successive splendors resemble Shun’s, and his manifest glory resembles King Wen’s. His rule, which promotes literary culture, is all the better able to bring about the realm’s transformation through a shared culture.

You scholars of Huguang will soon behold the splendor of the imperial capital and compete with scholars from throughout the realm at the Ministry of Rites in the Metropolitan Examination. Soon you will again be selected and entrusted with official duties and the responsibility to speak out. With your literary accomplishments, you will embellish imperial policy, adorn the instruments of government, and assist our august Ming dynasty in perpetuating its enlightened rule without end. Then your renown, too, will endure without end. Would this not be magnificent? I, Rizong [?], surely cannot remain indifferent and unmoved by these writings; I cannot but cherish earnest hopes for the scholars of Huguang.

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
河南開封府許州儒學學正
楊日宗謹序
punctuated: 河南開封府許州儒學學正楊日宗謹序。
translation_en: Preface respectfully composed by Yang Rizong, School Instructor of the Confucian School of Xuzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan.

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
弘治十一年湖廣鄉試
監臨官
巡按湖廣監察御史王恩〔克承浙江餘姚縣人丁未進士〕
提調官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司左布政使李濬〔德深直隸武進縣人己丑進士〕
湖廣等處承宣布政使司左參政梁方〔惟義廣東南海縣人壬辰進士〕
監試官
湖廣等處提刑按察司按察使吳雄〔文英浙江仁和縣人戊戌進士〕
湖廣等處提刑按察司副使鄭惟桓〔用文浙江常山縣人戊戌進士〕
===
考試官
河南開封府許州儒學學正楊曰宗〔汝慶福建莆田縣人壬子貢士〕
浙江湖州府長興縣儒學教諭俞鎧〔武元直隸無錫縣人己酉貢士〕
同考試官
廣西南寧府橫州儒學學正潘常〔秉彝福建閩縣人癸卯貢士〕
直隸鳳陽府泗州儒學學正蔡廷周〔希旦江西豐城縣人己酉貢士〕
直隸鎮江府金壇縣儒學教諭張居仁〔元之浙江新昌縣人丙午貢士〕
山西平陽府聞喜縣儒學教諭蔣忠〔廷臣直隸歸德衛人庚子貢士〕
山東濟南府章丘縣儒學教諭許性〔秉彝浙江天台縣人壬子貢士〕
punctuated:
弘治十一年湖廣鄉試。

監臨官：巡按湖廣監察御史王恩〔克承，浙江餘姚縣人，丁未進士〕。

提調官：湖廣等處承宣布政使司左布政使李濬〔德深，直隸武進縣人，己丑進士〕。湖廣等處承宣布政使司左參政梁方〔惟義，廣東南海縣人，壬辰進士〕。

監試官：湖廣等處提刑按察司按察使吳雄〔文英，浙江仁和縣人，戊戌進士〕。湖廣等處提刑按察司副使鄭惟桓〔用文，浙江常山縣人，戊戌進士〕。

考試官：河南開封府許州儒學學正楊曰宗〔汝慶，福建莆田縣人，壬子貢士〕。浙江湖州府長興縣儒學教諭俞鎧〔武元，直隸無錫縣人，己酉貢士〕。

同考試官：廣西南寧府橫州儒學學正潘常〔秉彝，福建閩縣人，癸卯貢士〕。直隸鳳陽府泗州儒學學正蔡廷周〔希旦，江西豐城縣人，己酉貢士〕。直隸鎮江府金壇縣儒學教諭張居仁〔元之，浙江新昌縣人，丙午貢士〕。山西平陽府聞喜縣儒學教諭蔣忠〔廷臣，直隸歸德衛人，庚子貢士〕。山東濟南府章丘縣儒學教諭許性〔秉彝，浙江天台縣人，壬子貢士〕。
translation_en:
Huguang Provincial Examination in the eleventh year of Hongzhi (1498).

Supervising Official
Wang En, Investigating Censor on inspection duty in Huguang, had the courtesy name Kecheng and was from Yuyao County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the dingwei year.

Proctors
Li Jun, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Huguang, had the courtesy name Deshen and was from Wujin County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jichou year.
Liang Fang, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of Huguang, had the courtesy name Weiyi and was from Nanhai County, Guangdong. He became a metropolitan graduate in the renchen year.

Examination Monitors
Wu Xiong, Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang, had the courtesy name Wenying and was from Renhe County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the wuxu year.
Zheng Weihuan, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Huguang, had the courtesy name Yongwen and was from Changshan County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the wuxu year.

Examiners
Yang Yuezong, Instructor at the Confucian School of Xuzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Ruqing and was from Putian County, Fujian. He became a tribute student (gongshi) in the renzi year.
Yu Kai, Instructor at the Confucian School of Changxing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Wuyuan and was from Wuxi County, Zhili. He became a tribute student in the jiyou year.

Associate Examiners
Pan Chang, Instructor at the Confucian School of Hengzhou, Nanning Prefecture, Guangxi, had the courtesy name Bingyi and was from Min County, Fujian. He became a tribute student in the guimao year.
Cai Tingzhou, Instructor at the Confucian School of Sizhou, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Xidan and was from Fengcheng County, Jiangxi. He became a tribute student in the jiyou year.
Zhang Juren, Instructor at the Confucian School of Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Yuanzhi and was from Xinchang County, Zhejiang. He became a tribute student in the bingwu year.
Jiang Zhong, Instructor at the Confucian School of Wenxi County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, had the courtesy name Tingchen and was from Guide Guard, Zhili. He became a tribute student in the gengzi year.
Xu Xing, Instructor at the Confucian School of Zhangqiu County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, had the courtesy name Bingyi and was from Tiantai County, Zhejiang. He became a tribute student in the renzi year.

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
陝西延安府甘泉縣儒學教諭李健〔子乾四川崇慶州人壬子貢士〕
四川嘉定州峨眉縣儒學教諭易紘〔道張江西吉水縣人壬子貢士〕
直隸寧國府涇縣儒學教諭陳垣〔子崇浙江臨海縣人壬子貢士〕
印卷官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司照磨所照磨劉溥〔公濟直隸懷寧縣人庚戌進士〕
湖廣等處提刑按察司經歷司知事張統〔公冕直隸南陵縣人監生〕

武昌府知府冒政〔有恒直隸泰州人乙未進士〕
長沙府知府王瑫〔宗玉浙江鄞縣人辛丑進士〕

荊州府知府吳彥華〔汝和應天府句容縣人辛丑進士〕
德安府知府王宥〔敬之浙江淳安縣人辛丑進士〕
彌封官
衡州府同知鄧淮〔安濟江西吉水縣人辛丑進士〕
襄陽府同知周楫〔濟之四川內江縣人丁未進士〕
岳州府推官弓元〔大方應天府江浦縣人丙辰進士〕
德安府推官胡世寧〔永清浙江仁和縣人癸丑進士〕
謄錄官

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
周監於二代郁郁乎文哉
和也者天下之達道也
仁者無不愛也急親賢之為務
易
夫大人者與天地合其德
巽而耳目聰明柔進而上行得中而應乎
剛是以元亨
===
繼之者善也成之者性也
利用安身以崇德也
書
克勤于邦克儉于家
聖謨洋洋嘉言孔彰
乃服惟弘王應保殷民亦惟助王宅天命
作新民
惟周公克慎厥始惟君陳克和厥中惟公
克成厥終
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
周監於二代，郁郁乎文哉！
和也者，天下之達道也。
仁者無不愛也，急親賢之為務。

易
夫大人者，與天地合其德。
巽而耳目聰明，柔進而上行，得中而應乎剛，是以元亨。
繼之者善也，成之者性也。
利用安身，以崇德也。

書
克勤于邦，克儉于家。
聖謨洋洋，嘉言孔彰。
乃服惟弘王，應保殷民，亦惟助王宅天命，作新民。
惟周公克慎厥始，惟君陳克和厥中，惟公克成厥終。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
Zhou took the two preceding dynasties as its models. How splendid its culture!
Harmony is the universally followed Way of all under Heaven.
The benevolent person loves everyone, but makes associating closely with the worthy his most urgent task.

Book of Changes (Yijing)
The great man accords in his virtue with Heaven and Earth.
Yielding, yet keen of hearing and clear of sight; the yielding advances and moves upward, attains the central position, and responds to the firm. Hence there is supreme success.
What continues it is goodness; what brings it to completion is human nature.
It is beneficial to secure oneself, thereby exalting one's virtue.

Book of Documents (Shangshu)
He was diligent in affairs of state and frugal in his household.
The sage's counsels were far-reaching; his excellent words were greatly illuminating.
In your office, magnify the king, attend to and protect the people of Yin, and also assist the king in securing Heaven's mandate and renewing the people.
The Duke of Zhou was able to take care at the beginning; Jun Chen was able to maintain harmony in the middle; you, my lord, can bring it to completion at the end.

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
詩
如金如錫如圭如璧
我有嘉賓德音孔昭
上天之載無聲無臭儀刑文王萬邦作孚
俾侯于魯大啟爾宇為周室輔
春秋
六月雨〔僖公三年〕
宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯會晉師于棽林伐鄭〔宣公元年〕公會晉師于瓦〔定公八年〕
===
叔孫舍至自晉〔昭公二十四年〕
叔孫州仇帥師墮郈季孫斯仲孫何忌
帥師墮費〔定公十二年〕
禮記
悉其聰明致其忠愛以盡之
禮樂刑政四達而不悖則王道備矣
誠信之謂盡盡之謂敬敬盡然後可以事
神明
以之軍旅有禮故武功成也
punctuated:
詩
如金如錫，如圭如璧。
我有嘉賓，德音孔昭。
上天之載，無聲無臭。儀刑文王，萬邦作孚。
俾侯于魯，大啟爾宇，為周室輔。

春秋
六月，雨。〔僖公三年〕
宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯會晉師于棽林，伐鄭。〔宣公元年〕公會晉師于瓦。〔定公八年〕
叔孫舍至自晉。〔昭公二十四年〕
叔孫州仇帥師墮郈，季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費。〔定公十二年〕

禮記
悉其聰明，致其忠愛，以盡之。
禮樂刑政，四達而不悖，則王道備矣。
誠信之謂盡，盡之謂敬，敬盡然後可以事神明。
以之軍旅，有禮，故武功成也。
translation_en:
Book of Odes

“Like gold, like tin; like a jade tablet, like a jade disc.”
“I have worthy guests; their virtuous reputation shines brightly.”
“The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell. Take King Wen as your model, and the myriad states will put their trust in you.”
“He made you lord in Lu, greatly expanding your domain, to serve as a support for the royal house of Zhou.”

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In the sixth month, it rained.” 〔Third year of Duke Xi〕
“The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao joined the army of Jin at Chenlin [?] and attacked Zheng.” 〔First year of Duke Xuan〕 “The duke met the army of Jin at Wa.” 〔Eighth year of Duke Ding〕
“Shusun She returned from Jin.” 〔Twenty-fourth year of Duke Zhao〕
“Shusun Zhouqiu led troops to demolish the fortifications of Hou; Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led troops to demolish the fortifications of Fei.” 〔Twelfth year of Duke Ding〕

Book of Rites

“Fully employ your powers of hearing and sight, and bring your loyalty and love to the utmost, so as to fulfill your duty completely.”
“When rites, music, punishments, and government operate everywhere without conflicting, the Way of the Kings is complete.”
“Sincerity and trustworthiness constitute complete fulfillment; complete fulfillment constitutes reverence. Only after achieving reverence and complete fulfillment can one serve the spirits.”
“When this is applied to military affairs, ritual propriety prevails; therefore military achievements are accomplished.”

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第貳場
論
士以名節忠義為本
詔誥表内科一道
擬漢定太初曆以正月為歲首詔太初元
年
擬唐以馬周為監察御史誥貞觀三年
擬宋以韓琦為陝西安撫使謝表康定元
年
===
判語五條
選用軍職
收養孤老
禁止迎送
辯明冤枉
脩理倉庫
第叄場
策五道
問嘗伏讀我
punctuated:
第貳場。
論：士以名節忠義為本。
詔誥表内科一道：擬漢定太初曆，以正月為歲首詔，太初元年。擬唐以馬周為監察御史誥，貞觀三年。擬宋以韓琦為陝西安撫使謝表，康定元年。
判語五條：選用軍職。收養孤老。禁止迎送。辯明冤枉。脩理倉庫。
第叄場。
策五道。
問：嘗伏讀我
translation_en:
Second Session

Discourse: A scholar takes reputation, moral integrity, loyalty, and righteousness as his foundation.

One question from the categories of edict, proclamation of appointment, and memorial [?]:
Compose an edict as if issued under the Han establishing the Taichu calendar and making the first month the beginning of the year. First year of Taichu.
Compose a proclamation as if issued under the Tang appointing Ma Zhou as Investigating Censor. Third year of Zhenguan.
Compose a memorial of thanks as if submitted under the Song for the appointment of Han Qi as Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi. First year of Kangding.

Five legal judgments:
Selection and appointment of military officers.
Provision of care for the orphaned and elderly without support.
Prohibition of ceremonial receptions and send-offs.
Investigation and clarification of wrongful accusations.
Repair of granaries and storehouses.

Third Session

Five policy questions.

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
太宗文皇帝御製性理大全書序有曰聖人未
生道在天地聖人既生道在聖人聖人
已往道在六經六經者聖人為治之迹
也大哉
王言誠知聖人之治本於道也然未識所謂
道者何道也千聖一心萬古一理洪惟
我
朝自
太祖高皇帝肇造鴻基創制立法
===
列聖相承勵精圖治莫不各有作述若
大誥三編我
太祖高皇帝之所條成也
為善陰騭
孝順事實二書
太宗文皇帝之所編輯也
宣宗章皇帝則有
五倫書之頒
英宗睿皇帝則又有
punctuated: 太宗文皇帝御製《性理大全書》序有曰：「聖人未生，道在天地；聖人既生，道在聖人；聖人已往，道在六經。六經者，聖人為治之迹也。」大哉，王言！誠知聖人之治本於道也。然未識所謂道者，何道也？千聖一心，萬古一理。洪惟我朝，自太祖高皇帝肇造鴻基，創制立法，列聖相承，勵精圖治，莫不各有作述。若《大誥》三編，我太祖高皇帝之所條成也；《為善陰騭》《孝順事實》二書，太宗文皇帝之所編輯也；宣宗章皇帝則有《五倫書》之頒；英宗睿皇帝則又有
translation_en: …the imperially composed preface by Emperor Taizong Wen to the Complete Compendium of Human Nature and Principle (Xingli daquan shu) says: “Before the sages were born, the Way resided in Heaven and Earth. Once the sages were born, the Way resided in the sages. After the sages had passed away, the Way resided in the Six Classics. The Six Classics are the traces of the sages’ practice of government.” How great are these royal words! We indeed understand that the government of the sages is rooted in the Way. Yet we do not understand: what Way is this so-called Way? The thousand sages share one mind; through all ages there is one principle. Reverently considering our dynasty, from the time Emperor Taizu Gao established its grand foundations, created institutions, and laid down laws, successive sage emperors have applied themselves diligently to good government. Each has composed or compiled works. The three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da gao), for example, were drawn up article by article by our Emperor Taizu Gao. The two books Hidden Recompense for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and Factual Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi) were compiled by Emperor Taizong Wen. Emperor Xuanzong Zhang promulgated the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu), while Emperor Yingzong Rui, in turn, had…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
大明一統志之作
憲宗純皇帝又
命諸儒臣續編資治通鑑綱目
聖祖神宗宸章奎翰輝耀古今如日中天萬方
仰照觀其文字似各異指究其旨歸無
非勸善懲惡所以使民避凶趨吉全性
分篤倫理歸於至治而已治天下之道
豈復有加於此哉誠與古聖人之六經
脗合無間同一為治之迹也然其所以
===
脗合無間者何在可各舉一二以實之
歟今我
皇上繼體守成孳孳
宵旰日御
經筵講求治理凡所以稱制臨決訓飭臣民
無非有得六經之旨申明
祖宗之制而天下臣民惟皇敷言是訓是行允
光
前烈愈隆而愈盛也諸士子誦習六經服膺
punctuated: 《大明一統志》之作。憲宗純皇帝又命諸儒臣續編《資治通鑑綱目》。聖祖神宗，宸章奎翰，輝耀古今，如日中天，萬方仰照。觀其文字，似各異指；究其旨歸，無非勸善懲惡，所以使民避凶趨吉，全性分，篤倫理，歸於至治而已。治天下之道，豈復有加於此哉？誠與古聖人之六經脗合無間，同一為治之迹也。然其所以脗合無間者何在？可各舉一二以實之歟？今我皇上繼體守成，孳孳宵旰，日御經筵，講求治理。凡所以稱制臨決，訓飭臣民，無非有得六經之旨，申明祖宗之制。而天下臣民，惟皇敷言是訓是行，允光前烈，愈隆而愈盛也。諸士子誦習六經，服膺
translation_en:
…the compilation of the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi). Emperor Xianzong Chun also ordered the Confucian scholar-officials to compile a continuation of the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government (Zizhi tongjian gangmu). The imperial compositions and writings of our sagely ancestors and divine forebears illuminate past and present, like the sun at the zenith, toward whose radiance all lands look up. Examining their wording, one might think that each has a different purport; investigating their ultimate intent, however, one finds nothing other than encouragement of good and chastisement of evil. Their purpose is simply to enable the people to avoid misfortune and seek good fortune, preserve their allotted moral nature intact, strengthen ethical relationships, and attain the most perfect order. Could any way of governing the realm surpass this? They indeed accord seamlessly with the Six Classics of the ancient sages and follow the same course in bringing about good government. Yet wherein lies this seamless accord? Can you cite one or two examples from each to substantiate it?

Now our Emperor has inherited the throne and preserves the achievements of his predecessors, diligently attending to affairs from before dawn until late in the day. He attends the Classics Colloquium daily to investigate the principles of government. Whenever he issues decrees, personally decides affairs, or instructs and admonishes officials and people, he invariably shows his grasp of the purport of the Six Classics and elucidates the institutions of his ancestors. Throughout the realm, officials and people take the Emperor’s pronouncements alone as their instruction and guide to conduct, truly bringing glory to the great achievements of his predecessors, with ever greater eminence and flourishing. You candidates have recited and studied the Six Classics and taken to heart…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
聖訓有年于茲矣願明揚以對使天下後世知
我
朝
列聖治化之所由盛
問忠孝常道類能言之亦能行之惟若臨
大節有不能兩全者其幾間不容髮苟
察之毫釐不精則處之多有失當者矣
試將往事評之陳情養祖孝矣宜忠也
而何有偽朝之稱奉表勤王忠矣宜孝
===
也而何有絶裾之忍守城棄母而泣血
喪生者忠孝全矣其處之果盡道乎報
君備父而隨父殺身者忠孝全矣其處
之果盡善乎漢有二母同質敵營也其
子或事漢而功則成或從母而名墮泯
其心孰為安歟晉有二父同死非命也
其子或從王而節以著或讎晉而身終
隱其事孰為得歟又有貧躬執爨而先
憂後樂迎母廬墓而盡忠報國者其人
punctuated:
聖訓有年于茲矣，願明揚以對，使天下後世知我朝列聖治化之所由盛。

問：忠孝常道，類能言之，亦能行之。惟若臨大節，有不能兩全者，其幾間不容髮。苟察之毫釐不精，則處之多有失當者矣。試將往事評之：陳情養祖，孝矣，宜忠也，而何有偽朝之稱？奉表勤王，忠矣，宜孝也，而何有絶裾之忍？守城棄母而泣血喪生者，忠孝全矣，其處之果盡道乎？報君備父而隨父殺身者，忠孝全矣，其處之果盡善乎？漢有二母同質敵營也，其子或事漢而功則成，或從母而名墮。泯其心，孰為安歟？晉有二父同死非命也，其子或從王而節以著，或讎晉而身終隱。其事孰為得歟？又有貧躬執爨而先憂後樂，迎母廬墓而盡忠報國者，其人
translation_en:
…the sagely instructions for many years now. We hope you will set forth their meaning clearly in your replies, so that the world and later generations may understand how the rule and transforming influence of the successive sage emperors of our dynasty came to flourish.

Question: Loyalty and filial piety are enduring moral principles. People generally can speak of them and can also put them into practice. Yet when confronting a decisive moral test, one may be unable to fulfill both. At such a juncture, the distinction is so fine that not even a hair can fit between the alternatives. If one’s discernment falls short by the slightest degree, one’s response will often be inappropriate. Try evaluating the following past events.

To state one’s circumstances in a memorial and care for one’s grandmother was filial, and ought also to have been loyal; why, then, speak of a “spurious dynasty”? To submit a memorial and hasten to the sovereign’s aid was loyal, and ought also to have been filial; why, then, have the heart to sever one’s robe and leave one’s mother behind? The man who defended a city and abandoned his mother, then wept blood and died, fulfilled both loyalty and filial piety; but did his response truly accord fully with the Way? The man who repaid his ruler, made provision for his father [?], and followed his father in giving up his life fulfilled both loyalty and filial piety; but was his response truly perfect?

Under the Han, two mothers were alike held hostage in enemy camps. One son served the Han and achieved success; the other followed his mother and his reputation fell. Considering their intentions [?], which could be at peace? Under the Jin, two fathers alike met unnatural deaths. One son followed the prince and became renowned for his integrity; the other treated the Jin as his enemy and spent the rest of his life in seclusion. Which acted rightly?

There were also those who, though poor and personally tending the cooking fire, worried before others and took their pleasure after them; and those who brought their mothers to live with them, dwelt in huts beside their parents’ graves, and devoted their utmost loyalty to repaying the state. These men…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
可歴指歟昔人有言凡學者所以學為
忠與孝也諸士子志學有年矣不知居
平日曾何以為孝自今日將何以為忠
抑忠孝兼全如往哲者以何人為可法
患難當處如前事者以何道而能濟幸
相與講明之毋隱毋略
問書所以載道能明夫書則明夫道矣然
太博則學者無從入太約則徒為徑約
故必由約而博由博而反之約則其道
===
得矣故紫陽夫子與伯恭先生讀周子
二程張子之書懼其浩瀚不便初學故
掇取其關於大體切於日用者纂為一
書之約首之以求端次之以用力次之
以處己又次之以治人不知其求端用
力者何事處己治人者何道闢邪所以
衛正也為我兼愛異端也何為此道同
出於儒直内方外儒道也何謂異端得
此失彼答導氣之問其言何術答神僊
punctuated:
可歴指歟？昔人有言：「凡學者，所以學為忠與孝也。」諸士子志學有年矣，不知居平日曾何以為孝，自今日將何以為忠？抑忠孝兼全如往哲者，以何人為可法？患難當處如前事者，以何道而能濟？幸相與講明之，毋隱毋略。

問：書所以載道，能明夫書，則明夫道矣。然太博則學者無從入，太約則徒為徑約。故必由約而博，由博而反之約，則其道得矣。故紫陽夫子與伯恭先生讀周子、二程、張子之書，懼其浩瀚不便初學，故掇取其關於大體、切於日用者，纂為一書之約。首之以求端，次之以用力，次之以處己，又次之以治人。不知其求端、用力者何事，處己、治人者何道？闢邪所以衛正也，為我、兼愛，異端也，何為此道同出於儒？直内方外，儒道也，何謂異端得此失彼？答導氣之問，其言何術？答神僊
translation_en:
…can these men be identified one by one? Someone of old said: “All who study do so to learn loyalty and filial piety.” You candidates have devoted yourselves to learning for years. How have you practiced filial piety in your everyday lives, and how will you practice loyalty from this day forward? Whom can you take as a model for fulfilling both loyalty and filial piety, as did the worthy thinkers of the past? When confronted with adversity like that in the foregoing cases, by what Way can you come through it successfully? Please discuss and elucidate these matters together, concealing nothing and omitting nothing.

Question: Books convey the Way. If one can understand the books, one can understand the Way. Yet if their scope is too broad, learners have no point of entry; if too condensed, they offer merely a shortcut. Thus one must proceed from the essentials to breadth, and from breadth return to the essentials: only then can the Way be attained. Accordingly, when Master Ziyang and Master Bogong read the writings of Master Zhou, the two Cheng masters, and Master Zhang, they feared that their vast extent would make them difficult for beginners. They therefore selected passages bearing on the larger framework and directly relevant to daily practice, compiling them into a single concise book. They began with seeking the starting point, followed by applying effort, then conducting oneself, and then governing others. What matters are involved in seeking the starting point and applying effort? What is the Way of conducting oneself and governing others?

Refuting error serves to defend what is correct. “Acting for oneself” and “impartial caring” are heterodox teachings: why did these teachings alike originate among Confucians? “Being upright within and square without” is the Confucian Way: why is it said that heterodox teachings attain the one but miss the other? In the reply to the question about guiding qi, what technique is discussed? In the reply concerning divine immortals…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之說其指何歸方人所以窮理也何者
德似堯舜何者德似湯武元氣春生秋
殺所擬何人過多過少所論何士度越
諸子道有未盡其事必有可言一隱君
子近世豪傑其實必有可考窻前草不
除食便不美者是果何意一團和氣瞑
目立雪者是果何人此則其關於大體
切於日用之不可不考者諸士子博學
待問有日願悉言之毋隱
===
問文武並用國家久安長治之策也然文
非操觚染翰而已而謀謨足以經邦詞
藻足以華國武非汗馬血戰而已而建
功於創造之時宣力於艱難之際勝國
以前姑置勿論
天啓
皇明我
太祖高皇帝以武功定天下以文德綏太平
列聖相承文恬武熈而文臣武將之中所以掀
punctuated:
之說，其指何歸？方人所以窮理也，何者德似堯舜？何者德似湯武？元氣春生秋殺，所擬何人？過多過少，所論何士？度越諸子，道有未盡，其事必有可言；一隱君子，近世豪傑，其實必有可考。窻前草不除，食便不美者，是果何意？一團和氣，瞑目立雪者，是果何人？此則其關於大體、切於日用之不可不考者。諸士子博學待問有日，願悉言之，毋隱。

問：文武並用，國家久安長治之策也。然文非操觚染翰而已，而謀謨足以經邦，詞藻足以華國；武非汗馬血戰而已，而建功於創造之時，宣力於艱難之際。勝國以前，姑置勿論。天啓皇明，我太祖高皇帝以武功定天下，以文德綏太平。列聖相承，文恬武熈，而文臣武將之中，所以掀
translation_en:
…the doctrine of immortals: toward what does his response ultimately point? Comparing people is a means of fully investigating principle. Whose virtue resembled that of Yao and Shun? Whose virtue resembled that of Tang and Wu? Who was likened to primordial vital energy, bringing forth life in spring and killing in autumn? Which men were being discussed in the remarks about excessive and insufficient faults? Concerning surpassing the various masters and not fully exhausting the Way, there must be something to say about the circumstances. Concerning “a gentleman in retirement” and “a heroic figure of recent times,” there must be facts that can be examined. What was really meant by not removing the grass before the window, and by food then becoming unpalatable? Who, precisely, were those described as “a mass of harmonious vital energy,” as closing their eyes, and as standing in the snow? These are matters bearing upon the essentials and closely relevant to daily practice that must be investigated. You candidates have long pursued broad learning in readiness for questioning. I ask you to explain everything fully, withholding nothing.

Question: Employing civil and military means together is the policy by which a state secures enduring peace and lasting good government. Yet civil accomplishment consists in more than holding writing tablets and dipping brushes in ink: its plans must suffice to order the realm, and its literary brilliance to adorn the state. Military accomplishment likewise consists in more than sweating warhorses and bloody combat: it means establishing achievements at the founding and exerting strength in times of difficulty. Let us set aside, for now, the preceding dynasty and earlier times. Heaven inaugurated our august Ming. Our Emperor Taizu Gao pacified the realm through military achievement and secured peace through civil virtue. Successive sage emperors continued his rule; civil affairs were tranquil and military affairs flourished. Among the civil officials and military commanders, those whose deeds shook …

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
揭天地光昭簡冊者夥矣玆不暇泛論
請舉其尤者與諸士子言之文臣有才
堪王佐炳於幾先而運籌制勝翼
龍以飛者誰歟有學本聖經粹於德容而輔導
青宮文章名世者誰歟有爲中丞而以守法
見稱者有爲司成而以純德是許者又
誰歟其他或秉節堅貞而匡輔
四帝或遇事剛果而擁佑
三朝或養學中秘之久而危言動
===
主者其人可歷陳歟武將有功高一代反狄隂
山而攻城不屠可方宋之曹彬者誰歟
有勇冠三軍席卷強漢而光復中土可
比唐之鄂公者誰歟有
封侯而著平交之績者有
封伯而興漕運之利者又誰歟其他或取方
氏而靖海上之難或縛明昇而收全蜀
之功或貴爲
帝甥而宣威萬里之遠者其人可悉數歟彼若
punctuated:
揭天地、光昭簡冊者夥矣，玆不暇泛論，請舉其尤者與諸士子言之。文臣有才堪王佐，炳於幾先，而運籌制勝，翼龍以飛者，誰歟？有學本聖經，粹於德容，而輔導青宮，文章名世者，誰歟？有爲中丞而以守法見稱者，有爲司成而以純德是許者，又誰歟？其他或秉節堅貞而匡輔四帝，或遇事剛果而擁佑三朝，或養學中秘之久而危言動主者，其人可歷陳歟？

武將有功高一代，反狄隂山，而攻城不屠，可方宋之曹彬者，誰歟？有勇冠三軍，席卷強漢，而光復中土，可比唐之鄂公者，誰歟？有封侯而著平交之績者，有封伯而興漕運之利者，又誰歟？其他或取方氏而靖海上之難，或縛明昇而收全蜀之功，或貴爲帝甥而宣威萬里之遠者，其人可悉數歟？彼若
translation_en:
…those whose deeds shook heaven and earth and shone brightly in the historical records were many indeed. There is no time here for a general discussion; let us select the most outstanding and speak of them with you candidates. Among the civil officials, who possessed talents worthy of assisting a king, discerned events before their first stirrings, devised strategies that secured victory, and gave the dragon wings to fly? Who grounded his learning in the sages’ classics, displayed purity in virtue and bearing, guided the heir apparent, and became renowned for his literary compositions? Who served as Vice Censor-in-Chief and was praised for upholding the law, and who served as Director of Studies and was esteemed for his pure virtue? Among the others, some maintained steadfast integrity and assisted four emperors; some acted with firmness and resolution when affairs arose and supported three reigns; and some cultivated their learning for many years in the palace library and moved their sovereign with forthright words. Can these men be set forth one by one?

Among the military commanders, who achieved merit unsurpassed in his age, drove the northern foes back to Yinshan [?], and captured cities without massacring their inhabitants, so that he could be compared with Cao Bin of the Song? Who surpassed the three armies in valor, swept away the mighty Han regime, and restored the central lands, so that he could be compared with the Duke of E of the Tang? Who was enfeoffed as a marquis and distinguished himself by pacifying Jiao, and who was enfeoffed as an earl and developed the benefits of grain transport? Among the others, some subdued the Fang clan and quelled troubles along the coast; some captured Ming Sheng and achieved the conquest of all Shu; and some, honored as the emperor’s nephew, extended imperial might ten thousand li away. Can all these men be enumerated? Such men…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
人者建立於天造草昧之秋遭逢於重
熈累洽之世或以文德顯或以武功著
皆一世之賢豪而無容議矣然其間亦
有優劣可言歟方今
聖天子在上文治丕顯武備精强凡列名於文
武之班者濟濟然蹌蹌然碩德重望鴻
勳偉烈皆足以媲美前脩而無愧矣然
其間亦有得失可議歟諸士子儲養學
宮寤寐賢豪久矣茲應賓興而來駸駸
嚮用有日文事武備尚以何人爲法歟
請陳爾志用愜予懷不然則裹棗而問
捫燭而對發策之意荒矣
問方今天下之急務多矣姑舉湖藩之急
者與諸士子言之
朝廷大封宗藩本以親親亦以固邦本誠所
當厚也今
宗支日漸繁衍府第之工役累歲無間莊田
之
punctuated:
人者，建立於天造草昧之秋，遭逢於重熈累洽之世，或以文德顯，或以武功著，皆一世之賢豪而無容議矣。然其間亦有優劣可言歟？方今聖天子在上，文治丕顯，武備精强，凡列名於文武之班者，濟濟然，蹌蹌然，碩德重望，鴻勳偉烈，皆足以媲美前脩而無愧矣。然其間亦有得失可議歟？諸士子儲養學宮，寤寐賢豪久矣。茲應賓興而來，駸駸嚮用有日，文事武備尚以何人爲法歟？請陳爾志，用愜予懷。不然，則裹棗而問，捫燭而對，發策之意荒矣。
問：方今天下之急務多矣，姑舉湖藩之急者與諸士子言之。朝廷大封宗藩，本以親親，亦以固邦本，誠所當厚也。今宗支日漸繁衍，府第之工役累歲無間，莊田之
translation_en:
…such men established their achievements in the unsettled beginnings of the dynasty or lived in an age of accumulating brilliance and enduring harmony. Some distinguished themselves through civil virtue, others through military accomplishments. All were worthy and heroic men of their age, beyond reproach. Yet might differences in their relative merits still be discussed? Now the sagely Son of Heaven reigns above; civil governance is splendidly manifest, and military preparations are refined and strong. All who rank among the civil and military officials are dignified and stately. Their great virtue, weighty reputations, immense contributions, and magnificent achievements suffice to rival their worthy predecessors without shame. Yet might their successes and failings still be debated? You candidates have long been nurtured in the schools, pondering worthy and heroic men waking and sleeping. Now you have come in response to the call for the selection of worthies, and the day when you will advance into service draws near. Whom will you take as your models in civil affairs and military preparedness? Please set forth your aspirations and satisfy my hopes. Otherwise, questions posed like someone asking about a wrapped jujube, and answers given like someone identifying the sun by feeling a candle, would defeat the purpose of setting this policy question.
Question: There are many urgent matters in the realm today. Let us take those most pressing in Huguang and discuss them with you candidates. In extensively enfeoffing imperial princes, the court intended both to cherish its kin and to secure the foundations of the state. They should indeed receive generous provision. Now the branches of the imperial lineage grow ever more numerous. Labor on their princely residences continues year after year without interruption, while the princely estates’…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
斂乎頻年有加湖湘之民財力亦旣竭矣不知
將來何以待之玆欲財力少節上下相
安如有宋之家法果何者可采而行之
世襲武臣本以報功亦以脩武備誠所
當重也今武臣日習紈綺或累干
憲典而科剋倍常或虚冒軍功而廕襲如故
湖湘之軍尺籍亦旣耗矣不知將來何
以處之玆欲刑賞嚴明軍伍充實如
祖宗之成憲果何者當謹而守之流民嘯聚嘗
===
特命大臣以撫治可無患矣近者鄖襄山谷之
中雜聚萬計識者不能無厝火積薪之
慮遣之不可也留之亦不可也玆欲體
當今立撫治之本意果有要歟苗賊劫殺嘗
特遣大臣以鎮守似無虞矣邇者永郴寶靖之
地劫殺靡常議者不能無履霜堅氷之
戒窮追不可也少縱亦不可也玆欲取
古人備禦之長策果何當歟夫士當先
天下之憂而憂諸士子生長湖藩習聞
punctuated:
斂乎頻年有加，湖湘之民財力亦旣竭矣，不知將來何以待之？玆欲財力少節，上下相安，如有宋之家法，果何者可采而行之？
世襲武臣，本以報功，亦以脩武備，誠所當重也。今武臣日習紈綺，或累干憲典而科剋倍常，或虚冒軍功而廕襲如故。湖湘之軍尺籍亦旣耗矣，不知將來何以處之？玆欲刑賞嚴明，軍伍充實，如祖宗之成憲，果何者當謹而守之？
流民嘯聚，嘗特命大臣以撫治，可無患矣。近者鄖襄山谷之中，雜聚萬計，識者不能無厝火積薪之慮。遣之不可也，留之亦不可也。玆欲體當今立撫治之本意，果有要歟？
苗賊劫殺，嘗特遣大臣以鎮守，似無虞矣。邇者永郴寶靖之地，劫殺靡常，議者不能無履霜堅氷之戒。窮追不可也，少縱亦不可也。玆欲取古人備禦之長策，果何當歟？夫士當先天下之憂而憂，諸士子生長湖藩，習聞
translation_en:
…the levies [?] have increased year after year, and the financial resources and strength of the people of Huxiang are already exhausted. How are these demands to be met in the future? If we now wish to conserve resources and labor somewhat, so that those above and below may live in mutual peace, which of the Song dynasty’s rules for its imperial house could actually be adopted and put into practice?
Hereditary military offices were originally intended both to reward merit and to maintain military preparedness; they certainly deserve serious attention. Yet military officials now grow daily more accustomed to silken luxury. Some repeatedly violate the law while imposing exactions at twice the customary rate; others fraudulently claim military merit, while succession through hereditary privilege continues as before. The troop registers of Huxiang are already depleted. How is this to be dealt with in the future? If we now wish to make punishments and rewards strict and clear, and to fill the ranks, which established regulations of the imperial ancestors should be scrupulously observed?
Displaced people have gathered in unruly bands. A high official was previously specially commissioned to pacify and administer them, so there should have been no cause for concern. Recently, however, people of various origins have congregated by the tens of thousands in the mountain valleys of Yun and Xiang. Those who understand the situation cannot help fearing that this is like placing fire beneath a pile of kindling. Sending them away is impracticable, yet allowing them to remain is also impracticable. If we now wish to give effect to the original intention behind the present establishment of an administration for pacification, is there an essential approach?
Miao bandits have plundered and killed. A high official was previously specially dispatched to take charge of regional defense, so there seemed to be no cause for apprehension. Lately, however, plundering and killing have occurred unpredictably in Yong, Chen, and Baojing. Those discussing the matter cannot ignore the warning that treading on frost foretells solid ice. Pursuing them relentlessly is impracticable, yet giving them even a little latitude is also impracticable. If we now wish to adopt an enduring strategy of defense from the ancients, which would be appropriate? Scholars ought to feel concern before all others under Heaven feel concern. You candidates were born and raised in Huguang and have often heard …

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其事蓋必籌之熟矣請酌古準今詳陳
以觀用世之學
punctuated: 其事，蓋必籌之熟矣。請酌古準今，詳陳，以觀用世之學。
translation_en: …these matters, and surely you have considered them thoroughly. Please weigh precedents from antiquity against present circumstances and set forth your views in detail, so that we may assess your learning for practical service in the world.

text:
第壹塲
四書
周監於二代郁郁乎文哉
張鍾靈
同考試官教諭陳批立意正大措辭詳明讀之宛然
目覩周家制作之盛是宜錄出
同考試官教諭許批周家制作發揮殆盡末提出教
養尤見親切

===
考試官學正楊批周之文盛類能言之求其詳盡
切當者僅見此篇
聖人美時王之制酌諸古而獨盛焉蓋成周之
禮監夏商而斟酌之者也然則其文之盛不亦
宜乎夫子美之如此蓋謂天地定位而禮制已
行聖王繼作而禮制斯備時維有周以文武周
公之元聖接夏商道統之正傳欲夏禮之從歟
夏尚忠不能以皆善也周則視乎夏而損益之
欲商禮之從歟商尚質不能以無弊也周則視
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
「周監於二代，郁郁乎文哉！」
張鍾靈

translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“Zhou took the two preceding dynasties as its models. How splendid was its cultural refinement!”
Zhang Zhongling

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Its conception is upright and elevated, and its wording detailed and clear. Reading it, one seems to see before one’s very eyes the splendor of Zhou’s institutional achievements. It deserves to be selected for inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: It expounds Zhou’s institutional achievements almost exhaustively. Its concluding introduction of education and material nurture is especially pertinent.

Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor: Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: Most can speak of the splendor of Zhou’s cultural refinement; but in seeking an account that is exhaustive, apt, and precise, I have found only this essay.

The Sage praised the institutions of the reigning dynasty: drawing judiciously upon antiquity, they attained unrivaled splendor. For the rites of Zhou at its full flourishing took Xia and Shang as models and weighed their practices judiciously. Was it not fitting, then, that its cultural refinement should be so splendid? In praising it thus, the Master meant that once Heaven and Earth had taken their appointed places, ritual institutions were already in operation; as sage kings arose in succession, these institutions became complete. When the time came for Zhou, the supreme sagacity of Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou carried forward the orthodox transmission of the Way from Xia and Shang. Should it simply follow the rites of Xia? Xia prized wholehearted sincerity, yet its practices could not all be good; Zhou therefore looked to Xia and made subtractions and additions. Should it simply follow the rites of Shang? Shang prized simplicity, yet its practices could not be free of defects; Zhou therefore looked to …

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
乎商而脩飾之若六官若六典凡所以爲家國
天下之綱維者莫不監夏商而爲之潤澤曰禮
儀曰威儀凡所以爲脩齊治平之品式者莫不
監夏商而爲之裁成夫參二代之舊章以立一
代之成法由是忠不徒忠有文以濟其忠質不
徒質有文以飾其質典章文物至明而至備不
啻日月星辰之麗天制度文爲盡善而盡美不
啻江淮河漢之行地語其養民也自都鄙以及
鄉遂九一什一之法合夏商而並行文命四訖
===
果何如其郁郁邪文則至矣盡矣不可以復加
矣語其敎民也自國都以及閭巷大學小學之
制合夏商而兼立文敎誕敷又何如其郁郁邪
文則美矣大矣不可以復尚矣吁酌諸古而成
於今合其二而歸於一此有周之文所以爲盛
而夫子之聖所以從之也歟抑論之先王之制
與氣數相爲始終而前後相爲損益固非一人
一日之所能致也三代之禮至周大備則以氣
數至此而極盛損益至是而大成也夫子美其
punctuated: 乎商而脩飾之。若六官，若六典，凡所以爲家國天下之綱維者，莫不監夏商而爲之潤澤；曰禮儀，曰威儀，凡所以爲脩齊治平之品式者，莫不監夏商而爲之裁成。夫參二代之舊章，以立一代之成法，由是忠不徒忠，有文以濟其忠；質不徒質，有文以飾其質。典章文物至明而至備，不啻日月星辰之麗天；制度文爲盡善而盡美，不啻江淮河漢之行地。語其養民也，自都鄙以及鄉遂，九一什一之法合夏商而並行，文命四訖，果何如其郁郁邪？文則至矣，盡矣，不可以復加矣。語其敎民也，自國都以及閭巷，大學小學之制合夏商而兼立，文敎誕敷，又何如其郁郁邪？文則美矣，大矣，不可以復尚矣。吁！酌諸古而成於今，合其二而歸於一，此有周之文所以爲盛，而夫子之聖所以從之也歟！抑論之，先王之制與氣數相爲始終，而前後相爲損益，固非一人一日之所能致也。三代之禮至周大備，則以氣數至此而極盛，損益至是而大成也。夫子美其
translation_en: …looked to the Shang and refined its institutions. Whether the six ministries or the six codes, all that provided the governing framework for families, states, and the realm was modeled on the Xia and Shang and given further polish. Whether ceremonial observances or dignified deportment, all that provided standards for cultivating oneself, ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the realm was fashioned by drawing upon the Xia and Shang. By consulting the established statutes of those two dynasties to institute settled laws for one dynasty, sincerity ceased to be mere sincerity: cultural refinement complemented it. Simplicity ceased to be mere simplicity: cultural refinement adorned it. Statutes and cultural institutions became supremely clear and complete, like the sun, moon, and stars shining in heaven; institutions and ceremonial practices became consummately good and beautiful, like the Chang Jiang, Huai, Huang He, and Han flowing across the earth. As for sustaining the people, from the capital and its outlying territories to the inner and outer rural districts, the systems of one part in nine and one part in ten combined the practices of Xia and Shang and operated together. Civilizing commands reached the four quarters: how richly flourishing was this refinement! It had reached its utmost extent and fullness; nothing more could be added. As for educating the people, from the capital to the neighborhood lanes, the institutions of higher and elementary learning combined those of Xia and Shang and were established together. Civilizing instruction spread far and wide: how richly flourishing, again, was this refinement! It was beautiful and great; nothing could surpass it. Ah! To weigh the institutions of antiquity and perfect them in the present, to combine the two and bring them into one—was this not why Zhou’s cultural refinement flourished, and why the Master, in his sageliness, followed it? Yet, to consider the matter further, the institutions of the former kings arose and declined with the cycles of cosmic force and underwent successive reductions and additions. Certainly they could not have been brought about by one person in a single day. The rites of the Three Dynasties attained their fullest completeness under Zhou because those cosmic cycles had then reached their greatest flourishing, and successive modifications had culminated in a grand synthesis. The Master praised its…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
文而從之豈苟云乎雖然他日答顏子為邦之
問又有取於四代之禮樂者何邪蓋從周之文
者所以遵一代大成之制取四代之禮樂者所
以立萬世常行之道也此又不可不知
和也者天下之達道也
曾得禄
同考試官教諭蔣批發皆中節斯可言和作者窘於
措辭類分喜怒哀樂為兩股講和且不就人倫上說却與
達道處全不照應殊戾本旨此篇得之允宜錄出
===
同考試官教諭張批理明辭暢可取
考試官教諭俞批此篇說理詳明取置前列孰曰
不宜
考試官學正楊批說出和字與達道字相貫穿明
白可取
論情之皆正乃世之通行蓋和乃情之正而即
率性之道也孰謂情之皆正而非天下古今之
所共由者哉子思子即情之德以明道不可離
之意如此蓋謂道原於性而發於情人莫不有
punctuated:
文而從之，豈苟云乎？雖然，他日答顏子為邦之問，又有取於四代之禮樂者，何邪？蓋從周之文者，所以遵一代大成之制；取四代之禮樂者，所以立萬世常行之道也。此又不可不知。

和也者，天下之達道也。
曾得禄

同考試官教諭蔣批：發皆中節，斯可言和。作者窘於措辭，類分喜怒哀樂為兩股講和，且不就人倫上說，却與達道處全不照應，殊戾本旨。此篇得之，允宜錄出。

同考試官教諭張批：理明辭暢，可取。

考試官教諭俞批：此篇說理詳明，取置前列，孰曰不宜？

考試官學正楊批：說出和字與達道字相貫穿，明白可取。

論情之皆正，乃世之通行。蓋和乃情之正，而即率性之道也。孰謂情之皆正，而非天下古今之所共由者哉？子思子即情之德，以明道不可離之意如此。蓋謂道原於性而發於情，人莫不有
translation_en:
…its cultural forms and followed them: could Confucius have said this lightly? Yet, on another occasion, when answering Master Yan’s question about governing a state, he drew upon the rites and music of four dynasties. Why was this? Following Zhou’s cultural forms meant observing the fully developed institutions of one dynasty; drawing upon the rites and music of four dynasties meant establishing a Way that could be practiced throughout all ages. This, too, must be understood.

“Harmony is the universally followed Way of all under Heaven.”
Zeng Delu

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Only when the emotions, upon being expressed, all attain due measure can one speak of harmony. Writers, constrained in their phrasing, commonly divide joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure into two parallel sections to discuss harmony. Moreover, they fail to explain it in terms of human relationships, leaving their discussion entirely disconnected from the phrase “universally followed Way” and seriously at odds with the original purport. This essay grasps it and certainly deserves to be recorded here.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Clear in reasoning and fluent in expression; worthy of selection.

Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor: This essay explains the principles thoroughly and clearly. Who could say that selecting it and placing it among the foremost would be inappropriate?

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Director: It explains how “harmony” and the “universally followed Way” are interconnected. Clear and worthy of selection.

When the emotions are all correct, this constitutes what is universally practiced in the world. For harmony is the correctness of the emotions, and is precisely the Way of following one’s nature. Who could say that the complete correctness of the emotions is not what all under Heaven, past and present, follow in common? Thus Master Zisi draws upon the virtue of the emotions to elucidate the meaning of the Way’s inseparability from us. His meaning is that the Way originates in human nature and finds expression in the emotions; there is no one who does not possess…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
是性則莫不有是情情之和道之用也何則人
生而靜感物而動使其動有不正則其情有不
和矣乃若君臣父子之相接夫婦昆弟朋友之
相與惟無喜怒也或順其心而喜逆其心而怒
喜怒之形在物而不在己惟無哀樂也或喪所
欲而哀得所欲而樂哀樂之動以天而不以人
隨感而見見皆當理無有於乖違隨觸而發發
皆中節無有於咈戾由乎中而應乎外一出於
自然之情徵於色而發於聲不越乎當然之則
===
情之和也如此若何而爲天下之達道乎誠以
情焉不和未免有我之累情焉旣和實愜人心
之公吾知是和不獨一家行之也推之一國亦
莫不然不徒一國由之也達之天下亦莫不爾
如君臣父子而和焉則爲親義之道合天下之
爲君臣爲父子者所通行矣如夫婦昆弟朋友
而和焉則爲別序信之道合天下之爲夫婦爲
昆弟爲朋友者所共由矣驗之古而古無間於
今有若大路然人莫不由之以出入也驗之今
punctuated: 是性，則莫不有是情。情之和，道之用也。何則？人生而靜，感物而動，使其動有不正，則其情有不和矣。乃若君臣父子之相接，夫婦昆弟朋友之相與，惟無喜怒也，或順其心而喜，逆其心而怒，喜怒之形在物而不在己；惟無哀樂也，或喪所欲而哀，得所欲而樂，哀樂之動以天而不以人。隨感而見，見皆當理，無有於乖違；隨觸而發，發皆中節，無有於咈戾。由乎中而應乎外，一出於自然之情；徵於色而發於聲，不越乎當然之則。情之和也如此，若何而爲天下之達道乎？誠以情焉不和，未免有我之累；情焉旣和，實愜人心之公。吾知是和，不獨一家行之也，推之一國亦莫不然；不徒一國由之也，達之天下亦莫不爾。如君臣父子而和焉，則爲親義之道，合天下之爲君臣、爲父子者所通行矣；如夫婦昆弟朋友而和焉，則爲別序信之道，合天下之爲夫婦、爲昆弟、爲朋友者所共由矣。驗之古，而古無間於今，有若大路然，人莫不由之以出入也。驗之今，
translation_en:
…this nature, then none is without these feelings. Harmony in the feelings is the functioning of the Way. Why is this so? Human beings are still at birth and become active when affected by things. If their activity is not correct, their feelings will lack harmony. Consider the dealings between ruler and minister or father and son, and the relations between husband and wife, elder and younger brothers, or friends. Unless joy and anger do not arise at all, one rejoices when things accord with one’s heart and becomes angry when they oppose it: the manifestation of joy and anger depends on things, rather than on oneself. Unless sorrow and delight do not arise at all, one grieves at losing what one desires and delights in obtaining it: the stirring of sorrow and delight follows Heaven rather than human contrivance. Feelings appear in response to each stimulus, and every appearance accords with principle, without deviation. They issue forth at each encounter, and every expression attains its proper measure, without discord. Proceeding from within and responding to what is outside, they arise entirely from spontaneous feeling. Manifested in the countenance and expressed in the voice, they do not exceed the standards of what ought to be.

Such is harmony in the feelings. How, then, does it constitute the universally followed Way of all under Heaven? Truly, when feelings lack harmony, they inevitably bear the burden of self-centeredness; once feelings are harmonious, they fully accord with the impartiality of the human heart. I know that this harmony is not practiced in just one household: extend it to a whole state, and it holds true everywhere. Nor is it followed in just one state: extend it throughout all under Heaven, and it holds true everywhere there as well. When harmony obtains between ruler and minister or father and son, it constitutes the Way of affection and righteousness, universally practiced by all rulers and ministers, fathers and sons, throughout the world. When harmony obtains between husband and wife, elder and younger brothers, or friends, it constitutes the Way of distinction, precedence, and trustworthiness, jointly followed by all husbands and wives, elder and younger brothers, and friends throughout the world. Test it against antiquity, and antiquity shows no divergence from the present. It is like a great road, which everyone follows in going out and coming in. Test it against the present…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
而今不殊於古有若康莊焉人莫不由之以往
來也吁和雖出於一人之情道實通乎天下之
大則道之不離於人可見矣君子烏可須臾離
也哉抑論之道原於天而賦於人命之則謂之
性率之則謂之道脩之則謂之教推而極之位
天地育萬物則謂之業然皆不外乎吾之一心
故曰放之則彌六合卷之則退藏於密學者欲
求至於是豈他求哉亦曰反求諸身而自得之
以去其外誘之私充其本然之善而已
===
仁者無不愛也急親賢之為務
朱衮
同考試官學正蔡批作者類講仁民愛物為無不愛
竟不體下文不徧愛人之意且不知親賢為務則自無不
愛也此作深得本旨是宜錄出
考試官教諭俞批仁者急於親賢正欲廣吾之愛
也此作得之
考試官學正楊批辭贍理明說出仁者之知務殆
無餘蘊
punctuated:
而今不殊於古，有若康莊焉，人莫不由之以往來也。吁！和雖出於一人之情，道實通乎天下之大，則道之不離於人可見矣。君子烏可須臾離也哉？抑論之，道原於天而賦於人，命之則謂之性，率之則謂之道，脩之則謂之教，推而極之，位天地，育萬物，則謂之業。然皆不外乎吾之一心，故曰：「放之則彌六合，卷之則退藏於密。」學者欲求至於是，豈他求哉？亦曰反求諸身而自得之，以去其外誘之私，充其本然之善而已。

仁者無不愛也，急親賢之為務。
朱衮

同考試官學正蔡批：作者類講仁民愛物為無不愛，竟不體下文不徧愛人之意，且不知親賢為務則自無不愛也。此作深得本旨，是宜錄出。

考試官教諭俞批：仁者急於親賢，正欲廣吾之愛也。此作得之。

考試官學正楊批：辭贍理明，說出仁者之知務，殆無餘蘊。
translation_en:
…and the present does not differ from antiquity: it is like a broad highway along which everyone travels to and fro. Ah! Although harmony arises from the feelings of a single person, the Way extends throughout the vastness of all under Heaven. We can thus see that the Way is inseparable from human beings. How could the gentleman depart from it even for a moment? To consider this further: the Way originates in Heaven and is endowed in human beings. As bestowed, it is called human nature; following it is called the Way; cultivating it is called instruction. Extending it to its utmost, establishing Heaven and Earth in their proper places and nurturing the myriad things, is called achievement. Yet none of this lies outside our own single mind. Thus it is said: “Unfurled, it fills the six directions; rolled up, it withdraws into concealment.” If learners wish to attain this, need they seek elsewhere? They need only turn back and seek it within themselves, attaining it for themselves, thereby removing the selfishness induced by external enticements and bringing their inherent goodness to fullness.

“The benevolent person loves all, but makes associating closely with the worthy his most urgent task.”
Zhu Gun 朱衮

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai 蔡, School Director: Writers generally explain “loves all” as being benevolent toward the people and loving all things. They entirely fail to grasp the meaning of the ensuing passage—that one does not love all people indiscriminately. Nor do they understand that, by making close association with the worthy their task, they will naturally extend their love to all. This composition profoundly grasps the original purport and deserves to be included in the record.

Comment by Examiner Yu 俞, Instructor: The benevolent person gives urgency to close association with the worthy precisely because he wishes to extend his love more widely. This composition grasps that point.

Comment by Examiner Yang 楊, School Director: Rich in expression and clear in principle, this composition explains how the benevolent person understands his priorities, leaving scarcely any underlying meaning unexpressed.

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
論仁人之恩固博於所施恒先於所重蓋君子
固無所不愛也使不急於親賢則無以廣吾愛
矣仁者固如此哉昔孟子之意蓋謂仁之爲用
固欲其博而用之所施貴得其要維彼仁者體
乾父坤母之心合天覆地載之德意以一民不
安伊誰之責一夫不獲時予之辜存心於天下
加志於窮民饑者思與之食寒者思與之衣固
無一不在所愛之中愚者欲使之明柔者欲使
之強亦無一不在所愛之內視天下猶一家惟
===
恐其施之不博視中國猶一人每患其濟之不
眾仁者之無不愛如此果將家賜而人益之歟
抑將家至而日見之歟亦曰急親賢之爲務耳
何則一己之恩有限天下之眾無窮使自我愛
之又自我而徧焉將自我行之亦自我而止矣
何以徧天下哉以故養民非所急也宵旰孳孳
常以親賢爲之急教民非所先也夙夜遑遑恒
以親賢爲之先如尊德樂義足以匡吾之不逮
此賢者也吾則翕受敷施與之共天位也與之
punctuated: 論：仁人之恩，固博於所施，恒先於所重。蓋君子固無所不愛也，使不急於親賢，則無以廣吾愛矣。仁者固如此哉！昔孟子之意，蓋謂仁之爲用，固欲其博，而用之所施，貴得其要。維彼仁者，體乾父坤母之心，合天覆地載之德，意以一民不安，伊誰之責？一夫不獲，時予之辜。存心於天下，加志於窮民。饑者思與之食，寒者思與之衣，固無一不在所愛之中；愚者欲使之明，柔者欲使之強，亦無一不在所愛之內。視天下猶一家，惟恐其施之不博；視中國猶一人，每患其濟之不眾。仁者之無不愛如此，果將家賜而人益之歟？抑將家至而日見之歟？亦曰急親賢之爲務耳。何則？一己之恩有限，天下之眾無窮。使自我愛之，又自我而徧焉，將自我行之，亦自我而止矣，何以徧天下哉？以故養民非所急也，宵旰孳孳，常以親賢爲之急；教民非所先也，夙夜遑遑，恒以親賢爲之先。如尊德樂義，足以匡吾之不逮，此賢者也，吾則翕受敷施，與之共天位也，與之
translation_en:
Discourse: The benevolence of a humane person is indeed broad in its application, yet always gives precedence to what matters most. The gentleman certainly loves all; but unless he makes drawing close to the worthy his urgent concern, he has no means of extending his love. Such indeed is the humane person! The intent of Mengzi’s words of old was surely that, although humanity should operate broadly, the essential thing in putting it into practice is to grasp what is crucial.

The humane person embodies the heart that regards Heaven as father and Earth as mother, and accords with the virtue by which Heaven shelters and Earth sustains all things. He thinks: “If a single person is ill at ease, whose responsibility is it? If a single man fails to find his proper place, this is my fault.” He sets his heart upon all under Heaven and directs his concern toward the impoverished. For the hungry he thinks of providing food; for the cold he thinks of providing clothing. Certainly none falls outside his love. He wishes to enlighten the ignorant and strengthen the weak; these too are all included within his love. He regards all under Heaven as one family, fearing only that his beneficence may not extend widely enough; he regards the central realm as one person, constantly worrying that those he aids may not be numerous enough.

Such is the humane person’s love for all. But is he really to bestow gifts upon every household and benefit each person individually? Or is he to visit every household and see its members daily? It is simply a matter of making closeness to the worthy his urgent concern. Why is this? One individual’s beneficence is limited, whereas the multitude under Heaven is inexhaustible. If I myself must love them and personally extend that love to everyone, then its practice will begin with me and also end with me. How could it reach all under Heaven?

For this reason, nourishing the people is not his most urgent task: laboring diligently from before dawn until late in the day, he always makes closeness to the worthy his urgent concern. Teaching the people is not his first priority: exerting himself anxiously morning and night, he always gives precedence to drawing close to the worthy. Those who honor virtue and delight in righteousness, and can remedy my shortcomings, are worthy men. I therefore receive their counsel fully and put it broadly into effect, sharing with them the positions conferred by Heaven, and with them …

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
治天職也雖一沐而三握髮不暇計焉如樂道
忘勢足以輔吾之不及亦賢者也吾則旁求博
訪與之食天禄也與之治天民也雖一飯而三
吐哺不遑恤焉夫急親賢之爲務如此則君子
在朝賢者在位將廣吾力之所能而恩惠極於
廣大繼吾身之所存而教化推於無窮愛自無
所不及矣仁人之恩一何博哉我思古人克當
此者其惟堯舜乎堯仁如天舜德好生非不愛
人而亦曷嘗徧愛人哉第以不得舜禹皐陶爲
===
己憂耳所以然者正惟以己愛人則所及有限
以人愛人則所及無窮此博施濟衆所以爲聖
人之猶病而爲天下得人所以爲聖人之仁也
歟
易
繼之者善也成之者性也
蘇純
同考試官教諭易批繼善成性之說觀朱子註通書
數語最爲明白此作獨能參考宜取以冠本房
punctuated:
治天職也。雖一沐而三握髮，不暇計焉。如樂道忘勢，足以輔吾之不及，亦賢者也。吾則旁求博訪，與之食天禄也，與之治天民也。雖一飯而三吐哺，不遑恤焉。夫急親賢之爲務如此，則君子在朝，賢者在位，將廣吾力之所能，而恩惠極於廣大；繼吾身之所存，而教化推於無窮，愛自無所不及矣。仁人之恩，一何博哉！我思古人，克當此者，其惟堯舜乎！堯仁如天，舜德好生，非不愛人，而亦曷嘗徧愛人哉？第以不得舜、禹、皐陶爲己憂耳。所以然者，正惟以己愛人，則所及有限；以人愛人，則所及無窮。此博施濟衆所以爲聖人之猶病，而爲天下得人所以爲聖人之仁也歟！
易
繼之者善也，成之者性也。
蘇純
同考試官教諭易批：「繼善成性之說，觀朱子註《通書》數語，最爲明白。此作獨能參考，宜取以冠本房。」
translation_en:
…and share with them the discharge of Heaven’s offices. Even if I must interrupt a single washing of my hair three times, clutching my wet hair to receive them, I have no leisure to count the inconvenience. Those who delight in the Way and disregard power, and who can make up for my shortcomings, are likewise worthy men. I therefore seek them far and wide, sharing with them Heaven’s emoluments and the governance of Heaven’s people. Even if I must spit out my food three times during a single meal to receive them, I have no time to fret over it. If I thus make drawing close to worthy men my urgent task, gentlemen will serve at court and worthy men will hold office. They will extend what my strength can accomplish, spreading beneficence far and wide; they will carry on beyond my own lifetime, extending moral transformation without end. My love will naturally reach everywhere. How vast is the benevolence of the humane man!
When I consider the ancients, surely only Yao and Shun fully answered to this description! Yao’s humanity was like Heaven; Shun’s virtue cherished life. It was not that they did not love others, but when did they ever personally extend love to everyone? They merely took as their own concern the failure to obtain men such as Shun, Yu, and Gao Yao. The reason is precisely this: when one loves others through one’s own efforts, one’s reach is limited; when one loves others through the agency of others, one’s reach is inexhaustible. Is this not why even the sages found it difficult to bestow benefits widely and bring relief to the multitude, while securing able men for All under Heaven constituted the sages’ humanity?
Book of Changes
“What continues it is goodness; what brings it to completion is nature.”
Su Chun
Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor, comments: “The doctrine of continuing in goodness and completing nature is most clearly explained in a few statements in Master Zhu’s commentary on the Comprehensive Treatise (Tongshu). This composition alone has drawn upon them; it should be selected to head this examining section.”

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正潘批理氣分明一洗塵陋
考試官教諭俞批得旨
考試官學正楊批說得理氣明白且通篇無陳語
相雜作易義正是如此
大傳之論道也行而爲大化之渾然具而爲萬
化之本然夫盈天地間皆道也然所以具於陰
而行乎陽者何莫而非是道哉昔大傳論道之
體用不外乎陰陽至此若曰一陰一陽之所以
迭運固謂之道矣然道无終窮也自其流行而
===
觀之歸藏之後繼之以發舒闔翕之終繼之以
流動鼓元氣於冲漠无朕之中絪縕而交密嘘
太和於於穆不已之際融液而薰蒸斯時也氣
之方出理斯行焉未賦於人而太極之本體渾
淪自如未著於物而无妄之本貞純粹不雜此
蓋化育之功善之謂也善之所在道之所在也
曰繼善非道之行於陽者乎自其賦予而言之
流動之極妙合而成形發舒之餘凝聚而成質
大以成大具元氣於軀殻之中小以成小涵太
punctuated:
同考試官學正潘批：理氣分明，一洗塵陋。
考試官教諭俞批：得旨。
考試官學正楊批：說得理氣明白，且通篇無陳語相雜。作易義，正是如此。
大傳之論道也，行而爲大化之渾然，具而爲萬化之本然。夫盈天地間皆道也，然所以具於陰而行乎陽者，何莫而非是道哉？昔大傳論道之體用，不外乎陰陽。至此若曰：一陰一陽之所以迭運，固謂之道矣。然道无終窮也，自其流行而觀之，歸藏之後繼之以發舒，闔翕之終繼之以流動。鼓元氣於冲漠无朕之中，絪縕而交密；嘘太和於於穆不已之際，融液而薰蒸。斯時也，氣之方出，理斯行焉。未賦於人，而太極之本體渾淪自如；未著於物，而无妄之本貞純粹不雜。此蓋化育之功，善之謂也。善之所在，道之所在也。曰繼善，非道之行於陽者乎？自其賦予而言之，流動之極，妙合而成形；發舒之餘，凝聚而成質。大以成大，具元氣於軀殻之中；小以成小，涵太
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Pan, School Instructor, comments: “Principle and material force are clearly distinguished, sweeping away all stale and vulgar notions.”
Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: “He grasps the essential meaning.”
Examiner Yang, School Instructor, comments: “He explains principle and material force clearly, and no hackneyed expressions intrude anywhere in the essay. This is precisely how an exposition of the Changes should be written.”
In its discussion of the Way, the Great Commentary presents its operation as the undivided entirety of the great transformation, and its inherent presence as the original ground of the myriad transformations. All that fills heaven and earth is the Way. What, then, of that which is inherent in yin and operates through yang is not this same Way? When the Great Commentary discussed the substance and function of the Way, it did not go beyond yin and yang. At this point it seems to say: that by which yin and yang operate in alternation is indeed called the Way. Yet the Way has neither end nor limit. Viewed in its flowing operation, return and concealment are followed by unfolding and expansion; closing and gathering are followed by flowing movement. It stirs the primordial material force within empty stillness, where no trace is yet apparent, interweaving it in intimate conjunction. It breathes forth supreme harmony amid profound and unceasing activity, blending and suffusing all. At this moment, as material force first issues forth, principle operates within it. Before being endowed upon human beings, the original substance of the Supreme Ultimate remains whole and undivided in itself; before becoming manifest in things, the original rectitude of freedom from falsity remains pure and unmixed. This is the work of transformation and nurture, and is what is meant by goodness. Where goodness is, there the Way is also. When we speak of goodness in its continuation, is this not the Way operating through yang?
Speaking of its bestowal, at the culmination of flowing movement, wondrous union produces form; following unfolding and expansion, condensation and gathering produce substance. The great thereby becomes great, containing primordial material force within its bodily frame; the small thereby becomes small, enfolding the Great…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
和於郛郭之內斯時也氣以成形理亦賦焉□
而爲人莫不各全夫本然之善而不相假借蠢
而爲物莫不各得其有生之理而不相凌奪此
蓋天命之正性之謂也性之所存道之所存也
曰成性非道之具於陰者乎是則繼之者屬乎
陽陽一道也成之者屬乎陰陰一道也道之體
用不外乎陰陽而其所以然者又何嘗倚於陰
陽也哉嗟夫天地之間陰陽兩端而已陰不一
於陰而陽繼之陽不一於陽而陰繼之莫非道
===
之全體也而世之偏見者或以爲仁或以爲智
而氣禀每下者則又昧而不知皆非也殊不知
陰陽一氣也形而下者也道則理也形而上者
也故曰動靜无端陰陽无始非知道者孰能識
之
利用安身以崇德也
戴惢
同考試官教諭易批題本明白作者多欠體認此篇
獨得其旨是宜錄出
punctuated:
和於郛郭之內。斯時也，氣以成形，理亦賦焉。□而爲人，莫不各全夫本然之善，而不相假借；蠢而爲物，莫不各得其有生之理，而不相凌奪。此蓋天命之正，性之謂也。性之所存，道之所存也。曰成性，非道之具於陰者乎？是則繼之者屬乎陽，陽一道也；成之者屬乎陰，陰一道也。道之體用不外乎陰陽，而其所以然者，又何嘗倚於陰陽也哉！嗟夫！天地之間，陰陽兩端而已。陰不一於陰，而陽繼之；陽不一於陽，而陰繼之，莫非道之全體也。而世之偏見者，或以爲仁，或以爲智；而氣禀每下者，則又昧而不知，皆非也。殊不知陰陽一氣也，形而下者也；道則理也，形而上者也。故曰：「動靜无端，陰陽无始。」非知道者，孰能識之？

利用安身以崇德也。
戴惢

同考試官教諭易批：題本明白，作者多欠體認。此篇獨得其旨，是宜錄出。
translation_en:
…harmony within its enclosing walls. At this moment, as material force gives things form, principle is also imparted to them. Those who become human beings through [?] each possess the full goodness of their original condition, without borrowing it from one another; the creatures that stir into life each obtain the principle of their existence, without encroaching upon or taking it from one another. This is the correctness of Heaven’s mandate: it is what is called nature. Where nature resides, the Way resides. When we speak of completing nature, is this not the Way embodied in yin? Thus, what carries it forward belongs to yang, and yang is the one Way; what brings it to completion belongs to yin, and yin is the one Way. The substance and functioning of the Way do not lie outside yin and yang, yet when has the principle that makes them so ever depended upon yin and yang? Ah! Between Heaven and Earth there are only the two poles of yin and yang. Yin does not remain exclusively yin: yang succeeds it. Yang does not remain exclusively yang: yin succeeds it. All of this is the Way in its entirety. Yet those in the world whose views are partial take it to be benevolence or take it to be wisdom; those whose endowment of material force is inferior remain benighted and unaware of it. All are mistaken. They fail to understand that yin and yang are a single material force, belonging to what is below form; the Way is principle, belonging to what is above form. Thus it is said: “Movement and stillness have no endpoint; yin and yang have no beginning.” Who but one who knows the Way could understand this?

“To make one’s actions beneficial and bring ease to one’s person is how one exalts virtue.”
Dai Suo 戴惢

Comment by Associate Examiner Yi, an Instructor: The topic itself is clear, but most writers lack a thorough grasp of it. This essay alone captures its purport and therefore merits inclusion.

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正潘批題本下學交養之事而作者疎
泛乏不切明白可觀者無踰此篇
考試官教諭俞批辭順理明
考試官學正楊批崇德處發揮明白
裕所行於外充所得於中下學屈信之機也蓋
為學之機内外交相養而互相發也然則所行
旣裕於外則行而有得於己者豈不日積而益
高乎大傳釋咸九四爻義至此蓋謂屈信往來
豈特造化物理為然哉觀之下學亦可見矣是
===
故内外有交養之理屈信有相感之機下學君
子夫旣精義入神以為致用之本矣由是日用
常行之間事至物來之際雖曰有常有變應之
皆將觸機而中无有於固滯身亦隨之而无適
不安何危殆邪雖曰有經有權御之皆將迎刄
而解无有於括礙身亦因之而无往不得何阸
脆邪如遇父子而親遇君臣而敬動罔不宜吾
身為之怡然其順適如遇賓主而恭遇賢否而
哲行无不得吾身為之泰然其安舒夫利用安
punctuated:
同考試官學正潘批：題本下學交養之事，而作者疎泛乏不切，明白可觀者無踰此篇。
考試官教諭俞批：辭順理明。
考試官學正楊批：崇德處發揮明白。
裕所行於外，充所得於中，下學屈信之機也。蓋為學之機，内外交相養而互相發也。然則所行旣裕於外，則行而有得於己者，豈不日積而益高乎？大傳釋咸九四爻義至此，蓋謂屈信往來，豈特造化物理為然哉？觀之下學，亦可見矣。是故内外有交養之理，屈信有相感之機。下學君子，夫旣精義入神，以為致用之本矣。由是日用常行之間，事至物來之際，雖曰有常有變，應之皆將觸機而中，无有於固滯，身亦隨之而无適不安，何危殆邪？雖曰有經有權，御之皆將迎刄而解，无有於括礙，身亦因之而无往不得，何阸脆邪？如遇父子而親，遇君臣而敬，動罔不宜，吾身為之怡然其順適；如遇賓主而恭，遇賢否而哲，行无不得，吾身為之泰然其安舒。夫利用安
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Pan, an Instructor, comments: “The topic concerns learning through everyday affairs and the mutual cultivation of the inner and outer aspects. Yet writers are vague, diffuse, and inadequate, failing to address it closely [?]. For clarity and merit, no essay surpasses this one.”
Examiner Yu, an Instructor, comments: “The language flows smoothly, and the reasoning is clear.”
Examiner Yang, an Instructor, comments: “The discussion of exalting virtue is clearly developed.”
To give ample scope to what one practices outwardly and bring to fullness what one has attained inwardly: this is the dynamic of contraction and extension in learning through everyday affairs. For the dynamic of learning lies in the inner and outer aspects nourishing and bringing forth one another. Thus, once one’s outward practice has become ample, will not what one personally gains through practice accumulate daily and rise ever higher? At this point in its explanation of the fourth line, a yang line, of the hexagram Xian (Influence), the Great Commentary means that contraction and extension, departure and arrival, are surely not confined to the workings of creation and the patterns of things. They can also be seen in learning through everyday affairs.
Thus, the inner and outer aspects have a principle of mutual nourishment, and contraction and extension have a dynamic of mutual response. The gentleman who learns through everyday affairs has already refined his understanding of rightness to the point of penetrating the numinous, thereby establishing the foundation for practical application. Consequently, amid daily activities and ordinary conduct, whenever affairs arise and things present themselves, whether circumstances are constant or changing, his response will strike the mark as soon as the occasion arises, without rigidity or stagnation. Accordingly, he himself will be at ease wherever he goes. What peril could there be? Whether a situation calls for abiding principles or discretionary judgment, everything he handles will come apart as readily as something meeting a blade, without obstruction or impediment. Accordingly, wherever he goes, he will find things fitting. What distress or frailty could there be [?]?
For example, in the relationship between father and son he is affectionate, and in that between ruler and minister he is reverent. None of his actions is inappropriate, and he himself feels content in their smooth and fitting course. In the relationship between guest and host he is respectful, and in dealing with the worthy and the unworthy he is discerning. None of his conduct fails to attain what is fitting, and he himself feels composed, peaceful, and at ease. Now, making practical application beneficial and bringing peace …

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
身如此若无與於內也殊不知躬行益熟則涵
養益深踐履愈純則操存愈固行旣有以裕於
外矣德豈不有以充於中邪將見理之得於己
者日進而益盛道之得於心者日積而益高如
德不外乎仁義也今父子君臣之道旣行之而
无不裕則仁義之德將由美而大由大而化日
造乎高明矣土自一簣而成九仞之山曷足以
喻之乎德不外乎禮智也今賓主賢否之道旣
行之而无不得則禮智之德將由知而好由好
===
而樂日詣乎高遠矣木自拱把而聳千尋之榦
何足以方之乎是則裕乎外者信也充乎內者
屈也屈信相感莫非自然咸之九四何以憧憧
爲哉大抵天下之理有感必有應有屈必有信
造化且然而況於物類乎況於下學乎世之人
智不出此往往溺於私感而自役於憧憧亦獨
何哉此傳易聖人所以有感於世而極言之也
然則君子當何如亦曰以虛受人則无私感矣
書
punctuated:
身如此，若无與於內也。殊不知躬行益熟，則涵養益深；踐履愈純，則操存愈固。行旣有以裕於外矣，德豈不有以充於中邪？將見理之得於己者日進而益盛，道之得於心者日積而益高。如德不外乎仁義也，今父子君臣之道旣行之而无不裕，則仁義之德將由美而大，由大而化，日造乎高明矣。土自一簣而成九仞之山，曷足以喻之乎？德不外乎禮智也，今賓主賢否之道旣行之而无不得，則禮智之德將由知而好，由好而樂，日詣乎高遠矣。木自拱把而聳千尋之榦，何足以方之乎？是則裕乎外者信也，充乎內者屈也。屈信相感，莫非自然。《咸》之九四，何以憧憧爲哉？大抵天下之理，有感必有應，有屈必有信。造化且然，而況於物類乎？況於下學乎？世之人智不出此，往往溺於私感而自役於憧憧，亦獨何哉？此傳《易》聖人所以有感於世而極言之也。然則君子當何如？亦曰以虛受人，則无私感矣。

書
translation_en:
…bringing ease to oneself in this way might seem to have nothing to do with the inner life. Yet one fails to realize that the more practiced one's personal conduct becomes, the deeper one's inner cultivation grows; the purer one's practice becomes, the firmer one's preservation of the moral mind. Once conduct has brought abundance to one's outward activity, how could virtue fail to bring fullness within? One will see the principles apprehended in oneself advance daily and flourish ever more, and the Way apprehended in one's heart accumulate daily and rise ever higher. For example, virtue does not extend beyond benevolence and righteousness. Now, once the Way governing fathers and sons, rulers and ministers has been practiced with complete adequacy, the virtues of benevolence and righteousness will advance from beauty to greatness, and from greatness to transformative perfection, attaining loftiness and clarity day by day. How could earth accumulating from a single basketful into a mountain nine ren high suffice as an analogy?

Virtue likewise does not extend beyond ritual propriety and wisdom. Now, once the Way of dealing with hosts and guests and with the worthy and unworthy has been practiced with complete appropriateness, the virtues of ritual propriety and wisdom will advance from knowing to loving, and from loving to delighting, reaching ever greater heights day by day. How could a tree growing from a trunk one can encircle with one's hands into a towering stem a thousand xun high suffice as a comparison? Thus, outward abundance is extension, while inward fullness is contraction. Contraction and extension move one another in response, and all of this is spontaneous. What need, then, is there for the restless preoccupation mentioned in the fourth, yang line of the hexagram Influence (Xian)?

In general, according to the principles of all under Heaven, wherever there is a stimulus there must be a response, and wherever there is contraction there must be extension. If even the processes of creation and transformation are like this, how much more so are the various kinds of things? How much more so is learning that begins with ordinary affairs? The understanding of people in this world does not go beyond this, yet they often become immersed in self-interested impulses and enslave themselves to restless preoccupation. Why is this? This is why the sage who composed the commentary on the Changes, moved by the condition of the world, expounded the matter so fully. How, then, should the gentleman act? Simply put: receive others with an empty, receptive mind, and there will be no self-interested impulses.
