title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
克勤于邦克儉于家
曾得祿
同考試官教諭蔣批作者率以克勤作治水之功得
其旨者僅見此篇
同考試官教諭張批辭贍理明優於衆作本房之冠
舍子其誰
考試官教諭俞批勤儉二字發揮殆盡塲中如此
作者絕少是宜錄之
考試官學正楊批通暢可取
===
不怠於公事不侈於私養惟大臣能然也夫勤
儉美德也今大臣處家國而能之其賢於人也
何如哉昔帝舜命禹居攝而因其辭故叙其功
德之盛及此蓋謂水滔天而卒致平成厥功偉
矣常人處此將恃功而怠烏能勤邪汝則不然
蓋嘗觀之在邦百揆是宅何官弗總宜可責仼
而自逸矣汝則祗承于帝而思日孳孳猶昔過
門不入之心克艱厥臣而終日乾乾猶昔娶妻
弗顧之念汝翼汝爲命汝多矣曷嘗以賢勞而
punctuated:
克勤于邦，克儉于家。
曾得祿
同考試官教諭蔣批：作者率以克勤作治水之功，得其旨者僅見此篇。
同考試官教諭張批：辭贍理明，優於衆作，本房之冠，舍子其誰？
考試官教諭俞批：勤儉二字，發揮殆盡。塲中如此作者絕少，是宜錄之。
考試官學正楊批：通暢可取。
不怠於公事，不侈於私養，惟大臣能然也。夫勤儉，美德也。今大臣處家國而能之，其賢於人也何如哉！昔帝舜命禹居攝，而因其辭，故叙其功德之盛及此。蓋謂水滔天而卒致平成，厥功偉矣。常人處此，將恃功而怠，烏能勤邪？汝則不然。蓋嘗觀之在邦，百揆是宅，何官弗總？宜可責仼而自逸矣。汝則祗承于帝，而思日孳孳，猶昔過門不入之心；克艱厥臣，而終日乾乾，猶昔娶妻弗顧之念。汝翼汝爲，命汝多矣，曷嘗以賢勞而
translation_en:
“Diligent in affairs of state, frugal in the household.”
By Zeng Delu.
Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “Writers generally interpret ‘diligent’ as referring to the achievement of controlling the floods. This is the only essay I have seen that grasps the passage’s purport.”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Rich in expression and clear in reasoning, this surpasses the other essays and ranks first in this examining section. Who but you could hold that place?”
Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: “The two terms ‘diligence’ and ‘frugality’ are expounded almost exhaustively. Writers like this are exceedingly rare in the examination hall. This essay certainly deserves inclusion in the record.”
Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “Lucid and fluent; worthy of selection.”
To be untiring in public business and free from extravagance in one’s personal maintenance: only a great minister can achieve this. Diligence and frugality are fine virtues. If a great minister can practice them in managing both household and state, how greatly he surpasses others in worth!
Long ago, Emperor Shun commanded Yu to act as regent. When Yu declined, Shun recounted the greatness of his achievements and virtues, reaching this point in his praise. His meaning was this: “The waters rose to heaven, yet you ultimately brought the land and waters into order. Your achievement was magnificent. An ordinary person in such a position would rely upon his achievements and grow idle. How could he remain diligent? But you are different.
“I have observed you in affairs of state. You occupy the office of Director of the Hundred Departments: what office is outside your supervision? You might well have delegated responsibilities and taken your ease. Yet you reverently serve your sovereign, your thoughts intent upon your duties each day, retaining the resolve that once led you to pass your own gate without entering. You recognize the difficulty of being a minister and exert yourself tirelessly all day, retaining the determination that once led you to marry yet give no thought to your wife. You assist me and carry out the work; many are the commands laid upon you. When have you ever, on account of the heavy labors borne by the worthy, …”

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
辭汝明汝聽責汝備矣曷嘗以怠荒而廢凡此
皆汝之克勤于邦而予所親見者也廷臣出汝
右者誰歟民鮮食而卒能乃粒厥功大矣常人
處此將矜功而侈烏能儉邪汝則不然又嘗驗
之在家百祿是遒何求不得宜可從厚以自奉
矣汝則飲食之菲而旨酒是絕殆得大羹不和
之餘風宮室之卑而峻宇是懲殆得茅茨不翦
之遺意色荒禽荒自戒嚴矣而用度曷由以奢
惡衣惡服自奉薄矣而經費何由以侈凡此皆
===
汝之克儉于家而予所素知者也廷臣求汝似
者誰歟夫然則勤儉之德備而賢於人也遠矣
天位之攝汝終誰讓也邪故下文又稱其弗矜
弗伐而遂曰天之曆數在爾躬汝終陟元后者
此也雖然竊有惑焉天下大器而謂禹惟勤儉
曆數遂歸者何也蓋天之為民而立君也欲以
一人治天下不以天下奉一人夫以一人而治
天下匪勤則事隳矣以天下奉一人匪儉則民
蠢矣民蠢事隳如天心何此自古得天下者必
punctuated:
辭？汝明汝聽，責汝備矣，曷嘗以怠荒而廢？凡此皆汝之克勤于邦，而予所親見者也。廷臣出汝右者誰歟？民鮮食而卒能乃粒，厥功大矣。常人處此，將矜功而侈，烏能儉邪？汝則不然。又嘗驗之，在家百祿是遒，何求不得？宜可從厚以自奉矣。汝則飲食之菲，而旨酒是絕，殆得大羹不和之餘風；宮室之卑，而峻宇是懲，殆得茅茨不翦之遺意。色荒禽荒，自戒嚴矣，而用度曷由以奢？惡衣惡服，自奉薄矣，而經費何由以侈？凡此皆汝之克儉于家，而予所素知者也。廷臣求汝似者誰歟？夫然則勤儉之德備，而賢於人也遠矣。天位之攝，汝終誰讓也邪？故下文又稱其弗矜弗伐，而遂曰：「天之曆數在爾躬，汝終陟元后。」者此也。

雖然，竊有惑焉。天下大器，而謂禹惟勤儉，曆數遂歸者，何也？蓋天之為民而立君也，欲以一人治天下，不以天下奉一人。夫以一人而治天下，匪勤則事隳矣；以天下奉一人，匪儉則民蠢矣。民蠢事隳，如天心何？此自古得天下者必
translation_en:
…decline? Your discernment and your hearing have been called upon, and the responsibilities placed upon you are comprehensive. Yet when have you ever neglected them through indolence? All these are instances of your diligence in serving the state, which I have witnessed personally. Who among the ministers at court surpasses you? The people lacked food, yet you ultimately enabled them to eat grain: great indeed was your achievement. An ordinary person in this position would grow conceited over his achievements and become extravagant. How could he remain frugal? You, however, were otherwise. I have also observed that, in your household, every blessing accrued to you. What could you seek that you could not obtain? You might reasonably have provided lavishly for yourself. Yet your food and drink were meager, and you renounced fine wine, seemingly preserving the ancient practice of leaving the great sacrificial broth unseasoned. Your dwelling was lowly, and you shunned lofty buildings, seemingly retaining the spirit of leaving the thatch of a roof untrimmed. You strictly guarded against excessive indulgence in women and hunting: how, then, could your expenditure become extravagant? You wore poor clothing and provided sparingly for yourself: how, then, could your household expenses become excessive? All these are instances of your frugality at home, which I have long known. Who among the ministers at court can be found to equal you? Thus, possessing both diligence and frugality in full, you far surpass others in worth. To whom, then, would you ultimately yield the regency of the imperial throne? This is why the text below further praises his freedom from conceit and boasting, and then says: “Heaven’s ordained succession rests in your person; you shall ultimately ascend as sovereign.”

Nevertheless, I venture to express a doubt. All under Heaven is a weighty charge. Why is it said that merely through Yu’s diligence and frugality, Heaven’s ordained succession came to him? Heaven establishes a ruler for the people because it wishes one person to govern all under Heaven, rather than all under Heaven to support one person. If one person is to govern all under Heaven, without diligence affairs will fall into ruin. If all under Heaven supports one person, without frugality the people will be reduced to brutishness. With the people thus degraded and affairs in ruins, how could Heaven’s will be satisfied? Thus, from antiquity, those who gained all under Heaven invariably…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
以勤儉而失之者必以縱逸也是知勤儉也者
天之心民之命而君之德也後之人主可不深
思而加念之哉
聖謨洋洋嘉言孔彰
黃鉞
同考試官教諭蔣批場中作者講洋洋孔彰類欠明
白惟此篇體認真切措辭通暢是宜錄出
同考試官教諭張批聖謨嘉言一本風愆之戒作者
類多分析不明此篇鋪張明白獨異衆作
===
考試官教諭俞批先王儆有位之意伊尹告賢王
之心宛然在目
考試官學正楊批辭暢而矩度不差
先王貽謀為甚大垂訓為甚明夫三風十愆之
戒先王所以厲臣而正君者也其貽謀豈不甚
大而垂訓豈不甚明哉昔太甲嗣位伊尹作書
訓誥而終之以此蓋謂非謀無以制訓非訓無
以達謀使謀出常情則或溺於淺近未可謂之
大也乃若三風十愆之戒在我先王之心熟慮
punctuated:
以勤儉，而失之者必以縱逸也。是知勤儉也者，天之心、民之命，而君之德也。後之人主可不深思而加念之哉？

聖謨洋洋，嘉言孔彰。
黃鉞

同考試官教諭蔣批：場中作者講洋洋、孔彰，類欠明白。惟此篇體認真切，措辭通暢，是宜錄出。
同考試官教諭張批：聖謨、嘉言，一本風愆之戒。作者類多分析不明，此篇鋪張明白，獨異衆作。
考試官教諭俞批：先王儆有位之意、伊尹告賢王之心，宛然在目。
考試官學正楊批：辭暢而矩度不差。

先王貽謀為甚大，垂訓為甚明。夫三風十愆之戒，先王所以厲臣而正君者也。其貽謀豈不甚大，而垂訓豈不甚明哉？昔太甲嗣位，伊尹作書訓誥，而終之以此。蓋謂非謀無以制訓，非訓無以達謀。使謀出常情，則或溺於淺近，未可謂之大也。乃若三風十愆之戒，在我先王之心熟慮
translation_en:
…through diligence and frugality, while those who lose it invariably do so through indulgence and idleness. Thus we know that diligence and frugality embody Heaven’s intent, sustain the people’s lives, and constitute the ruler’s virtue. Can later rulers fail to ponder this deeply and take it to heart?

“The sage counsels are vast; the excellent words are most manifest.”
Huang Yue

Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: Candidates in this examination generally lack clarity in explaining “vast” and “most manifest.” This essay alone shows a true and penetrating understanding, expressed in fluent language. It deserves to be included in the record.

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: The “sage counsels” and “excellent words” alike derive from the admonition against the pernicious customs and faults. Most candidates fail to distinguish and explain these clearly. This essay expounds them lucidly and stands apart from the other compositions.

Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: The former king’s intention to admonish those holding office, and Yi Yin’s concern in instructing a worthy king, appear vividly before our eyes.

Examiner Yang, School Instructor, comments: The language flows smoothly without departing from the prescribed standards.

The plans bequeathed by the former king were exceedingly great; the instructions he handed down were exceedingly clear. The admonition against the three pernicious customs and ten faults was the means by which the former king exhorted ministers and rectified rulers. Were not the plans he bequeathed exceedingly great, and the instructions he handed down exceedingly clear? Formerly, when Tai Jia succeeded to the throne, Yi Yin composed a written admonition to instruct him and concluded it with these words. The meaning is that without plans there can be no formulation of instructions, and without instructions there can be no communication of plans. If plans arise from ordinary thinking, they may become mired in the shallow and immediate, and cannot yet be called great. But as for the admonition against the three pernicious customs and ten faults, our former king deliberated upon it carefully in his heart…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
審處知犯此者必敗必喪事制曲防使縱此者
必墨必刑謨實聖謨而其謀也不惟爲卿士有
家者計而且爲邦君有國者計不惟爲邦君有
國者計而且爲嗣世有天下者計以儆有位憂
之也深以訓童蒙慮之也遠神機默運周流事
物洋洋乎如江淮河海之行地豈不爲甚大乎
訓非至理則或涉於荒唐未可謂之明也乃若
三風十愆之戒出我先王之口綱舉目張事關
乎家國天下詞嚴義正道貫乎脩齊治平訓實
===
嘉言而其訓也曰風曰愆森然酖葛之陳前而
進嘗必死曰刑曰墨凛然斧鉞之在後而退縮
必誅其儆有位言之也切其訓童蒙說之也詳
天語丁寧光昭簡冊粲粲乎如日月星辰之麗
天豈不爲甚明乎夫謀之大而訓之明如此着
之何可忽而不念邪抑太甲異時欲敗度縱敗
禮伊尹先見其微故惓惓及此尹言弗用湯祀
幾覆不得已而爲桐宮之舉弗順之人使之弗
狎蓋刑墨或加焉幸而徂桐之餘克終允德傳
punctuated: 審處，知犯此者必敗必喪，事制曲防，使縱此者必墨必刑。謨實聖謨，而其謀也，不惟爲卿士有家者計，而且爲邦君有國者計；不惟爲邦君有國者計，而且爲嗣世有天下者計。以儆有位，憂之也深；以訓童蒙，慮之也遠。神機默運，周流事物，洋洋乎如江淮河海之行地，豈不爲甚大乎？訓非至理，則或涉於荒唐，未可謂之明也。乃若三風十愆之戒，出我先王之口，綱舉目張，事關乎家國天下，詞嚴義正，道貫乎脩齊治平。訓實嘉言，而其訓也，曰風曰愆，森然酖葛之陳前，而進嘗必死；曰刑曰墨，凛然斧鉞之在後，而退縮必誅。其儆有位，言之也切；其訓童蒙，說之也詳。天語丁寧，光昭簡冊，粲粲乎如日月星辰之麗天，豈不爲甚明乎？夫謀之大而訓之明如此着之，何可忽而不念邪？抑太甲異時欲敗度，縱敗禮，伊尹先見其微，故惓惓及此。尹言弗用，湯祀幾覆，不得已而爲桐宮之舉。弗順之人，使之弗狎，蓋刑墨或加焉。幸而徂桐之餘，克終允德，傳
translation_en: …deliberated carefully and judged thoroughly, knowing that those who violated these admonitions would surely meet ruin and destruction. He established restraints for every affair and safeguards for every contingency, ensuring that those who indulged in these faults would be subjected to tattooing and punishment. His counsels were truly those of a sage. His planning was not merely for high ministers possessing households, but also for rulers possessing states; not merely for rulers possessing states, but also for successors possessing all under Heaven. In admonishing those in office, his concern was profound; in instructing the youthful and inexperienced, his foresight was far-reaching. His wondrous intelligence worked silently, extending throughout affairs and things, vast as the Yangzi, Huai, and Yellow Rivers and the seas spreading over the earth. Was this not exceedingly great? If instruction does not embody the highest principles, it may stray into absurdity and cannot be called clear. But the admonitions concerning the three pernicious tendencies and ten faults issued from the mouth of our former king: their main principles were raised and their particulars unfolded. Their concerns embraced household, state, and all under Heaven; their language was stern and their meaning upright. Their Way ran through cultivating oneself, regulating the household, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven. His instructions were truly excellent words. In naming these tendencies and faults, his teaching was like deadly poisons [?] arrayed forbiddingly before one: to advance and taste them meant certain death. In naming punishment and tattooing, it was like executioners’ axes standing menacingly behind one: to retreat and shrink back meant certain execution. His admonitions to those in office were urgent in expression; his instruction of the youthful and inexperienced was detailed in explanation. His heavenly words, earnest and repeated, shone upon the written records, brilliant as the sun, moon, and stars set in the heavens. Was this not exceedingly clear? With the greatness of his counsels and the clarity of his instructions so manifest [?], how could one disregard them and fail to reflect upon them? Now, in later days, Tai Jia’s desires would undermine the established standards, and his indulgence would undermine ritual propriety. Yi Yin foresaw the first signs of this and therefore addressed these matters with earnest concern. When Yi Yin’s words went unheeded, the sacrifices to Tang nearly came to an end, and he had no choice but to take the measure of sending Tai Jia to the palace at Tong. He kept Tai Jia from associating closely with disobedient men; punishment and tattooing might otherwise have been inflicted upon him. Fortunately, after going to Tong, Tai Jia was able ultimately to fulfill true virtue and transmit…

之後世其君罔不成王畏相其臣罔不歷年有
恭而殷禮至於陟配天則由成湯前日謨訓之
及伊尹今日告戒之功也讀是書者所宜悉之
詩
如金如錫如圭如璧
張鍾靈

體認不真且於金錫圭璧處發揮不出此作形容殆盡讀
之使人興起
===
同考試官教諭許批發揮武公成德由進脩中來明
白通暢宜錄以式後學
考試官教諭俞批純正
考試官學正楊批能發揮詩人比德之意
詩人美賢侯德之成必儗以物之似者也甚矣
武公之德之成精純溫潤之至也詩人即物以
儗之不亦宜哉念昔武公慨俗學之沉迷資朝
士之交戒盡學問自脩之功極恂慄威儀之盛
其德之成宜何如哉是故自其德之精純者言
punctuated:
之後世，其君罔不成王畏相，其臣罔不歷年有恭，而殷禮至於陟配天，則由成湯前日謨訓之及伊尹今日告戒之功也。讀是書者所宜悉之。
詩

translation_en:
…to later generations, its rulers without exception became accomplished kings who held their ministers in awe, and its ministers without exception remained reverent throughout their years of service. That the rites of Yin reached the point of honoring its ascended rulers as counterparts to Heaven was due to the efficacy of Cheng Tang’s earlier counsels and instructions and Yi Yin’s admonitions on this occasion. Those who read this book should understand this fully.
Book of Odes
“Like gold, like tin; like a jade tablet, like a jade disc.”
Zhang Zhongling
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Writers generally fail to grasp truly Duke Wu’s refined purity and gentle warmth of virtue, and cannot develop the significance of the gold, tin, jade tablet, and jade disc. This composition describes these qualities almost exhaustively; reading it inspires one to better oneself.
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: It develops clearly and fluently the point that Duke Wu’s perfected virtue arose from advancing in self-cultivation. It should be recorded as a model for later students.
Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor: Pure and correct.
Comment by Examiner Yang, Director of Studies: It successfully develops the poet’s intention in comparing virtue to these objects.
When the poet praises a worthy lord’s perfected virtue, he invariably likens it to objects that resemble it. How great was the perfection of Duke Wu’s virtue: the utmost in refined purity and gentle warmth! Was it not fitting for the poet to draw upon objects to portray it? Consider how Duke Wu in former times deplored the delusions of conventional learning, drew upon the mutual admonitions of the gentlemen at court, devoted his utmost efforts to learning and self-cultivation, and brought reverent vigilance and dignified bearing to their fullest expression. How complete, then, must his virtue have become! Thus, speaking of the refined purity of his virtue…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之我武公由明而底於誠由反而復於性人泯
天定一真為之自如欲盡理還萬感為之俱寂
仁之至義之盡無二而無雜也德之精純如此
不如金如錫乎蓋金錫之為物出於鍛鍊也查
滓不留渾然無粗迹泥沙盡汰瑩然無餘疵莫
精純如也武公如之則德之精純有在於進脩
也明矣自其德之溫潤者言之我武公自勉然
而造於自然自可欲而至於無欲優游涵泳心
廣而體胖和順從容睟面而盎背仁之愛義之
和非猛而非厲也德之溫潤如此不如圭如璧
乎蓋圭璧之為物語其生質也具精粗之美雖
廉而不劌全天人之道恒柔而可嘉莫溫潤如
也武公如之則德之溫潤能充其美質也審矣
吁不惟精純而又溫潤如此則武公之德之成
至是而無以加矣詩人即金錫圭璧而形容之
其亦樂道人善而善言德行者歟抑考武公作
聖之功老而彌篤行年九十有五猶箴於國以
求交戒自警有懿戒之詩悔過有賓筵之作及
punctuated: 之，我武公由明而底於誠，由反而復於性，人泯天定，一真為之自如；欲盡理還，萬感為之俱寂。仁之至，義之盡，無二而無雜也。德之精純如此，不如金如錫乎？蓋金錫之為物，出於鍛鍊也，查滓不留，渾然無粗迹；泥沙盡汰，瑩然無餘疵，莫精純如也。武公如之，則德之精純有在於進脩也，明矣。自其德之溫潤者言之，我武公自勉然而造於自然，自可欲而至於無欲，優游涵泳，心廣而體胖；和順從容，睟面而盎背。仁之愛，義之和，非猛而非厲也。德之溫潤如此，不如圭如璧乎？蓋圭璧之為物，語其生質也，具精粗之美，雖廉而不劌；全天人之道，恒柔而可嘉，莫溫潤如也。武公如之，則德之溫潤能充其美質也，審矣。吁！不惟精純而又溫潤如此，則武公之德之成，至是而無以加矣。詩人即金錫圭璧而形容之，其亦樂道人善而善言德行者歟？抑考武公作聖之功，老而彌篤，行年九十有五，猶箴於國以求交戒。自警有懿戒之詩，悔過有賓筵之作，及
translation_en:
…speaking of this, our Duke Wu proceeded from understanding to sincerity, and through turning back recovered his original nature. Human selfishness vanished and Heaven’s endowment became settled; undivided authenticity operated freely within him. Desires were exhausted and principle restored; the myriad stirrings of feeling all became still. His benevolence reached its utmost and his righteousness its fullest extent, without division or admixture. With his virtue so refined and pure, was he not like gold and tin? Gold and tin emerge from smelting and refinement: no dross remains, and their wholeness bears no trace of coarseness; earth and sand are entirely removed, leaving a lustrous substance without any residual flaw. Nothing matches their refinement and purity. Since Duke Wu resembled them, it is clear that the refinement and purity of his virtue depended upon advancing in self-cultivation.
Speaking of the warmth and lustre of his virtue, our Duke Wu progressed from deliberate effort to natural ease, and from what is worthy of desire to freedom from desire. At ease, he immersed himself in cultivation; his mind was broad and his body at ease. Harmonious, compliant, and composed, his virtue shone in his face and filled his back. His benevolent love and righteous harmony were neither fierce nor severe. With his virtue so warm and lustrous, was he not like a jade tablet or jade disc? As for the native substance of jade tablets and discs, they possess beauty in both their finer and coarser aspects [?]; though edged, they do not cut. They embody the completeness of the ways of Heaven and humanity, ever gentle and worthy of praise. Nothing matches their warmth and lustre. Since Duke Wu resembled them, it is certain that the warmth and lustre of his virtue fully realized the beauty of his native endowment.
Ah! Being not only refined and pure but also warm and lustrous in this way, Duke Wu’s perfected virtue had reached a point beyond which nothing could be added. In depicting him through gold, tin, jade tablets, and jade discs, was the poet not one who delighted in speaking of others’ goodness and excelled at describing virtuous conduct? Moreover, if we examine Duke Wu’s efforts to become a sage, they grew still more earnest in old age. At ninety-five, he still sought admonitions throughout his state so that all might counsel him. To admonish himself, he had the poem Admonition to Restraint (Yi jie) [?]; to repent of his faults, he composed The Guests at the Mats (Bin yan). And…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
是詩所詠自切磋琢磨以至於瑟僩赫咺寬綽
戲謔則其動容周旋之間無適而非禮也然則
盛德至善民不能忘而謂之睿聖武公豈不有
由然哉
俾侯于魯大啓爾宇為周室輔
劉槩
同考試官教諭陳批成王分封宗室意正如此學者
偏見臆說類以大啓爾宇將錫之山川土田附庸入講殊
與傳註居字相礙此作一本經傳發揮深得本旨
===
同考試官教諭許批文辭雄偉真作家也取寘前列
允稱
考試官教諭俞批此作體認親切一洗塵腐
考試官學正楊批辭理俱優
重宗室之封為王室之計周王告親臣然也甚
矣封建之不苟也成王封伯禽而重之者正所
以為周室計耳豈特為伯禽計哉昔魯人美僖
公脩廟而推原有魯之由至此述成王告周公
之意若曰當牧野敦商之日正叔父建功之時
punctuated:
是詩所詠，自切磋琢磨以至於瑟僩赫咺、寬綽戲謔，則其動容周旋之間，無適而非禮也。然則盛德至善，民不能忘，而謂之睿聖武公，豈不有由然哉？
俾侯于魯，大啓爾宇，為周室輔。
劉槩

translation_en:
…what this poem celebrates, from cutting and filing, chiseling and polishing, through dignity and majesty, brilliance and distinction, generosity and ease, and playful conversation, shows that every movement and action of his accorded with ritual propriety. Thus, his abundant virtue and consummate goodness were unforgettable to the people, who called him the sagacious and sage Duke Wu. Surely there was good reason for this?
“Let him be enfeoffed as lord in Lu; greatly enlarge your dwelling, to serve as a bulwark of the royal house of Zhou.”
Liu Gai 劉槩
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Precisely such was King Cheng’s intention in enfeoffing members of the royal clan. Scholars, with their partial views and conjectural explanations, commonly interpret ‘greatly enlarge your dwelling’ by bringing into their exposition the mountains, rivers, lands, fields, and dependent states that would be bestowed. This is quite at odds with the word ‘dwelling’ in the commentary. This composition develops its argument wholly on the basis of the classic and its commentary, thoroughly grasping the original meaning.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “The language is powerful and magnificent: truly the work of an accomplished writer. Its placement among the foremost is fully deserved.”
Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor: “This composition shows an intimate and precise grasp of its subject, sweeping away all stale conventions.”
Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: “Both expression and reasoning are excellent.”
To attach great importance to the enfeoffment of the royal clan was to plan for the royal house: such was the meaning of the king of Zhou’s address to his kinsman and minister. How far the establishment of fiefs was from being a casual matter! King Cheng’s enfeoffment of Boqin, and the importance he attached to it, were precisely a means of planning for the royal house of Zhou. Could he have been planning solely for Boqin’s sake? In former times, the people of Lu praised Duke Xi for restoring the ancestral temple and traced the origins of Lu. At this point, they recounted the purport of King Cheng’s words to the Duke of Zhou, as though he had said: “The day when Shang was attacked at Muye was precisely the time when you, my uncle, rendered meritorious service …

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
迨我小子豈敢忘哉爰舉報功之典允宜元子
之封封之何如蓋地有不善不可以爲爾元子
處也我今爲爾圖之蒙羽之野實惟形勝俾侯
于此信圭驚冕照耀乎泗水之湄乘馬路車馳
驅乎泰山之麓鳧繹龜蒙舉奄有而無外須句
常許悉兼統而不遺隱然爲東方之巨鎮也宇
有不大不可以爲爾元子居也我其爲爾啓之
宮宇之制實惟宏壯使居於斯竹苞松茂夏屋
爲之渠渠烏革翬飛堂寢爲之翼翼規模以拓
===
不苟合而苟完制度以新必美輪而美奐屹然
爲東魯之雄藩也是則隆封建之典者豈直爲
爾元子富貴之計哉誠以王都乃藩國之本根
藩國實王都之保障正欲爾元子思恩之所自
出而敏於効勞念本之所由來而勤於圖報作
之屏作之翰翊我宗社於無虞謹乃度愼乃心
鞏我皇圖於不拔郟鄏之鼎扶之於萬年保爾
魯於萬年也蒼姬之統輔之於百世綿爾魯於
百世也是則我魯之封其來之遠如此爲僖公
punctuated: 迨我小子，豈敢忘哉？爰舉報功之典，允宜元子之封。封之何如？蓋地有不善，不可以爲爾元子處也。我今爲爾圖之，蒙羽之野，實惟形勝，俾侯于此。信圭驚冕，照耀乎泗水之湄；乘馬路車，馳驅乎泰山之麓。鳧繹龜蒙，舉奄有而無外；須句常許，悉兼統而不遺。隱然爲東方之巨鎮也。宇有不大，不可以爲爾元子居也。我其爲爾啓之，宮宇之制，實惟宏壯，使居於斯。竹苞松茂，夏屋爲之渠渠；烏革翬飛，堂寢爲之翼翼。規模以拓，不苟合而苟完；制度以新，必美輪而美奐。屹然爲東魯之雄藩也。是則隆封建之典者，豈直爲爾元子富貴之計哉？誠以王都乃藩國之本根，藩國實王都之保障。正欲爾元子思恩之所自出而敏於効勞，念本之所由來而勤於圖報。作之屏，作之翰，翊我宗社於無虞；謹乃度，愼乃心，鞏我皇圖於不拔。郟鄏之鼎，扶之於萬年，保爾魯於萬年也；蒼姬之統，輔之於百世，綿爾魯於百世也。」是則我魯之封，其來之遠如此。爲僖公
translation_en:
…Now that rule has passed to me, the young one, how could I dare forget? Accordingly, I institute the ceremony of rewarding merit: it is indeed fitting that your eldest son receive a fief. What should his enfeoffment be like? Land that is unsuitable cannot serve as a place for your eldest son to settle. I shall now plan this for you. The countryside of Meng and Yu has commanding terrain; let him rule here as a lord. His ceremonial jade tablet and cap [?] will shine beside the Si River; his team of four horses and state carriage will speed along the foot of Mount Tai. The mountains Fu, Yi, Gui, and Meng shall all fall within his possession, with none excluded; Xuju, Chang, and Xu [?] shall all come under his authority, with none omitted. Thus his domain will stand imposingly as a great stronghold of the east.

“Dwellings that are insufficiently spacious cannot serve as a residence for your eldest son. I shall establish them for you. The palace buildings shall be grand and imposing in design, and he shall dwell here. Like clustered bamboo and flourishing pines, the great buildings shall be spacious; like a crow spreading its wings [?] and a pheasant in flight, the halls and private chambers shall rise in stately order. Their scale shall be expansive: they must not be carelessly put together or hastily completed. Their design shall be renewed: they must be magnificent in height and splendid in ornament. Thus his domain will stand tall as a mighty bulwark in eastern Lu.

“In thus honoring the institution of enfeoffment, could I be planning merely for your eldest son’s wealth and rank? Truly, the royal capital is the root of the feudatory states, and the feudatory states are the protection of the royal capital. My purpose is precisely that your eldest son should reflect on the source of his favor and be prompt in rendering service, remember whence his foundations came and strive diligently to repay that kindness. Let him serve as a screen and a supporting pillar, protecting our ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain from danger. Be scrupulous in your conduct and cautious in your heart, securing our imperial dominion against overthrow. By sustaining the tripods at Jiaru for ten thousand years, you will preserve your Lu for ten thousand years; by supporting the succession of the venerable Ji house for a hundred generations, you will perpetuate your Lu for a hundred generations.”

Such, then, are the distant origins of the enfeoffment of our Lu. As for Duke Xi…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
者可不知所自哉抑論封建非古也而肇於周
周之封建豈苟焉哉因其有功而報之非濫冀
其立功而託之非輕也繼周而漢封三庶孽分
天下半已失周人之遺意矣降及後世支庶益
繁分封益廣而民之財力益竭不識是時司民
命者節奢費省勞役而厚邦本果若之何留意
邪斯固魯人言之未及者故表而出之
春秋
六月雨僖公三年
李文欽
同考試官教諭李批題本平易作者不失之枯則失
之泛殊為可厭此篇說出僖公喜雨之意詳盡允宜錄出
考試官教諭俞批說出當時喜雨氣象
考試官學正楊批僖公敬天勤民之意宛然可見
春秋志天道之順所以著人君之賢蓋喜雨而
樂民之樂其必閔雨而憂民之憂矣春秋特書
六月雨則僖公有志於民而君道之盡也端可
見矣慨昔魯僖當國旱魃為災歷三時之不雨
punctuated:
者，可不知所自哉？抑論封建，非古也，而肇於周。周之封建，豈苟焉哉？因其有功而報之，非濫；冀其立功而託之，非輕也。繼周而漢，封三庶孽，分天下半，已失周人之遺意矣。降及後世，支庶益繁，分封益廣，而民之財力益竭。不識是時司民命者，節奢費、省勞役而厚邦本，果若之何留意邪？斯固魯人言之未及者，故表而出之。

春秋
「六月雨。」僖公三年。
李文欽

同考試官教諭李批：題本平易，作者不失之枯，則失之泛，殊為可厭。此篇說出僖公喜雨之意，詳盡，允宜錄出。
考試官教諭俞批：說出當時喜雨氣象。
考試官學正楊批：僖公敬天勤民之意，宛然可見。

春秋志天道之順，所以著人君之賢。蓋喜雨而樂民之樂，其必閔雨而憂民之憂矣。春秋特書「六月雨」，則僖公有志於民，而君道之盡也，端可見矣。慨昔魯僖當國，旱魃為災，歷三時之不雨。
translation_en:
…could one in Duke Xi’s position fail to understand whence this came? Now, as for enfeoffment, it was not an ancient institution but began with the Zhou. Could the Zhou have enfeoffed lords arbitrarily? Rewarding men for their achievements was no indiscriminate generosity; entrusting them with domains in the hope that they would render service was no trifling commitment. The Han, succeeding the Zhou, enfeoffed three sons of secondary wives [?], allotting them half the realm, and had already lost the intent bequeathed by the Zhou. In later ages, collateral branches and sons of secondary wives grew ever more numerous, enfeoffments ever more extensive, and the people’s wealth and strength ever more depleted. I wonder how much attention those responsible for the people’s lives at such times actually gave to curbing extravagant expenditure, reducing labor service, and strengthening the foundations of the state. These are matters that the people of Lu did not address in their words; therefore I have brought them to light.

Spring and Autumn Annals
“In the sixth month, it rained.” Third year of Duke Xi.
By Li Wenqin.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: The topic is straightforward, but writers either fall into dryness or lapse into vagueness, making their work particularly tiresome. This essay brings out Duke Xi’s joy at the rain in full detail and certainly deserves to be selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor: It conveys the atmosphere of rejoicing at the rain at that time.
Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: Duke Xi’s reverence for Heaven and diligent concern for the people are vividly apparent.

The Spring and Autumn Annals records the harmonious course of Heaven in order to manifest the worthiness of a ruler. For one who rejoices at rain and shares the people’s joy must also have been troubled by its absence and shared the people’s anxiety. By expressly recording, “In the sixth month, it rained,” the Spring and Autumn Annals makes plainly evident Duke Xi’s concern for the people and his complete fulfillment of the ruler’s Way. Alas, when Duke Xi of Lu governed the state, the drought demon brought calamity, and three seasons passed without rain…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
將五穀之不登僖也上懼天災下恤民隱遠惟
殷帝桑林之責近體周王方社之勤一誠格天
百神受職當三疇旱暵之際適六月亢陽之時
龍騰霄而陰雲四合鸛鳴垤而甘雨溥施地之
赤者以潤苗之槁者以興由公及私在在以之
而霑足自中徂外物物以之而欣榮大有可期
而滿慰三農之望昔之呻吟者轉而爲謳歌矣
豐登可卜而頓消四境之憂向之疾蹙者移而
爲懽欣矣公於斯時也夫豈不曰國以民爲本
===
民以食爲天雨而不降食何所仰邪又豈不曰
民以君爲心君以民爲體民而不樂君能獨樂
邪顧玆時雨之施竊喜豐年之兆彼農歌于野
工歌于肆民之樂矣公亦樂形舞蹈而不之知
商歌于市旅歌于途民之喜矣公亦喜動顏色
而莫之禦時乎燕享而爾游爾休則與卿士樂
於朝矣臺池鳥獸曷足以方其樂乎時乎巡行
而一遊一豫則與農夫樂於野矣鐘鼓管籥曷
足以擬其樂乎吁以吾心之和感天心之和以
punctuated: 將五穀之不登。僖也，上懼天災，下恤民隱，遠惟殷帝桑林之責，近體周王方社之勤。一誠格天，百神受職。當三疇旱暵之際，適六月亢陽之時，龍騰霄而陰雲四合，鸛鳴垤而甘雨溥施。地之赤者以潤，苗之槁者以興。由公及私，在在以之而霑足；自中徂外，物物以之而欣榮。大有可期，而滿慰三農之望，昔之呻吟者轉而爲謳歌矣；豐登可卜，而頓消四境之憂，向之疾蹙者移而爲懽欣矣。公於斯時也，夫豈不曰：「國以民爲本，民以食爲天，雨而不降，食何所仰邪？」又豈不曰：「民以君爲心，君以民爲體，民而不樂，君能獨樂邪？」顧玆時雨之施，竊喜豐年之兆。彼農歌于野，工歌于肆，民之樂矣，公亦樂形舞蹈而不之知；商歌于市，旅歌于途，民之喜矣，公亦喜動顏色而莫之禦。時乎燕享，而爾游爾休，則與卿士樂於朝矣，臺池鳥獸曷足以方其樂乎？時乎巡行，而一遊一豫，則與農夫樂於野矣，鐘鼓管籥曷足以擬其樂乎？吁！以吾心之和感天心之和，以
translation_en:
…and the five grains were on the verge of failing to ripen. Duke Xi feared Heaven’s calamities above and felt compassion for the people’s suffering below. Looking to the distant past, he pondered the Yin sovereign’s self-reproach at Sanglin; looking to more recent times, he emulated the Zhou king’s diligence in sacrifices to the powers of the four directions and the soil. His single-minded sincerity reached Heaven, and the hundred spirits fulfilled their duties. Just when the fields lay parched by drought, in the sixth month’s season of excessive heat, dragons soared into the sky and dark clouds gathered on every side; cranes cried upon the anthills and welcome rain fell everywhere. The bare, red earth was moistened, and withered seedlings revived. From the public fields to the private plots, every place received abundant moisture; from the center to the outlying regions, all things flourished joyfully. A great harvest could now be expected, fully satisfying the hopes of the farming people, and those who had formerly groaned now broke into song. An abundant yield could be foretold, suddenly dispelling anxiety throughout the realm, and those who had been distressed and hard-pressed became joyful.

At this moment, would the duke not have said: “The state takes the people as its foundation, and the people take food as their Heaven. If rain does not fall, on what can they depend for food?” And would he not also have said: “The people take their ruler as their heart, and the ruler takes the people as his body. If the people are not happy, can the ruler alone be happy?” Seeing this timely rain bestowed, he rejoiced inwardly at the promise of a plentiful year. Farmers sang in the fields and artisans in their workshops: the people were happy, and the duke, too, expressed his happiness in dancing without even realizing it. Merchants sang in the markets and travelers on the roads: the people rejoiced, and the duke, too, could not restrain the joy that showed upon his face. When he held banquets, taking his ease and rest, he shared the joy of his ministers and officers at court. How could terraces, ponds, birds, and beasts compare with such joy? When he made tours of inspection, each excursion and outing brought him joy together with the farmers in the countryside. How could bells, drums, pipes, and flutes rival such joy? Ah! With the harmony of my own heart I call forth the harmony of Heaven’s heart, and with…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
民心之樂爲吾心之樂天人相爲流通君民相
爲一體然則僖公其賢矣哉故春秋特於三時
不雨之後而有六月雨之書雨云者喜雨也所
以美僖公之賢而爲後世人君不以民事繫憂
樂者之戒垂訓之義不其大歟抑考僖公之賢
不止此也儉以足用寬以愛民務農重穀則誠
賢君也較之文公忽天灾而不懼視民隱而不
恤自樂其樂而不與民同者大相遠矣夫何中
年漸肆荒怠失政於大臣取執於伯主從夷慢
===
王之類經不絶書大非初年之比此僖所以不
得全爲賢侯也詩曰靡不有初鮮克有終其僖
之謂歟
叔孫州仇帥師墮郈季孫斯仲孫何忌
帥師墮費定公十二年
羅濟
同考試官教諭李批作者爲題目所窘率多牽撫成
文令人厭觀此篇說出聖人抑私家以張公室之意明白
痛快是宜錄之
punctuated:
民心之樂爲吾心之樂，天人相爲流通，君民相爲一體，然則僖公其賢矣哉！故《春秋》特於三時不雨之後，而有六月雨之書。雨云者，喜雨也，所以美僖公之賢，而爲後世人君不以民事繫憂樂者之戒。垂訓之義，不其大歟？抑考僖公之賢，不止此也。儉以足用，寬以愛民，務農重穀，則誠賢君也。較之文公忽天灾而不懼，視民隱而不恤，自樂其樂而不與民同者，大相遠矣。夫何中年漸肆荒怠，失政於大臣，取執於伯主，從夷慢王之類，經不絶書，大非初年之比！此僖所以不得全爲賢侯也。《詩》曰：「靡不有初，鮮克有終。」其僖之謂歟？

叔孫州仇帥師墮郈，季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費。定公十二年。
羅濟

同考試官教諭李批：作者爲題目所窘，率多牽撫成文，令人厭觀。此篇說出聖人抑私家以張公室之意，明白痛快，是宜錄之。
translation_en:
…take the joy of the people's hearts as the joy of my own heart. Heaven and humanity thus communicate with one another, and ruler and people form a single body. Was Duke Xi not, then, a worthy ruler! Thus, after recording three seasons without rain, the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically records rain in the sixth month. Its mention of rain expresses delight in rain: it praises Duke Xi's worthiness and warns later rulers who do not make the people's affairs the source of their sorrow and joy. Is the significance of this instruction for posterity not great? Moreover, Duke Xi's worthiness was not confined to this. He practiced frugality to ensure sufficient resources, showed generosity in caring for the people, promoted agriculture, and valued grain. He was indeed a worthy ruler. How greatly he differed from Duke Wen, who disregarded Heaven-sent calamities without fear, saw the people's suffering without concern, and enjoyed his own pleasures without sharing them with the people! Why, then, midway through his reign did he increasingly give himself over to negligence and indolence, lose control of government to his great ministers, and suffer capture by the hegemon? His following the barbarians, slighting the king, and similar acts are repeatedly recorded in the Classic; these were far removed from his early years. This is why Xi cannot be deemed an entirely worthy feudal lord. The Book of Odes says: “All have a beginning; few can carry through to the end.” Does this not describe Xi?

“Shusun Zhouqiu led troops to demolish the fortifications of Hou; Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led troops to demolish the fortifications of Fei.” Twelfth year of Duke Ding.
By Luo Ji.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Writers constrained by this topic have mostly resorted to forced connections [?] to compose their essays, making them tiresome to read. This essay brings out the Sage's intention to restrain the private ministerial houses and strengthen the ducal house. Its exposition is clear and thoroughly satisfying; it deserves inclusion.

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭俞批辭嚴義正深得聖人爲國以
之意
考試官學正楊批聖人過化之功觀此篇可以見
其一節云
即聖人以禮化强之速見聖人以禮爲國之兆
夫爲國莫大於禮也聖人以禮而革强都之僭
如此則其爲之兆也可見矣且郈乃叔孫之私
邑費則季孫之强都之二邑也嘗聞相繼而城
矣今相繼而墮何邪蓋由聖人以禮革其僭耳
===
誠以制國不過千乘都城不過百雉禮之大防
也家無甲兵之藏邑無百雉之城禮之大閑也
叔孫越禮城其郈季孫僭禮城其費公室由之
不張私家因之屢叛是蓋昧於禮之大防忽於
禮之大閑也幸而孔子用魯得政期月以治世
之禮律衰世之臣諭以陪臣屢叛之由諭之以
禮也示以食邑恃强之故示之以禮也由是叔
孫悔悟首起而墮郈季孫感化繼起而墮費圮
其城湮其池王制由之而正收爾兵出爾甲國
punctuated:
考試官教諭俞批：辭嚴義正，深得聖人爲國以之意。
考試官學正楊批：聖人過化之功，觀此篇可以見其一節云。
即聖人以禮化强之速，見聖人以禮爲國之兆。
夫爲國莫大於禮也。聖人以禮而革强都之僭如此，則其爲之兆也可見矣。且郈乃叔孫之私邑，費則季孫之强都，之二邑也，嘗聞相繼而城矣。今相繼而墮，何邪？蓋由聖人以禮革其僭耳。
誠以制國不過千乘，都城不過百雉，禮之大防也；家無甲兵之藏，邑無百雉之城，禮之大閑也。叔孫越禮城其郈，季孫僭禮城其費，公室由之不張，私家因之屢叛，是蓋昧於禮之大防，忽於禮之大閑也。幸而孔子用魯，得政期月，以治世之禮律衰世之臣。諭以陪臣屢叛之由，諭之以禮也；示以食邑恃强之故，示之以禮也。由是叔孫悔悟，首起而墮郈；季孫感化，繼起而墮費。圮其城，湮其池，王制由之而正；收爾兵，出爾甲，國
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor: The language is stern and the principles correct; it deeply grasps the sage’s intention in governing a state through [?].

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: This essay reveals one aspect of the sage’s power to transform wherever he passes.

From the speed with which the sage transformed the powerful through ritual propriety, we see an indication of his governing the state through ritual propriety.

In governing a state, nothing is more important than ritual propriety. When the sage used it to eliminate the usurpations of powerful fortified towns in this way, the signs of his governing could be seen. Hou was the private settlement of the Shusun lineage, while Bi was the powerful fortified town of the Jisun lineage. These two settlements [?], we have heard, had been fortified in succession. Why were their walls now demolished in succession? Simply because the sage used ritual propriety to eliminate their usurpations.

Indeed, a state’s establishment must not exceed a thousand chariots, and a town’s walls must not exceed a hundred zhi: these are the great safeguards of ritual propriety. A noble household must not store armor and weapons, and its settlements must not have walls of a hundred zhi: these are the great restraints of ritual propriety. Shusun transgressed ritual propriety by fortifying Hou; Jisun violated it through the presumptuous fortification of Bi. Consequently, the ducal house could not assert its authority, while the private households repeatedly rebelled. This was surely ignorance of ritual propriety’s great safeguards and disregard for its great restraints.

Fortunately, Confucius was employed in Lu and exercised governing authority for a full year, applying the ritual standards of an orderly age to the ministers of an age of decline. In explaining why their subordinate retainers repeatedly rebelled, he instructed them through ritual propriety; in showing why their fief settlements relied upon their strength, he enlightened them through ritual propriety. Thus Shusun repented and awakened, taking the lead in demolishing Hou’s walls; Jisun was moved and transformed, following him in demolishing Bi’s walls. Their walls were pulled down and their moats filled in, thereby restoring the proper royal institutions. Gather up your weapons and bring out your armor, and the state’s…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
勢以之而尊以身使臂之義斯明何有尾大不
掉之患强榦弱枝之勢已立何有末大必折之
虞不動聲色而公室自張不假威力而私家自
服何莫非聖人以禮為國之所致歟所謂期月
而可豈虛語哉是禮也推而形諸魯國而準則
地方五百里吾知疆理必正興滅繼絕之義舉
而王政行矣郈費之墮乃其權輿也吾知君臣
交順事上使下之禮得而王道復矣私邑之革
乃其造端也若此者豈非聖人以禮為國而發
===
此以為之兆也歟所謂三年有成有由然矣雖
然聖人以禮為國不特致魯臣之感化當夫夾
谷之會齊君亦感化而有三田之歸變齊變魯
之機無非一禮之所為者使魯終用聖人則文
武成康之治復見於今日矣惜夫女樂皐門聖
轍汶上豈天未欲平治天下而使之不克終用
也邪殆將欲其刪述六經以垂憲萬世也斯又
不可不知
禮記
punctuated:
勢以之而尊。以身使臂之義斯明，何有尾大不掉之患？强榦弱枝之勢已立，何有末大必折之虞？不動聲色而公室自張，不假威力而私家自服，何莫非聖人以禮為國之所致歟？所謂期月而可，豈虛語哉！是禮也，推而形諸魯國而準則，地方五百里，吾知疆理必正，興滅繼絕之義舉而王政行矣。郈費之墮，乃其權輿也。吾知君臣交順，事上使下之禮得而王道復矣。私邑之革，乃其造端也。若此者，豈非聖人以禮為國而發此以為之兆也歟？所謂三年有成，有由然矣。雖然，聖人以禮為國，不特致魯臣之感化。當夫夾谷之會，齊君亦感化而有三田之歸。變齊變魯之機，無非一禮之所為者。使魯終用聖人，則文武成康之治復見於今日矣。惜夫！女樂皐門，聖轍汶上，豈天未欲平治天下而使之不克終用也邪？殆將欲其刪述六經，以垂憲萬世也。斯又不可不知。

禮記
translation_en:
…the state's authority was thereby exalted. The principle of the body directing the arm was thus made clear: how could there be the trouble of a tail too large to wag? With the trunk strengthened and the branches weakened, how could there be fear that overgrown extremities would inevitably break off? Without any show of agitation, the ducal house naturally grew strong; without recourse to coercive force, the private houses naturally submitted. Was not all this brought about by the sage's governing the state through ritual propriety? Could the saying that results could be achieved within a full year have been empty words?

If this ritual propriety were extended and embodied in Lu as its standard, throughout its territory five hundred li square, I know that its boundaries would surely be properly ordered. The principles of restoring extinguished states and continuing severed lines of succession would be upheld, and kingly government would prevail. The demolition of Hou and Fei was its beginning. I know that ruler and ministers would act in mutual accord; the rites governing service to superiors and the direction of subordinates would be properly observed, and the Kingly Way would be restored. The reform of private domains was its first step. Were these not signs that the sage, governing the state through ritual propriety, brought forth to foreshadow what was to come? Thus the saying that success could be achieved in three years had good grounds.

Yet the sage's governing through ritual propriety did more than transform the ministers of Lu. At the meeting at Jiagu, the ruler of Qi was also transformed and returned the three territories. The impulse to transform Qi and Lu arose entirely from ritual propriety alone. Had Lu continued to employ the sage, the government of Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang would have appeared again in that age. Alas! Female musicians at the Gao Gate, and the sage's carriage tracks by the Wen River! [?] Was Heaven not yet willing to bring peace and order to the world, and did it therefore prevent Lu from continuing to employ him? Perhaps Heaven intended him to edit and transmit the Six Classics, leaving a model for ten thousand generations. This, too, must be understood.

Book of Rites

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
禮樂刑政四達而不悖則王道備矣
彭綸
同考試官學正蔡批作者多以王道備處就指禮樂刑
政為言殊失本旨此篇照應上章好惡無節以下入講最為得之
考試官教諭俞批講王道備處明白可取
考試官學正楊批理明辭順
治具畢張而無違王者之治化成矣甚矣治化
之難成也使非王者治具畢張而無違又何以
致之哉思昔先王慨人好惡之不平馴至人道
===
之不正不得不有以平天下之情而復人道之正
乎平之何如是故出治之本莫先於禮樂也于
焉為之禮樂以動化於其始輔治之法莫要於
刑政也于焉為之刑政以維持於其終然禮節
民心樂和民聲固行之天下而無間矣及刑以
防之政以行之亦達之四海而不遺焉生斯世
也為斯民也莫不心節於禮聲和於樂曽無一
人之或悖莫不奸防於刑教行於政亦無一夫
之敢違若然則是上焉綱舉目張而無遠弗届
punctuated:
禮樂刑政四達而不悖，則王道備矣。
彭綸
同考試官學正蔡批：作者多以王道備處就指禮樂刑政為言，殊失本旨。此篇照應上章好惡無節以下入講，最為得之。
考試官教諭俞批：講王道備處明白可取。
考試官學正楊批：理明辭順。
治具畢張而無違，王者之治化成矣。甚矣，治化之難成也！使非王者治具畢張而無違，又何以致之哉？思昔先王慨人好惡之不平，馴至人道之不正，不得不有以平天下之情而復人道之正乎？平之何如？是故出治之本，莫先於禮樂也，于焉為之禮樂，以動化於其始；輔治之法，莫要於刑政也，于焉為之刑政，以維持於其終。然禮節民心，樂和民聲，固行之天下而無間矣；及刑以防之，政以行之，亦達之四海而不遺焉。生斯世也，為斯民也，莫不心節於禮、聲和於樂，曽無一人之或悖；莫不奸防於刑、教行於政，亦無一夫之敢違。若然，則是上焉綱舉目張而無遠弗届
translation_en:
“When rites, music, punishments, and government extend everywhere without discord, the Kingly Way is complete.”
Peng Lun
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, School Director: Most writers, in discussing the completeness of the Kingly Way, simply speak of rites, music, punishments, and government, thoroughly missing the central meaning. This essay begins its exposition by taking account of the preceding chapter’s passage beginning “likes and dislikes are without restraint.” It captures the meaning particularly well.
Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor: The discussion of the completeness of the Kingly Way is clear and worthy of approval.
Comment by Examiner Yang, School Director: The reasoning is clear and the language flows smoothly.
When all the instruments of government are fully deployed and meet with no contravention, the true king’s governance and moral transformation are accomplished. How difficult it is to accomplish governance and moral transformation! Unless the true king’s instruments of government were fully deployed and met with no contravention, how could he achieve this? Consider the former kings of old: they lamented that people’s likes and dislikes lacked balance, gradually leading to disorder in the human way. Were they not therefore compelled to find means to bring the feelings of all under Heaven into balance and restore the human way to its proper order? How was this balance to be achieved? Thus, among the foundations of governing, nothing takes precedence over rites and music. Accordingly, they instituted rites and music to move and transform people at the outset. Among the methods that support governance, nothing is more essential than punishments and government. Accordingly, they instituted punishments and government to sustain this transformation through to its completion. Rites restrain the people’s hearts, and music harmonizes their voices: these were indeed practiced throughout all under Heaven without interruption. Punishments to guard against wrongdoing and government to put instruction into effect likewise reached throughout the Four Seas, leaving nowhere untouched. Of those born into this age and numbered among its people, none failed to have their hearts restrained by rites and their voices harmonized by music; not a single person acted discordantly. For all, wrongdoing was checked by punishments and instruction put into effect through government; not a single person dared contravene them. If this were so, then above, the guiding cord would be raised and every mesh of the net spread open, reaching even the most distant places …

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
下焉近悅遠懷而有感必從矣王道寧有不備
者哉吾見人人囿於化育之中在在歸諸範圍
之內危者安微者著人情由是而平善有勸惡
有懲人道由茲而正合衆寡強弱而各安其分
何有於悖逆詐僞之心合老幼孤獨而各得其
所何有於淫泆作亂之事無一地而不沐至治
之休所謂王道蕩蕩無偏無黨矣無一民而不
蒙至治之澤所謂王道平平無反無側矣王者
之治道豈不於是而備也邪抑論之人君之爲
===
治也有禮樂而無刑政是謂徒善有刑政而無
禮樂是謂徒法皆不足以言治也古之聖王有
見於此制禮于履作樂於豫致刑於豐明政於
賁既有禮樂以爲出治之本又有刑政以爲輔
治之法所以能使四海爲一家中國爲一人者
由舉此而措之耳後世則有不然或徒事刑威
而禮樂之未遑或有志禮樂而淫慝之靡正治
之所以卒不古若也然則欲求王道之備必禮
樂刑政四達不悖而後可
punctuated:
下焉近悅遠懷，而有感必從矣。王道寧有不備者哉？吾見人人囿於化育之中，在在歸諸範圍之內。危者安，微者著，人情由是而平；善有勸，惡有懲，人道由茲而正。合衆寡強弱而各安其分，何有於悖逆詐僞之心？合老幼孤獨而各得其所，何有於淫泆作亂之事？無一地而不沐至治之休，所謂王道蕩蕩，無偏無黨矣；無一民而不蒙至治之澤，所謂王道平平，無反無側矣。王者之治道豈不於是而備也邪？
抑論之，人君之爲治也，有禮樂而無刑政，是謂徒善；有刑政而無禮樂，是謂徒法：皆不足以言治也。古之聖王有見於此，制禮于履，作樂於豫，致刑於豐，明政於賁。既有禮樂以爲出治之本，又有刑政以爲輔治之法，所以能使四海爲一家、中國爲一人者，由舉此而措之耳。後世則有不然，或徒事刑威而禮樂之未遑，或有志禮樂而淫慝之靡正，治之所以卒不古若也。然則欲求王道之備，必禮樂刑政四達不悖而後可。
translation_en:
…among those below, the nearby rejoice and the distant are drawn to allegiance; all who feel its influence will follow. How could the kingly Way fail to be complete? I see everyone encompassed within its transforming and nurturing influence, and every place brought within its bounds. Those in peril find security, and the obscure gain recognition; human feelings thereby attain equilibrium. Goodness receives encouragement and evil receives punishment; the human Way is thereby set right. The many and the few, the strong and the weak, are brought together, each content with their allotted position: how could thoughts of rebellion or deceit arise? The old and the young, the orphaned and the solitary, are brought together, each finding their proper place: how could acts of debauchery or disorder occur? No place fails to enjoy the blessings of consummate government. This is what is meant by “The kingly Way is broad and open, without partiality or faction.” No person fails to receive the beneficence of consummate government. This is what is meant by “The kingly Way is level and even, without perversity or deviation.” Is not the king’s way of governing thereby made complete?
To consider the matter further: when a ruler governs with rites and music but without punishments and administration, this is called mere goodness; with punishments and administration but without rites and music, this is called mere law. Neither suffices to constitute government. The sage kings of antiquity understood this: they instituted rites in accordance with Lü (Treading), created music in accordance with Yu (Enthusiasm), applied punishments in accordance with Feng (Abundance), and clarified administration in accordance with Bi (Adornment). They possessed rites and music as the foundation from which government proceeds, and punishments and administration as the means of supporting it. Their ability to make all within the Four Seas one family and the Central States one person came simply from putting these into practice. In later ages this was not so. Some attended solely to the intimidating power of punishment and had no leisure for rites and music; others aspired to rites and music but failed to correct licentiousness and wickedness. This is why their government ultimately fell short of antiquity. Thus, to seek completeness in the kingly Way, rites, music, punishments, and administration must all extend everywhere without conflicting with one another; only then can it be achieved.

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
以之軍旅有禮故武功成也
朱衮
同考試官學正蔡批發揮行師之義詳盡本房無出
其右者矣
考試官教諭俞批辭暢理明蓋究心於是經者
考試官學正楊批辭理俱到
論行師之有制則無敵於天下矣甚矣天下無
敵則武功之成可知矣自非行師有制烏能以
致是哉仲尼燕居因論禮之無乎不在至此蓋
===
謂國之大事莫過乎戎戰之必克在得其道彼
王者受命而爲天子繼世以有天下或蠻夷猖
獗奉天討以徂征則軍旅不容於不出也或藩
屏跳梁奮神威而薄伐則軍旅不容以不興也
然果若之何而有禮邪是故萬二千五百人爲
軍五百人爲旅也當其命將出師之日選士厲
兵之時無忽心無惰氣持重謹畏之恒存不敢
妄動防範綱維之甚密左之右之而部
嚴明節制足以壯三軍之膽坐之起之而行
punctuated:
以之軍旅，有禮故武功成也。
朱衮。
同考試官學正蔡批：發揮行師之義詳盡，本房無出其右者矣。
考試官教諭俞批：辭暢理明，蓋究心於是經者。
考試官學正楊批：辭理俱到。
論行師之有制，則無敵於天下矣。甚矣！天下無敵，則武功之成可知矣。自非行師有制，烏能以致是哉？仲尼燕居，因論禮之無乎不在，至此蓋謂國之大事莫過乎戎，戰之必克在得其道。彼王者受命而爲天子，繼世以有天下，或蠻夷猖獗，奉天討以徂征，則軍旅不容於不出也；或藩屏跳梁，奮神威而薄伐，則軍旅不容以不興也。然果若之何而有禮邪？是故萬二千五百人爲軍，五百人爲旅也。當其命將出師之日，選士厲兵之時，無忽心，無惰氣，持重謹畏之恒存，不敢妄動，防範綱維之甚密。左之右之而部嚴明，節制足以壯三軍之膽；坐之起之而行
translation_en:
“Apply it to military affairs: because there is ritual propriety, military achievements are accomplished.”
Zhu Gun.
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, School Director: “The meaning of conducting military operations is expounded thoroughly. No essay in this examination section surpasses it.”
Comment by Examiner Yu, School Instructor: “The language flows smoothly and the reasoning is clear. The author has evidently devoted careful study to this Classic.”
Comment by Examiner Yang, School Director: “Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.”
When the conduct of military operations is governed by proper regulations, none under Heaven can withstand it. How momentous this is! If none under Heaven can withstand it, the accomplishment of military achievements is assured. Without proper regulation in conducting military operations, how could this be attained? In “Zhongni at Leisure,” Confucius discusses how ritual propriety is present everywhere. At this point, his meaning is that among the great affairs of a state, none is more consequential than warfare, and assured victory in battle depends on obtaining the proper Way.
A king receives the Mandate and becomes the Son of Heaven, succeeding to possession of all under Heaven. Should the Man and Yi peoples run rampant, he undertakes a campaign to carry out Heaven’s punishment; then his armies cannot but march forth. Should those who serve as the realm’s protective bulwarks rebel, he displays his divine might and launches a punitive expedition; then his armies cannot but be mobilized. But how, precisely, are they to possess ritual propriety?
Thus, twelve thousand five hundred men constitute an army, and five hundred a brigade. When commanders are appointed and troops dispatched, when soldiers are selected and weapons sharpened, there must be no careless thoughts or indolent spirits. Steadiness, caution, and reverence must constantly be maintained; none dare act rashly, and safeguards and structures of command must be exceedingly rigorous. Whether directed to the left or to the right, their units are strictly ordered [?], and their discipline suffices to embolden the Three Armies. Whether ordered to sit or to rise, their ranks …

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
整肅紀律足以奮六師之威出師有名不枉尺
以圖直尋之利殺人有禮不詭遇以要十禽之
功凡其金鼓旗物之用與夫攻圍擊刺之舉莫
不有禮如此吾知恃我之備乘彼之間以戰則
克以攻則取月羽一麾而渠魁授首向之猖獗
者于焉草薙而獸獮無復犯我邊陲矣星旗一
指而元惡就擒昔之跳梁者于焉魚散而鳥驚
無復干吾大憲矣獻俘執馘而沙漠爲之肅清
奏凱班師而疆埸爲之嘉靖在創業者以之則
===
===
有以成一統之盛在守成者以之則有以成中
興之美外患息而內變寧矣尚何武功之有不
成也哉抑論之兵凶器也戰危事也不得已而
後應之非聖人之所欲也蓋嘗求之易之師卦
自初六師出以律至於上六大君有命開國承
家小人勿用則一卦之間而出師駐師將兵將
將與夫奉辭伐罪旋師班賞之義無所不載王
者軍旅有禮而武功之成端不出此後世好大
喜功勤兵遠畧者不此之鑒而或至於敗衄不
punctuated:
整肅，紀律足以奮六師之威。出師有名，不枉尺以圖直尋之利；殺人有禮，不詭遇以要十禽之功。凡其金鼓旗物之用，與夫攻圍擊刺之舉，莫不有禮如此。吾知恃我之備，乘彼之間，以戰則克，以攻則取。月羽一麾，而渠魁授首，向之猖獗者，于焉草薙而獸獮，無復犯我邊陲矣；星旗一指，而元惡就擒，昔之跳梁者，于焉魚散而鳥驚，無復干吾大憲矣。獻俘執馘，而沙漠爲之肅清；奏凱班師，而疆埸爲之嘉靖。在創業者以之，則有以成一統之盛；在守成者以之，則有以成中興之美。外患息而內變寧矣，尚何武功之有不成也哉？

抑論之，兵，凶器也；戰，危事也。不得已而後應之，非聖人之所欲也。蓋嘗求之《易》之《師》卦，自初六「師出以律」，至於上六「大君有命，開國承家，小人勿用」，則一卦之間，而出師、駐師、將兵、將將，與夫奉辭伐罪、旋師班賞之義，無所不載。王者軍旅有禮，而武功之成，端不出此。後世好大喜功、勤兵遠畧者，不此之鑒，而或至於敗衄不
translation_en:
…orderly and disciplined, with regulations sufficient to rouse the might of the six armies. Troops are dispatched for a justifiable cause: one does not bend a foot to gain the advantage of straightening a fathom. Killing is governed by ritual propriety: one does not depart from the prescribed course of the hunt to secure the credit of taking ten animals. The use of gongs, drums, banners, and insignia, together with operations of attack, siege, striking, and thrusting, all observes ritual propriety in this way. I know that, relying on our preparedness and exploiting their openings, we shall prevail in battle and capture what we attack. At a single wave of the moon-and-feather standard [?], the ringleaders surrender their heads. Those who formerly ran rampant are cut down like grass and hunted down like beasts; no longer will they violate our frontiers. At a single pointing of the star-emblazoned banner, the chief malefactors are taken captive. Those who formerly defied authority scatter like fish and start like frightened birds; no longer will they transgress our great laws. Captives are presented and severed ears brought forward, and the desert is thereby cleared and pacified. Songs of victory sound as the army returns, and the frontier lands are brought to peace. When a founder of a dynasty employs these principles, he can achieve the grandeur of unification; when a ruler preserving an inherited realm employs them, he can achieve the glory of restoration. External troubles cease and internal disturbances are calmed. What military achievement could then remain unattained?

Yet, to consider the matter further: weapons are instruments of ill omen, and warfare is a perilous undertaking. One resorts to it only when there is no alternative; it is not what the sage desires. I have sought these principles in the Army hexagram of the Book of Changes. From the initial six, “The army sets forth under discipline,” to the top six, “The great ruler issues his command: establish states and inherit houses; petty men must not be employed,” this single hexagram contains all the principles of dispatching and encamping armies, commanding troops and commanding generals, proclaiming the sovereign’s charges and punishing offenders, and returning the army and distributing rewards. A true king’s observance of ritual propriety in military affairs, and the resulting accomplishment of martial achievements, lie entirely within these principles. Those in later ages who delighted in grandeur and coveted achievements, exhausting their troops on distant campaigns, failed to take this as their mirror; some consequently suffered defeat and could not…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
支亦獨何哉
第貳場
論
士以名節忠義爲本
朱衮
同考試官學正蔡批連日檢閱論場中非無作者
但多辭浮於理殊厭人觀晚得此卷辭氣高古議
論疊出讀之令人愕然名節忠義果自其胸中流出
也邪得士如此可以薦之
===
上矣
考試官教諭俞批議論切當文勢崢嶸全楚出色
之士
考試官學正楊批辭健而豐氣雄而正擢魁多士
允協輿情
士君子之身欲自立於天下則亦於其本
者先之而已夫天下之貴莫如士所貴乎
士者爲其有本也本得則士得本隳則士
亦隳矣然則士也者固可以徒爲邪士而
punctuated:
支，亦獨何哉？

第貳場
論
士以名節忠義爲本
朱衮

同考試官學正蔡批：連日檢閱論，場中非無作者，但多辭浮於理，殊厭人觀。晚得此卷，辭氣高古，議論疊出，讀之令人愕然。名節忠義，果自其胸中流出也邪？得士如此，可以薦之上矣。

考試官教諭俞批：議論切當，文勢崢嶸，全楚出色之士。

考試官學正楊批：辭健而豐，氣雄而正，擢魁多士，允協輿情。

士君子之身欲自立於天下，則亦於其本者先之而已。夫天下之貴莫如士，所貴乎士者，爲其有本也。本得則士得，本隳則士亦隳矣。然則士也者，固可以徒爲邪？士而
translation_en:
…unable to hold out—why indeed was this so?

Second Session
Discourse
Scholars Take Reputation, Integrity, Loyalty, and Righteousness as Their Foundation
By Zhu Gun

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, School Instructor: Over successive days of reviewing the discourses, I have found no lack of capable writers among the candidates. Yet their language generally exceeds their reasoning, making them decidedly tiresome to read. Late in the process I obtained this script: its diction and spirit are lofty and antique, and its arguments emerge one after another. Reading it leaves one astonished. Do reputation, integrity, loyalty, and righteousness truly flow from his own heart? Having found such a scholar, we may recommend him to His Majesty.

Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor: His arguments are apt and sound, and his prose has towering force. An outstanding scholar of all Chu.

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: His diction is vigorous and rich; his spirit is powerful and upright. To rank him first among the many scholars fully accords with the general judgment.

If a scholar and gentleman wishes to establish himself in the world, he must simply give priority to his foundation. Of those esteemed in the world, none ranks above the scholar. What makes the scholar worthy of esteem is that he has a foundation. When that foundation is secured, the scholar is secure; when it collapses, the scholar likewise collapses. Can one, then, merely be a scholar in name? A scholar who…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
徒為士之無用者也用之不濟則是自溺
於世有之不為補無之不為缺而尚足以
為貴哉蓋必有本之大焉而非士之至者
不能立也本者何也時而窮則名節為本
時而達則忠義為本名節忠義可相有而
不可相無者於此不之立而謂之士吾不
知也本之立有道焉其始也必貴有一定
之見見不定則功利異術易以攻之未免
得其似而失其真其終也必貴有一定之
===
守守不定則榮辱百端易以移之未免强
於常而渝於變始之不明終之不勇汎然
而議茫然而即卒然而罷汗漫恍忽無所
歸宿之地則亦何有於其身而何在於其
本邪吾獨愛夫古之人渾渾噩噩如標枝
野鹿然德之在天下者人皆有之人皆全
之士之名未命也名節忠義之事亦未彰
也迨夫皇降而帝帝降而王王降而下不
可知矣其俗於是大澆澆變而偸偸變而
punctuated: 徒為士之無用者也。用之不濟，則是自溺於世，有之不為補，無之不為缺，而尚足以為貴哉？蓋必有本之大焉，而非士之至者不能立也。本者何也？時而窮，則名節為本；時而達，則忠義為本。名節忠義，可相有而不可相無者。於此不之立而謂之士，吾不知也。本之立有道焉。其始也，必貴有一定之見。見不定，則功利異術易以攻之，未免得其似而失其真。其終也，必貴有一定之守。守不定，則榮辱百端易以移之，未免强於常而渝於變。始之不明，終之不勇，汎然而議，茫然而即，卒然而罷，汗漫恍忽，無所歸宿之地，則亦何有於其身，而何在於其本邪？吾獨愛夫古之人，渾渾噩噩，如標枝野鹿，然德之在天下者，人皆有之，人皆全之。士之名未命也，名節忠義之事亦未彰也。迨夫皇降而帝，帝降而王，王降而下，不可知矣。其俗於是大澆，澆變而偸，偸變而
translation_en:
…merely to be a scholar is to be a useless scholar. If, when employed, he accomplishes nothing, he merely submerges himself in the world: his presence adds nothing, and his absence leaves nothing lacking. Can he still deserve to be esteemed? There must surely be a great foundation, which only a scholar of the highest attainment can establish. What is this foundation? In straitened circumstances, reputation and integrity are the foundation; in a position of influence, loyalty and righteousness are the foundation. Reputation and integrity, loyalty and righteousness must coexist; neither pair can do without the other. If someone fails to establish himself in these yet is called a scholar, I cannot understand it.

There is a way to establish this foundation. At the outset, what matters is to have settled convictions. If one’s convictions are unsettled, the pursuit of achievement and profit and deviant teachings can readily assail them, so that one inevitably grasps the semblance and loses the reality. In the end, what matters is to have steadfast adherence to one’s principles. If that adherence is unsettled, honor and disgrace in their myriad forms can readily sway one, so that one inevitably stands firm in ordinary circumstances but falters amid change. Without clarity at the outset or courage at the end, one deliberates vaguely, undertakes things bewilderedly, and abandons them abruptly. Drifting and confused, with nowhere to find a settled resting place, what then does one possess within oneself, and where is one’s foundation?

I especially cherish the people of antiquity, in their simple, uncontrived wholeness, like branches high in the trees and deer in the wild. Yet the virtue present throughout the world was possessed by everyone and preserved intact by everyone. The designation “scholar” had not yet been bestowed, nor had deeds of reputation and integrity, loyalty and righteousness yet become conspicuous. When the age of the August Sovereigns declined into that of the Emperors, and that of the Emperors into that of the Kings, what followed the decline of the Kings is beyond reckoning. Customs then became profoundly corrupted; corruption turned into moral laxity, and moral laxity turned into…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
亂亂變而邪邪之習日成而人皆以正道
為諱是豈世道為之蓋士之自昧其志自
喪其守自鑿其情而又自滅裂其所學是
以初無以制之則患得之心勝而枉道求
進者有矣卒無以持之則患失之念動而
固寵欺君者有矣其於名節忠義之道不
亦澌盡矣乎是故有士之至者焉於是以
身先之方其窮也若無與也而達之本資
焉故毅然者固其守也浩然者直其氣也
===
道不可枉則紆金之榮不若仁義之良也
進不可求則軒冕之累不若泉石之雅也
涵養以大之泰山可頹滄海可變而吾之
名不可渝也勉强以堅之天地可臨鬼神
可質而吾之節不可奪也時則視天下之
事無有大於名節者及其出而在位則身
之本又有不同其寅亮者天下之工也其
經綸者天下之化也君不如堯□之使就
其如堯者去其不如堯者君不□□引之
punctuated: 亂，亂變而邪。邪之習日成，而人皆以正道為諱。是豈世道為之？蓋士之自昧其志，自喪其守，自鑿其情，而又自滅裂其所學。是以初無以制之，則患得之心勝，而枉道求進者有矣；卒無以持之，則患失之念動，而固寵欺君者有矣。其於名節忠義之道，不亦澌盡矣乎？是故有士之至者焉，於是以身先之。方其窮也，若無與也，而達之本資焉。故毅然者固其守也，浩然者直其氣也。道不可枉，則紆金之榮不若仁義之良也；進不可求，則軒冕之累不若泉石之雅也。涵養以大之，泰山可頹，滄海可變，而吾之名不可渝也；勉强以堅之，天地可臨，鬼神可質，而吾之節不可奪也。時則視天下之事，無有大於名節者。及其出而在位，則身之本又有不同。其寅亮者，天下之工也；其經綸者，天下之化也。君不如堯，□之使就其如堯者，去其不如堯者；君不□□，引之
translation_en:
…disorder, and disorder turns into depravity. Depraved habits take firmer hold each day, and everyone treats the correct Way as something taboo. Is this really the doing of the temper of the age? Rather, scholars themselves obscure their aspirations, abandon their principles, distort their true feelings, and further rend and ruin what they have learned. Thus, lacking the means to restrain themselves at the outset, they are overcome by anxiety about obtaining office, and some bend the Way to seek advancement. Lacking the means to hold firm in the end, they are stirred by anxiety about losing office, and some secure their favor by deceiving their ruler. Have they not utterly exhausted the Way of reputation, integrity, loyalty, and righteousness?

Therefore, there are scholars of the highest attainment who take the lead through their own conduct. While they remain obscure, they seem to have no part in public affairs; yet the foundation for their later success in office is laid here. Their resoluteness makes their principles firm; their expansive moral energy makes their vital force upright. Since the Way must not be bent, the glory of wearing a gold seal is inferior to the goodness of benevolence and righteousness. Since advancement must not be sought, the burdens of carriage and ceremonial cap are inferior to the refinement of springs and rocks. Through nurture and cultivation they enlarge this resolve: Mount Tai may crumble and the vast sea may change, but my good name cannot be altered. Through strenuous effort they strengthen it: Heaven and Earth may look down upon me, and spirits may be called upon as witnesses, but my integrity cannot be wrested from me. At this time, they regard nothing in the world as greater than reputation and integrity.

Once they come forward and hold office, however, the foundation of their personal conduct takes a different form. What they respectfully assist is the work of all under Heaven; what they order and administer is the transformation of all under Heaven. If the ruler does not measure up to Yao, they [illegible: guide him?] toward those qualities in which he resembles Yao and eliminate those in which he does not. If the ruler does not [two illegible characters], they guide him …

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
使就其如舜者去其不如舜者道苟在焉
則裾可引榻可叩檻可折而君不可欺也
道苟非焉則履可納冠可掛綬可解而寵
不可固也時則視天下之事無有大於忠
義者夫以所居之不同而所立之德亦異
則時與道二者而已道如是而時如是士
則以道從時道如是而時不如是士則以
時從道道固無異也而時則變耳雖然天
下未有外名節而可以爲忠義者亦豈有
===
無忠義而能以先名節者哉何也天下之
事制之在始始不可制不可要其終窮也
者達之始也始以是存之終以是措之故
發而爲文章之潤身推而爲政事之及物
者皆其本之餘事也然外此士固有不同
者華言華服繩趨尺步問其業顓顓然問
其威儀賔賔然問其行萎萎然者偽也內
之不足以理身外之不足以行於人剽竊
形似悻悻然詭遇以爲榮者利也旅逐旅
punctuated:
使就其如舜者，去其不如舜者。道苟在焉，則裾可引，榻可叩，檻可折，而君不可欺也。道苟非焉，則履可納，冠可掛，綬可解，而寵不可固也。時則視天下之事，無有大於忠義者。夫以所居之不同，而所立之德亦異，則時與道二者而已。道如是而時如是，士則以道從時；道如是而時不如是，士則以時從道。道固無異也，而時則變耳。雖然，天下未有外名節而可以爲忠義者，亦豈有無忠義而能以先名節者哉？何也？天下之事，制之在始；始不可制，不可要其終。窮也者，達之始也。始以是存之，終以是措之。故發而爲文章之潤身，推而爲政事之及物者，皆其本之餘事也。
然外此，士固有不同者。華言華服，繩趨尺步，問其業，顓顓然；問其威儀，賔賔然；問其行，萎萎然者，偽也。內之不足以理身，外之不足以行於人，剽竊形似，悻悻然詭遇以爲榮者，利也。旅逐旅
translation_en:
…lead him toward those qualities in which he resembles Shun and remove those in which he does not. If the Way is at stake, one may tug at the ruler’s robe, strike his couch, or break his balustrade in remonstrance, but one must not deceive him. If the Way is violated, one may put on one’s shoes to depart, hang up one’s official cap, or untie one’s seal ribbon, but one must not cling to imperial favor. At such a time, one regards nothing in the world as greater than loyalty and righteousness. That the virtues one establishes differ according to the position one occupies comes down to just two things: circumstances and the Way. When the Way is thus and circumstances accord with it, the scholar follows the times in accordance with the Way; when the Way is thus but circumstances do not accord with it, the scholar makes circumstances conform to the Way. The Way itself does not differ; only circumstances change. Nevertheless, no one in the world can practice loyalty and righteousness apart from reputation and integrity. How, then, could anyone without loyalty and righteousness give precedence to reputation and integrity? Why is this? The affairs of the world must be directed at their beginning. If their beginning cannot be directed, their outcome cannot be assured. Obscurity is the beginning of eminence. What one preserves within oneself at the outset is what one puts into practice at the end. Thus, whether it finds expression in literary compositions that adorn one’s person or extends into governmental affairs that benefit others, all this is merely the further effect of that foundation.
Yet outside this there are indeed other sorts of scholars. Florid in speech and splendid in dress, they move as though measured by line and rule. Inquire into their studies, and they appear earnestly absorbed; inquire into their deportment, and they appear polished; inquire into their conduct, and they prove feeble. This is hypocrisy. Inwardly unable to order themselves, outwardly unable to conduct themselves among others, they plagiarize outward forms and, with self-righteous insistence, seek glory through crooked means. This is the pursuit of gain. In groups they chase after advancement, in groups…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
進侈然以自饜舉平生所學如弁髦而盡
棄之者惑也若乃耳目司之股肱任之營
營焉惟所私硜硜焉無所建明而上負其
君下負其學者賊也之數者其於名節忠
義之在我者何如其於所以謂之士者何
如而顧以是自置其身於蕩然之地哉然
此亦有其故矣固非士之得已也蓋君上
之趨向士習之權輿君不能作養而濯磨
之則士亦孰肯自重而不愛市其欲於君
===
乎夫士固有無所待而興者然爲人上者
何可無道以風厲之故庠序學校所以養
其身詩書禮樂所以陶其性禮義廉耻所
以張其維而見於進黜予奪抑揚好惡之
間者又皆出於人心之同然而不涉於毀
譽愛憎之私恬退者必進而奔競者弭矣
鯁直者必容而諂媚者退矣廉介者必揚
而貪墨者懼矣然後天下之士皆奮然以
行檢自勵曉然以得齒於士君子之行爲
punctuated: 進，侈然以自饜，舉平生所學如弁髦而盡棄之者，惑也。若乃耳目司之，股肱任之，營營焉惟所私，硜硜焉無所建明，而上負其君，下負其學者，賊也。之數者，其於名節忠義之在我者何如？其於所以謂之士者何如？而顧以是自置其身於蕩然之地哉？然此亦有其故矣，固非士之得已也。蓋君上之趨向，士習之權輿。君不能作養而濯磨之，則士亦孰肯自重而不愛市其欲於君乎？夫士固有無所待而興者，然爲人上者何可無道以風厲之？故庠序學校所以養其身，詩書禮樂所以陶其性，禮義廉耻所以張其維，而見於進黜予奪抑揚好惡之間者，又皆出於人心之同然，而不涉於毀譽愛憎之私。恬退者必進，而奔競者弭矣；鯁直者必容，而諂媚者退矣；廉介者必揚，而貪墨者懼矣。然後天下之士皆奮然以行檢自勵，曉然以得齒於士君子之行爲
translation_en: … advancing, extravagantly indulging themselves, and casting aside everything they have learned throughout their lives as though it were a discarded ceremonial cap or childhood forelocks—such men are deluded. As for those entrusted with the duties of eyes and ears and charged with the responsibilities of arms and legs, yet who busily pursue only their private interests, stubbornly offer no constructive counsel, and thus betray their ruler above and their learning below—such men are pernicious. These several types [?]—how do they measure up to the reputation, integrity, loyalty, and righteousness that should reside within us? How do they measure up to what makes a man worthy of being called a scholar? Yet would they thereby place themselves beyond all moral bounds? There are reasons for this, however; it is surely not entirely within scholars’ power to avoid it. For the ruler’s inclinations are the starting point of scholars’ habits. If the ruler cannot nurture and refine them, who among the scholars will be willing to value himself and refrain from bartering with the ruler to satisfy his desires [?]? Certainly, some scholars rise to virtue without awaiting encouragement. Yet how can those who rule others lack ways to inspire and exhort them? Thus, schools provide for their persons; the Odes, Documents, rites, and music cultivate their natures; and ritual propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame uphold their moral bonds. What is manifested in advancement and dismissal, bestowal and withdrawal, discouragement and encouragement, approval and disapproval must likewise proceed entirely from what human hearts commonly recognize as right, without involving private bias in disparagement or praise, affection or hatred. When the quiet and retiring are assured of advancement, those who scramble for preferment will desist. When the forthright are assured of acceptance, flatterers will withdraw. When the incorruptible and principled are assured of recognition, the corrupt and avaricious will be afraid. Only then will scholars throughout the realm vigorously spur themselves to disciplined conduct and clearly regard being counted among the ranks of scholarly gentlemen as …

text:
□見其所見守其所守而所謂名節忠義
皆相忘於無何有之鄉也夫是之謂士之
全者是故其道在乎上之人也謹論

===
