translation_en:
…[illegible] see what they see and hold fast to what they uphold; and what are called reputation, integrity, loyalty, and righteousness are all forgotten together in the realm of Nothing Whatever. This is what is meant by a fully realized scholar. Thus, the means of bringing this about rests with those above. Respectfully submitted as a discourse.

Memorial
A memorial of thanks composed in the person of Han Qi upon his appointment by the Song court as Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi
Zhang Zhongling

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: It conveys well the Duke of Wei’s devotion to his sovereign and love of his country.
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: Classical and well regulated, yet omitting none of the historical precedents and allusions; it amply demonstrates broad learning.
Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: The wording forms a seamless whole, without the slightest trace of patchwork. He is indeed skilled in four-and-six parallel prose.
Examiner Yang, School Director, comments: A fine memorial.

I humbly submit: To govern a region and raise the command banner is to be entrusted with the lands west of Shan; to secure the frontier and receive the battle-axe is to exercise sole authority beyond the military threshold. The office commands soldiers and civilians alike; its duties encompass both civil and military affairs. Considering the weight of this regional military command, it surely calls for a worthy man capable of ordering the state. Who could have imagined that one so ordinary and mediocre would mistakenly receive this appointment!

I reflect that I, your servant Qi, possess neither courage nor wisdom, and am not yet mature in years and judgment. I have always cherished simple loyalty, and have fortunately…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
叨科甲臚傳適彩雲之瑞史占表捧日之
誠天假微臣受知
明主小官二轉遂歷清階司諫三年復兼詞掖
籌邊無定策慚非李迪之明使蜀甫成功
又更梁顥之職捫心知感揣分奚堪兹蓋
伏遇
〇〇〇〇
堯德安安
文心翼翼
===
恭儉出乎天性
仁愛浹于民心
躬大禹之克艱開天章而日旰乃食
邁高宗之時敏御
經筵而盛暑弗停睦族之
恩弘敷求言之
詔屢下財以不蓄爲富刑以不殺爲威
信及豚魚
誠孚夷狄凡居覆載悉荷生成蠢兹元昊之
punctuated: 叨科甲，臚傳適彩雲之瑞，史占表捧日之誠。天假微臣受知明主，小官二轉，遂歷清階；司諫三年，復兼詞掖。籌邊無定策，慚非李迪之明；使蜀甫成功，又更梁顥之職。捫心知感，揣分奚堪！兹蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，堯德安安，文心翼翼，恭儉出乎天性，仁愛浹于民心。躬大禹之克艱，開天章而日旰乃食；邁高宗之時敏，御經筵而盛暑弗停。睦族之恩弘敷，求言之詔屢下。財以不蓄爲富，刑以不殺爲威。信及豚魚，誠孚夷狄。凡居覆載，悉荷生成。蠢兹元昊之
translation_en:
…I was undeservedly admitted among those successful in the examinations. When the names were ceremonially announced, auspicious colored clouds appeared; the court historian’s prognostication revealed my sincerity in upholding the sun—that is, the sovereign. Heaven granted your humble servant recognition by an enlightened ruler. After two promotions in minor offices, I advanced through posts of distinction; after three years as Remonstrator, I also served in the imperial drafting offices. In planning frontier defense, I had no settled strategy, and was ashamed to lack Li Di’s discernment. My mission to Shu had barely been accomplished when I was transferred to the office once held by Liang Hao. Searching my heart, I know my gratitude; measuring my abilities, how could I be equal to the charge?

This, indeed, is because I have humbly encountered [〇〇〇〇: four circle marks in the text], whose virtue, like Yao’s, is naturally at ease, and whose heart, like King Wen’s, is reverent and vigilant. Your respectfulness and frugality spring from your heavenly nature; your benevolence and love permeate the people’s hearts. You personally embody Great Yu’s diligence in undertaking difficult tasks: you open the Tianzhang Pavilion and do not eat until late in the day. You surpass King Gaozong in constant diligence: you attend the Classics Colloquium without interruption even in the height of summer. Your favor promoting harmony among imperial kinsmen is widely extended; your edicts soliciting counsel are repeatedly issued. In finances, you regard refraining from hoarding as wealth; in punishments, you regard refraining from killing as authority. Your trustworthiness reaches even pigs and fish; your sincerity wins the confidence of the Yi and Di peoples. All who dwell beneath Heaven and upon Earth receive your bounty, which brings them into being and nurtures them. This unruly Yuanhao’s…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
小羌蕞爾繼遷之遺孽犬羊其性梟獍爲
心錦繡忘
恩衣冠僭號異圖潛蓄賴曹瑋之先知大亂敢
行偶劉平之敗衂螳螂奮臂雖彼勢之無
成豺虎磨牙奈吾民之受毒我
皇上赫發徂征之怒大興薄伐之師爰
命儒臣出撫邊鎮臣今受
命而往拜
表即行敢竭庸愚用圖報稱皷戎行而戮力
===
進分五路之兵偕僚佐以同謀務出萬全
之計先招吐蕃以爲掎角之勢次收靈夏
以爲興復之基直搗賀蘭山願縛單于於
萬里大蒐地斤澤期克鬼方於三年坐收
中國之舊疆丕振
皇朝之新化伏願
道大而不自以爲大益嚴至儆於無虞
功高而不自以爲高必致太平於有象九夷
八蠻通道永全四海之金甌群黎百姓歸
punctuated: 小羌，蕞爾繼遷之遺孽，犬羊其性，梟獍爲心，錦繡忘恩，衣冠僭號。異圖潛蓄，賴曹瑋之先知；大亂敢行，偶劉平之敗衂。螳螂奮臂，雖彼勢之無成；豺虎磨牙，奈吾民之受毒。我皇上赫發徂征之怒，大興薄伐之師，爰命儒臣出撫邊鎮。臣今受命而往，拜表即行，敢竭庸愚，用圖報稱。皷戎行而戮力，進分五路之兵；偕僚佐以同謀，務出萬全之計。先招吐蕃，以爲掎角之勢；次收靈夏，以爲興復之基。直搗賀蘭山，願縛單于於萬里；大蒐地斤澤，期克鬼方於三年。坐收中國之舊疆，丕振皇朝之新化。伏願道大而不自以爲大，益嚴至儆於無虞；功高而不自以爲高，必致太平於有象。九夷八蠻通道，永全四海之金甌；群黎百姓歸
translation_en: …that petty Qiang, the paltry surviving scion of Jiqian, has the nature of dogs and sheep and the heart of the owl and jing-beast, which devour their own parents. Clad in brocades, he forgets imperial kindness; wearing ceremonial robes and headgear, he usurps a sovereign title. He secretly harbored rebellious designs, which Cao Wei fortunately foresaw; he dared launch a great rebellion when Liu Ping happened to suffer defeat. Though his forces can accomplish nothing, like a mantis brandishing its forelegs, what are we to do about the suffering inflicted on our people as these jackals and tigers grind their teeth? Our August Sovereign, blazing with wrath, has resolved upon a punitive expedition and raised a great army to chastise him. He has therefore commanded a scholarly official to go forth and pacify the frontier garrisons. Your servant now proceeds under this command: I respectfully submit this memorial and immediately depart, venturing to exhaust my mediocre abilities in the hope of adequately repaying imperial favor. I shall rouse the ranks to united exertion and advance with troops divided among five routes. Together with my colleagues and assistants, I shall deliberate, striving to devise a plan that ensures complete success. First I shall win over the Tufan to establish a mutually supporting military position; next I shall recover Ling and Xia as a foundation for restoration. Striking directly at Helan Shan, I hope to bind the chanyu ten thousand li away; conducting a great military sweep at Dijin Ze, I expect to conquer the Guifang within three years. Thus shall we readily recover the former territories of the Central Realm and greatly extend the renewing influence of our august dynasty. I humbly pray that, though Your Way is great, You will not deem Yourself great, but maintain still stricter vigilance even when no danger is apparent; and that, though Your achievements are lofty, You will not deem Yourself lofty, but bring about a Great Peace manifest in tangible signs. May the Nine Yi and Eight Man open their routes to us, preserving forever the golden vessel of the realm within the Four Seas; and may the common people turn…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
心長保萬年之玉燭臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策五道
第一問
===
蘇純
同考試官教諭易批發揮
聖制與六經貫通畧無滲漏足見博洽之學也
同考試官學正潘批五策皆才思優裕此篇尤條答
詳明錄之
考試官教諭俞批
聖聖相傳古今一道此作得之
考試官學正楊批善敷揚我
朝制作之盛
punctuated:
心，長保萬年之玉燭。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叄場
策五道
第一問

蘇純

同考試官教諭易批：發揮聖制，與六經貫通，畧無滲漏，足見博洽之學也。

同考試官學正潘批：五策皆才思優裕，此篇尤條答詳明，錄之。

考試官教諭俞批：聖聖相傳，古今一道，此作得之。

考試官學正楊批：善敷揚我朝制作之盛。
translation_en:
…give their allegiance, forever preserving the harmonious order of the seasons for ten thousand years. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, is overwhelmed with fervent emotion and reverent trepidation. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question

Su Chun

Comment by Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor (jiaoyu): He expounds the imperial writings and connects them thoroughly with the Six Classics, without the slightest omission. This amply demonstrates his broad and comprehensive learning.

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor (xuezheng): All five policy essays display abundant talent and ideas. This piece is especially detailed and clear in answering each point. Select it for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor (jiaoyu): Transmitted from sage to sage, the Way is one throughout antiquity and the present. This composition grasps it.

Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor (xuezheng): He ably expounds the splendor of our dynasty’s institutions and writings.

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
聖人之治天下也本於道而其傳諸後
也託於書蓋道者治之本書者道之寓道
見於治則其澤被於當時道傳於書則其
澤及於萬世此古聖人之六經與我
朝
列聖之制作無非斯道之所寓同一為治之迹
也請復明問一氣未分斯道寓於太極兩
儀攸位斯道具於聖人聖人以一身體天
地之道以斯道治天下之民羲農之所以
===
皇天下者斯道也堯舜之所以帝天下者
斯道也禹湯文武之所以王天下者亦斯
道也先聖後聖授受一道夫豈别有所謂
道哉原於帝降之衷根於烝民之彝見於
日用事物之間其體仁義禮智其倫君臣
父子昆弟夫婦朋友其用禮樂刑政斯道
之在天下曷嘗一日亡哉惟其傳於人者
或絶或續故其行於世者有明有晦使天
下常有聖人則斯道以行而天下自治矣
punctuated: 聖人之治天下也，本於道；而其傳諸後也，託於書。蓋道者，治之本；書者，道之寓。道見於治，則其澤被於當時；道傳於書，則其澤及於萬世。此古聖人之六經與我朝列聖之制作，無非斯道之所寓，同一為治之迹也。請復明問：一氣未分，斯道寓於太極；兩儀攸位，斯道具於聖人。聖人以一身體天地之道，以斯道治天下之民。羲農之所以皇天下者，斯道也；堯舜之所以帝天下者，斯道也；禹湯文武之所以王天下者，亦斯道也。先聖後聖，授受一道，夫豈别有所謂道哉？原於帝降之衷，根於烝民之彝，見於日用事物之間，其體仁義禮智，其倫君臣、父子、昆弟、夫婦、朋友，其用禮樂刑政。斯道之在天下，曷嘗一日亡哉？惟其傳於人者，或絶或續，故其行於世者，有明有晦。使天下常有聖人，則斯道以行，而天下自治矣。
translation_en: The sages’ governance of all under Heaven is rooted in the Way, while its transmission to later generations is entrusted to writings. For the Way is the foundation of governance, and writings are the repository of the Way. When the Way is manifested in governance, its blessings reach the people of that age; when the Way is transmitted through writings, its blessings extend to ten thousand generations. Thus the Six Classics of the ancient sages and the institutions and writings of the successive sage rulers of our dynasty are all repositories of this Way, alike recording its realization in governance. Allow me to respond to your discerning question: before the single vital force divided, this Way resided in the Supreme Ultimate; when the two primal powers, Heaven and Earth, took their places, this Way was fully embodied in the sages. The sages personally embodied the Way of Heaven and Earth and used this Way to govern the people of all under Heaven. It was through this Way that Fuxi and Shennong ruled all under Heaven as august sovereigns; through this Way that Yao and Shun ruled as emperors; and likewise through this Way that Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu ruled as kings. Earlier and later sages handed down and received one and the same Way. How could there be some other thing called the Way? It originates in the moral nature bestowed by the Lord on High, is rooted in the constant norms of the people, and manifests itself amid everyday affairs and things. Its substance is benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom; its relationships are those between ruler and minister, father and son, elder and younger brothers, husband and wife, and friends; its applications are rites, music, punishments, and administration. Has this Way ever been absent from the world for even a single day? Yet its transmission among people is sometimes broken and sometimes sustained, and consequently its practice in the world is sometimes manifest and sometimes obscure. If there were always sages in the world, this Way would prevail, and all under Heaven would naturally be well governed.

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
柰何曰不常午聖人不常出使六經不作
則道何從而明天下何由而治哉噫此六
經所以不得不作也是故易以道陰陽則
凡羲文之卦爻周孔之彖象無非天道人
事之消長吉凶欲人知所以趨避也書以
道政事則凡虞夏之典謨商周之訓誥無
非脩齊治平之大經大法欲人知所以嚮
順也詩以理性情其言善惡於三百篇之
中蓋欲使人知吟詠得其性情之正而已
===
春秋以正名分其寓褒貶於一字之間蓋
欲世之亂賊禁其人欲之肆而已以至禮
以謹節文所謂安上治民者於是樂以和
民心所謂移風易俗者於是六經一出斯
道大明出治者有所取則趨治者有所依
歸倫理以正恩義以篤而天下賴以治矣
故曰六經者聖人爲治之迹也千聖一心
萬古一理洪惟我
朝
punctuated: 柰何曰不常午，聖人不常出，使六經不作，則道何從而明，天下何由而治哉？噫！此六經所以不得不作也。是故易以道陰陽，則凡羲文之卦爻、周孔之彖象，無非天道人事之消長吉凶，欲人知所以趨避也。書以道政事，則凡虞夏之典謨、商周之訓誥，無非脩齊治平之大經大法，欲人知所以嚮順也。詩以理性情，其言善惡於三百篇之中，蓋欲使人知吟詠，得其性情之正而已。春秋以正名分，其寓褒貶於一字之間，蓋欲世之亂賊禁其人欲之肆而已。以至禮以謹節文，所謂安上治民者於是；樂以和民心，所謂移風易俗者於是。六經一出，斯道大明，出治者有所取則，趨治者有所依歸，倫理以正，恩義以篤，而天下賴以治矣。故曰：「六經者，聖人爲治之迹也。」千聖一心，萬古一理。洪惟我朝
translation_en: Yet alas, the sun does not always stand at noon [?], and sages do not always appear. If the Six Classics had not been composed, how could the Way have been made clear, and how could the world have been brought to order? Ah! This is why the Six Classics had to be composed. Thus the Book of Changes explains yin and yang: the hexagrams and their lines associated with Fu Xi and King Wen, and the judgments and images associated with the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, all concern waxing and waning, good fortune and misfortune, in the Way of Heaven and human affairs. Their purpose is to teach people what to pursue and what to avoid. The Book of Documents explains affairs of government: the canons and counsels of Yu and Xia, and the instructions and proclamations of Shang and Zhou, are all fundamental principles and great rules for cultivating oneself, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world. Their purpose is to teach people what to follow and obey. The Book of Odes regulates human nature and feelings. Its treatment of good and evil within its three hundred poems is intended simply to teach people, through chanting and singing, to attain correctness in their nature and feelings. The Spring and Autumn Annals rectifies titles and distinctions of status. Its lodging of praise and blame within a single word is intended simply to make rebels and traitors in the world restrain their unbridled human desires. Furthermore, the Book of Rites ensures care in ceremonial forms and observances: herein lies what is called securing those above and governing the people. The Book of Music harmonizes the people's hearts: herein lies what is called transforming prevailing customs and practices. Once the Six Classics appeared, this Way became fully manifest. Those administering government had standards to follow, and those seeking good order had something on which to rely and to which to turn. Ethical relationships were thereby rectified, kindness and righteousness deepened, and the world depended on these for its good order. Hence it is said: “The Six Classics are the traces of the sages' work of government.” A thousand sages share one mind; through all ages there is one principle. In reverent contemplation of our great dynasty…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏輯寧邦家欲天下臣民
之向善去惡也萬幾之暇條成
大誥三編自是
聖聖相承皆有作述
太宗文皇帝欲天下臣民之爲善爲孝也編輯
爲善陰隲
孝順事實二書
宣宗章皇帝欲天下臣民盡人倫之道則有
五倫書之頒
===
===
英宗睿皇帝欲天下臣民歸一統之治則有
一統志之作
憲宗純皇帝欲天下臣民知古今治亂之機人
才進退之道風俗盛衰之由廼
命儒臣續編資治通鑑綱目
聖祖
神宗
宸章浩瀚如天地之覆幬無外
睿藻輝煌如日月之照臨不遺萬邦至寶億
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝肇造區夏，輯寧邦家，欲天下臣民之向善去惡也，萬幾之暇，條成《大誥》三編。自是聖聖相承，皆有作述。太宗文皇帝欲天下臣民之爲善爲孝也，編輯《爲善陰隲》《孝順事實》二書。宣宗章皇帝欲天下臣民盡人倫之道，則有《五倫書》之頒。英宗睿皇帝欲天下臣民歸一統之治，則有《一統志》之作。憲宗純皇帝欲天下臣民知古今治亂之機、人才進退之道、風俗盛衰之由，廼命儒臣續編《資治通鑑綱目》。聖祖神宗，宸章浩瀚，如天地之覆幬無外；睿藻輝煌，如日月之照臨不遺。萬邦至寶，億
translation_en: …Taizu, the Gao Emperor, founded the realm and brought peace to the state. Wishing the officials and people throughout the empire to turn toward good and abandon evil, he used the intervals between his myriad duties to compile the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) in three collections. Thereafter, sage sovereign succeeded sage sovereign, each producing writings and compilations. Taizong, the Wen Emperor, wishing the officials and people throughout the empire to practice goodness and filial piety, compiled the two books Hidden Blessings for Good Deeds (Weishan Yinzhi) and True Accounts of Filial Conduct (Xiaoshun Shishi). Xuanzong, the Zhang Emperor, wishing the officials and people throughout the empire to fulfill the way of human relationships, promulgated the Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun Shu). Yingzong, the Rui Emperor, wishing the officials and people throughout the empire to come under unified rule, had the Gazetteer of the Unified Realm (Yitong Zhi) produced. Xianzong, the Chun Emperor, wishing the officials and people throughout the empire to understand the factors underlying order and disorder past and present, the principles governing the advancement and dismissal of talented men, and the reasons for the flourishing and decline of customs, commanded his Confucian officials to compile a continuation of the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government (Zizhi Tongjian Gangmu). The imperial writings of these sage ancestors and divine forebears are vast, like Heaven and Earth, whose shelter and support exclude nothing; their brilliant compositions shine like the sun and moon, whose illumination leaves nothing untouched. They are the supreme treasure of the myriad states, and for countless…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
世成規化理天下之道豈復有加於此誠
與古聖人之六經脗合無間同一爲治之
迹也然其所以脗合無間者豈無證哉觀
大誥申明五常之諭即易之家人父子子
兄兄弟弟夫夫婦婦而家道正也君臣同
遊之言即書之元首明哉股肱良哉者也
爲善陰隲其與易之積善餘慶書之作善降
祥夫何殊
孝順事實其與書之克諧以孝詩之永言孝
===
思夫奚異
五倫書所以明人倫非即書之五典乎
一統志所以載輿圖非即書之禹貢乎
續編資治通鑑綱目又非春秋之筆削乎世
有古今而道無古今聖有先後而道無先
後方今我
皇上以天縱之資嗣
祖宗之緒孳孳圖治夙夜靡遑
聖不自至而日御乎
punctuated:
世成規，化理天下之道，豈復有加於此？誠與古聖人之六經脗合無間，同一爲治之迹也。然其所以脗合無間者，豈無證哉？觀《大誥》申明五常之諭，即《易》之《家人》「父子子，兄兄弟弟，夫夫婦婦，而家道正」也。「君臣同遊」之言，即《書》之「元首明哉，股肱良哉」者也。《爲善陰隲》，其與《易》之「積善餘慶」、《書》之「作善降祥」，夫何殊？《孝順事實》，其與《書》之「克諧以孝」、《詩》之「永言孝思」，夫奚異？《五倫書》所以明人倫，非即《書》之五典乎？《一統志》所以載輿圖，非即《書》之《禹貢》乎？《續編資治通鑑綱目》，又非《春秋》之筆削乎？世有古今，而道無古今；聖有先後，而道無先後。
方今我皇上以天縱之資，嗣祖宗之緒，孳孳圖治，夙夜靡遑。聖不自至，而日御乎
translation_en:
…a model for generations. Could anything surpass this way of transforming and governing all under Heaven? It accords perfectly with the Six Classics of the ancient sages, following the very same path of government. Yet is there no evidence of this perfect accord? Consider the injunction in the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) elucidating the Five Constant Virtues: it is precisely what the Changes says in the hexagram The Family: “When fathers [act as fathers?], sons as sons, elder brothers as elder brothers, younger brothers as younger brothers, husbands as husbands, and wives as wives, the way of the family is set right.” The words “ruler and ministers journey together” are precisely what the Documents expresses in “The head is enlightened; the limbs are good.” How does Doing Good and Hidden Recompense (Wei Shan Yin Zhi) differ from the Changes’ “Accumulated goodness brings blessings in abundance” or the Documents’ “On those who do good, blessings descend”? How does Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun Shishi) differ from the Documents’ “He was able to bring harmony through filial devotion” or the Odes’ “Ever cherish filial thoughts”? The Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun Shu) elucidates human relationships: is this not precisely the Documents’ five constant norms? The Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Unified Realm (Yitong Zhi) records the geography of the realm: is this not precisely the Documents’ Tribute of Yu? And is the Continuation of the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government (Xu Bian Zizhi Tongjian Gangmu) not likewise an exercise of the Spring and Autumn Annals’ discriminating inclusion and omission? Ages may be ancient or modern, but the Way is neither ancient nor modern; sages may come earlier or later, but the Way is neither earlier nor later.
Today our Emperor, endowed by Heaven, carries on the legacy of his ancestors. He diligently seeks good government, allowing himself no respite from dawn until night. Sagehood does not come of itself [?], and each day he attends…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
經筵治不自足而時講夫治道凡所以稱制
臨决訓飭臣民無非有得六經之旨申明
祖宗之制而已由是詩書之澤漸涵於中外道
德之化覃被於邇遐會極歸極者熈熈乎
春臺玉燭之中遵義遵道者皞皞乎光天
化日之下普天率土莫不歸心華夏蠻貊
罔不仰德自生民以來未有盛於
今日也執事乃欲諸生明揚以對於乎泰山
之高不可以丈尺計滄海之深不可以斗
===
斛量我
朝
列聖治化之盛天之高也地之厚也豈區區膚
見陋識所能形容其萬一哉惟進教之幸
甚
第二問
曾得祿
同考試官教諭蔣 批忠孝一策士子多演問目此篇
條答無遺其積學待問者歟
punctuated:
經筵，治不自足而時講夫治道。凡所以稱制臨决、訓飭臣民，無非有得六經之旨、申明祖宗之制而已。由是詩書之澤漸涵於中外，道德之化覃被於邇遐。會極歸極者，熈熈乎春臺玉燭之中；遵義遵道者，皞皞乎光天化日之下。普天率土，莫不歸心；華夏蠻貊，罔不仰德。自生民以來，未有盛於今日也。執事乃欲諸生明揚以對。於乎！泰山之高，不可以丈尺計；滄海之深，不可以斗斛量。我朝列聖治化之盛，天之高也，地之厚也，豈區區膚見陋識所能形容其萬一哉？惟進教之幸甚。
第二問
曾得祿
同考試官教諭蔣批：忠孝一策，士子多演問目，此篇條答無遺，其積學待問者歟？
translation_en:
…the Classics Colloquium; never content with his achievements in government, he regularly discusses the Way of governing. Whenever he exercises sovereign authority and renders decisions, or instructs and admonishes officials and people, he does nothing other than draw upon the purport of the Six Classics and reaffirm the institutions of his ancestors. Thus the beneficent influence of the Odes and Documents permeates the capital and the provinces, while moral transformation extends to places near and far. Those who assemble at and turn toward the supreme standard rejoice as though upon a terrace in spring, amid the harmonious radiance of the seasons; those who follow righteousness and the Way live in expansive contentment beneath a bright heaven and the sun of transforming virtue. Throughout all lands beneath heaven, none fails to give heartfelt allegiance; among the peoples of Huaxia and the Man and Mo, none fails to look up to his virtue. Since humankind first existed, there has never been prosperity greater than that of today. Yet you, honored examiners, wish us students to proclaim it clearly in our replies. Ah! The height of Mount Tai cannot be reckoned in feet and inches; the depth of the vast sea cannot be measured in pecks and bushels. The flourishing government and transforming influence of the succession of sage sovereigns of our dynasty are as lofty as heaven and as profound as the earth. How could my meager, superficial views and limited knowledge describe even one ten-thousandth of them? I would count it a great good fortune to receive your further instruction.
Second Question
Zeng Delu
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: On this policy question concerning loyalty and filial piety, most candidates merely elaborate upon the wording of the question. This essay answers point by point, omitting nothing. Is its author not one who has accumulated learning in readiness for questioning?

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭張批於人倫難處之際能權低昂而
善處如此足見擇理之精
考試官教諭俞批答之詳處之當其學於忠與孝
者乎
考試官學正楊批有考據知適從可嘉可嘉
天下莫難成者仁莫難取者義義精仁熟
而天下無難處之事矣何謂仁當理而無
私心之謂仁何謂義行而宜之之謂義仁
義人心之所固有也而以為難者則以其
===
氣禀拘之物欲蔽之曠其心而不求舍其
路而不由由是視之殆若登天之難矣有
志於學者擇善以明之克己以復之日愈
新月愈盛吾義既精吾仁既熟權度在我
而精切不差由是遇君則為忠遇親則為
孝吾之處常固各盡其道而處變亦不失
其常矣往事難處有如趙苞職守君城而
母為虜執當此之時守城棄母不可也從
母棄城不可也苞也始為君戰而棄其母
punctuated:
同考試官教諭張批：於人倫難處之際，能權低昂而善處如此，足見擇理之精。
考試官教諭俞批：答之詳，處之當，其學於忠與孝者乎？
考試官學正楊批：有考據，知適從，可嘉可嘉。
天下莫難成者仁，莫難取者義。義精仁熟，而天下無難處之事矣。何謂仁？當理而無私心之謂仁。何謂義？行而宜之之謂義。仁義，人心之所固有也，而以為難者，則以其氣禀拘之，物欲蔽之，曠其心而不求，舍其路而不由，由是視之，殆若登天之難矣。有志於學者，擇善以明之，克己以復之，日愈新，月愈盛。吾義既精，吾仁既熟，權度在我，而精切不差。由是遇君則為忠，遇親則為孝，吾之處常固各盡其道，而處變亦不失其常矣。往事難處，有如趙苞職守君城，而母為虜執。當此之時，守城棄母，不可也；從母棄城，不可也。苞也始為君戰，而棄其母
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: At difficult junctures in human relationships, he can weigh competing claims and handle them so well. This fully demonstrates the precision with which he discerns principle.
Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: His answers are detailed, and his handling of the issues appropriate. Is he not one who has devoted himself to studying loyalty and filial piety?
Examiner Yang, School Director, comments: He supplies textual evidence and knows which course to follow. Commendable, commendable!
Nothing under Heaven is harder to perfect than benevolence, and nothing harder to attain than righteousness. Yet when righteousness is finely discerned and benevolence fully developed, nothing under Heaven is difficult to handle. What is benevolence? Accord with principle without selfish intent is called benevolence. What is righteousness? Acting as is fitting is called righteousness. Benevolence and righteousness are inherent in the human heart. They are considered difficult because people are constrained by their endowment of vital energy and obscured by material desires. They leave their hearts untended without seeking to recover them, and abandon their proper path without following it. Viewed from this position, the task seems almost as difficult as ascending to Heaven. Those committed to learning choose what is good so as to understand it, and overcome the self so as to recover it, renewing themselves daily and growing fuller each month. Once my righteousness is finely discerned and my benevolence fully developed, the balance and measure lie within me, precise and exact, without error. Thus, toward my ruler I am loyal, and toward my parents I am filial. In ordinary circumstances I fully carry out the proper way in each relationship; in extraordinary circumstances, too, I do not depart from its constant principles. Among difficult situations in the past was that of Zhao Bao, whose duty was to defend his ruler’s city, while his mother was seized by enemy captors. At that moment, to defend the city and abandon his mother was unacceptable; to follow his mother and abandon the city was also unacceptable. Bao initially fought for his ruler and abandoned his mother…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
繼痛母死而喪其生苞之死死於忠孝矣
愚所追恨者苞不死於執母之時而死於
母喪之後也蓋當母之被執而不可請也
苞則當以軍旅之責寄之副貳而對賊自
殺則彼庶知專城不在吾而質母為無用
城守而母全矣忠孝不兩盡乎此則義精
仁熟之事而苞之倉卒蓋未能也李璀身
為王臣而父謀不軌當此之時黨父危君
不可也為君賣父不可也璀也始則報君
===
以備其父終則隨父以殺其身璀之死死
於忠孝矣愚所追惜者璀不死於諫父之
時而死於父叛之後也蓋當父之欲叛而
不可回也璀則當以家族之危泣之再三
而對父自殘則彼庶知人心不附己而赤
族為立致父悔而君安矣忠孝不兩全乎
此則仁至義盡之事而璀之計處蓋未及
也乃若李密陳情養祖母而表稱所事漢
為偽朝忘君諛儲於忠安在雖有烏鳥之
punctuated:
繼痛母死而喪其生。苞之死，死於忠孝矣。愚所追恨者，苞不死於執母之時，而死於母喪之後也。蓋當母之被執而不可請也，苞則當以軍旅之責寄之副貳，而對賊自殺，則彼庶知專城不在吾，而質母為無用，城守而母全矣。忠孝不兩盡乎？此則義精仁熟之事，而苞之倉卒蓋未能也。

李璀身為王臣，而父謀不軌。當此之時，黨父危君不可也，為君賣父不可也。璀也始則報君以備其父，終則隨父以殺其身。璀之死，死於忠孝矣。愚所追惜者，璀不死於諫父之時，而死於父叛之後也。蓋當父之欲叛而不可回也，璀則當以家族之危泣之再三，而對父自殘，則彼庶知人心不附己，而赤族為立致，父悔而君安矣。忠孝不兩全乎？此則仁至義盡之事，而璀之計處蓋未及也。

乃若李密陳情養祖母，而表稱所事漢為偽朝，忘君諛儲，於忠安在？雖有烏鳥之
translation_en:
…then, grieving over his mother's death, he lost his own life. Zhao Bao thus died for loyalty and filial devotion. What I, in my humble judgment, regret in retrospect is that Bao did not die when his mother was taken captive, but only after her death. When his mother had been captured and her release could not be secured by entreaty, Bao should have entrusted military responsibility to his deputy and killed himself before the enemy. They might then have realized that command of the city no longer rested with him and that holding his mother hostage was useless. The city would have been defended and his mother preserved. Would this not have fulfilled both loyalty and filial devotion? Such action requires a refined sense of righteousness and fully developed benevolence; in his haste, Bao was evidently unable to achieve it.

Li Cui was a servant of the sovereign, yet his father plotted rebellion. In those circumstances, he could not side with his father and endanger his ruler, nor could he betray his father for his ruler's sake. Cui first informed his ruler so that precautions could be taken against his father, and ultimately followed his father in meeting his own death. Cui thus died for loyalty and filial devotion. What I regret in retrospect is that Cui did not die while remonstrating with his father, but only after his father had rebelled. When his father intended to rebel and could not be turned back, Cui should have repeatedly pleaded with him in tears about the danger to their entire family and then inflicted mortal injury upon himself before his father. His father might then have realized that people's hearts did not support him and that the extermination of his clan would immediately follow. His father would have repented and his ruler would have been secure. Would this not have preserved both loyalty and filial devotion? Such action requires benevolence and righteousness carried to their fullest extent; Cui's deliberations evidently fell short of this.

As for Li Mi, he set forth his circumstances in a memorial requesting leave to care for his grandmother, yet in that memorial he called the Han, which he had served, an illegitimate dynasty. Forgetting his ruler and flattering the heir apparent [?], where was his loyalty? Though he possessed the crow's…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
私情不足尚也温嶠奉表赴江南而母留
不可遂至絶裾急仕忘親於孝何有雖有
犬馬之微勞不足道也漢王陵之母與徐
庶之母同質敵營也陵不顧母而致其殺
身以成事漢之功心能恝然乎若庶則辭
昭烈而奔母所在名雖泯而心則安矣晉
嵇紹之父與王裒之父同死非命也紹不
讎晉而仕爲侍中以著蕩隂之節事能全
善乎若裒則辭徵辟而隱居教授身雖隱
===
而事則得矣忠孝兼全有如范文正公者
先憂後樂志形於言其出將入相忠效於
宋仁宗之世者多矣而其貧時養母妻躬
執爨孝莫大焉又有如岳武穆王者盡忠
報國銘涅於背其攘夷却狄忠效於宋高
宗之朝者大矣而其遣人迎母守喪廬墓
孝莫尚焉昔唐陽城爲國子司業引諸生
告之曰凡學者所以學爲忠與孝也旨哉
言乎今忠孝之道具載聖經而掌於
punctuated:
私情，不足尚也。温嶠奉表赴江南，而母留不可，遂至絶裾，急仕忘親，於孝何有？雖有犬馬之微勞，不足道也。漢王陵之母與徐庶之母同質敵營也，陵不顧母而致其殺身，以成事漢之功，心能恝然乎？若庶則辭昭烈而奔母所在，名雖泯而心則安矣。晉嵇紹之父與王裒之父同死非命也，紹不讎晉而仕爲侍中，以著蕩隂之節，事能全善乎？若裒則辭徵辟而隱居教授，身雖隱而事則得矣。
忠孝兼全，有如范文正公者，先憂後樂，志形於言，其出將入相，忠效於宋仁宗之世者多矣。而其貧時養母，妻躬執爨，孝莫大焉。又有如岳武穆王者，盡忠報國，銘涅於背，其攘夷却狄，忠效於宋高宗之朝者大矣。而其遣人迎母，守喪廬墓，孝莫尚焉。昔唐陽城爲國子司業，引諸生告之曰：「凡學者，所以學爲忠與孝也。」旨哉言乎！今忠孝之道具載聖經，而掌於
translation_en:
…private affection, it is not worthy of esteem. Wen Jiao bore a memorial to Jiangnan; his mother could not persuade him to stay, and he went so far as to sever the skirt of his robe to leave her. Eager for office, he forgot his parent: what filial devotion was there in this? Though he rendered some slight service, like that of a dog or horse, it is not worth mentioning. The mother of Wang Ling of the Han and the mother of Xu Shu were both held hostage in enemy camps. Ling disregarded his mother and thereby brought about her taking her own life, securing his achievement in serving the Han. Could his heart remain unmoved? Shu, by contrast, took leave of Emperor Zhaolie and hastened to where his mother was. Though his reputation faded into obscurity, his heart was at peace. The father of Ji Shao of the Jin and the father of Wang Pou both met violent deaths. Shao did not treat the Jin as his enemy but served it as Palace Attendant, thereby displaying his steadfast loyalty at Dangyin. Could his conduct be wholly good? Pou, by contrast, declined summonses to office and lived in retirement, teaching. Though he remained obscure, his conduct was right.
Among those who fulfilled both loyalty and filial devotion was Lord Fan Wenzheng. His resolve found expression in his words: to be first in anxiety and last in enjoyment. Serving as a general in the field and as chief minister at court, he rendered many loyal services in the reign of Emperor Renzong of the Song. Yet when he was poor, he supported his mother, and his wife personally tended the cooking fire: no filial devotion could be greater. Another such man was Prince Yue Wumu. The words “Exhaust your loyalty in repaying the country” were tattooed on his back. In expelling the barbarians and repelling their incursions, he rendered great loyal service at the court of Emperor Gaozong of the Song. Yet he also sent someone to bring his mother to him and, after her death, observed mourning and dwelt in a hut beside her grave: no filial devotion could surpass this. Formerly, when Yang Cheng of the Tang was Director of Studies of the Directorate of Education, he gathered the students and told them: “All learning is a means of learning to be loyal and filial.” How profound these words are! Now the Way of loyalty and filial devotion is fully recorded in the sages’ classics, and its administration is entrusted to…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
邦教愚生樂育庠序之中漸摩
仁義之化于兹有年矣平日在家庸行之常
黽勉朝夕蓋無足道者而大節之處則幸
逢
熈皥之世萬不一遇無足慮焉但高山景行
之懷每念昔賢文正公之為人平生勵風
節樂名教信而好古六經之旨通於斷齏
之時憂不忘公萬言之書上於枕塊之日
其任天下之重也毀譽憂戚不動其心其
===
恤祖宗之後也恩例俸賜嘗均於族凡所
以立身行道處家報國者磊磊落落如青
天白日無疵瑕之可議竊不自揣事君事
父處窮處達一願學之而未能也若夫等
而上之聖人義精仁熟之道則猶陟華始
步未敢望巔惟執事進而教之幸甚
第三場
張鍾靈
同考試官教諭陳批條答無遺蓋嘗究心理學者
punctuated:
邦教。愚生樂育庠序之中，漸摩仁義之化，于兹有年矣。平日在家，庸行之常，黽勉朝夕，蓋無足道者。而大節之處，則幸逢熈皥之世，萬不一遇，無足慮焉。但高山景行之懷，每念昔賢文正公之為人：平生勵風節，樂名教，信而好古；六經之旨，通於斷齏之時；憂不忘公，萬言之書，上於枕塊之日。其任天下之重也，毀譽憂戚不動其心；其恤祖宗之後也，恩例俸賜嘗均於族。凡所以立身行道、處家報國者，磊磊落落，如青天白日，無疵瑕之可議。竊不自揣，事君事父，處窮處達，一願學之而未能也。若夫等而上之，聖人義精仁熟之道，則猶陟華始步，未敢望巔。惟執事進而教之，幸甚。

第三場

張鍾靈

同考試官教諭陳批：條答無遺，蓋嘗究心理學者。
translation_en:
…the instruction of the realm. This humble student has enjoyed nurturing instruction in the schools and has been gradually imbued with the transforming influence of benevolence and righteousness for several years now. In everyday life at home, I diligently attend morning and evening to the ordinary duties of conduct; there is surely nothing in this worth mentioning. As for occasions demanding great moral resolve, I am fortunate to live in an age of radiant harmony: such occasions scarcely arise once in ten thousand instances, and there is no cause for concern. Yet, in my longing to look up to lofty mountains and follow the great road of virtue, I constantly reflect upon the character of the worthy Lord Wenzheng of old. Throughout his life he cultivated moral integrity, delighted in the ethical teachings, and trusted and cherished antiquity. He mastered the meaning of the Six Classics while still living on meager portions of chopped pickled vegetables. Even in grief he did not forget public concerns, submitting a memorial of ten thousand words while using a clod of earth as his pillow in mourning. When bearing the weight of responsibility for the realm, neither blame nor praise, anxiety nor sorrow could disturb his heart. In caring for the descendants of his ancestors, he regularly shared imperial favors, his salary, and gifts with his clansmen. In everything by which he established his character and practiced the Way, managed his household and repaid his country, he was open and upright, like the clear sky and bright sun, without a blemish that could invite criticism. Presumptuous though it may be, in serving my ruler and my father, in adversity and in success, my sole wish is to emulate him, though I have not yet succeeded. As for ascending still higher to the sages’ Way of perfected righteousness and fully matured benevolence, I am like someone taking his first step up Mount Hua, not yet daring to look toward the summit. If you would lead me onward and instruct me, I would be most fortunate.

Third Session

Zhang Zhongling

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: His answers address every point without omission. He is evidently someone who has devoted serious thought to the Learning of Principle.

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭許批近思錄一書最切於日用而學者
者所當用心者也此篇敷答詳盡是宜錄之
考試官教諭俞批考據詳悉
考試官學正楊批載道之文精熟如此於道亦庶
幾矣
對道有體用而著書者必由體以達乎用
道有邪正而著書者必崇正以闢乎邪甚
矣古人之著書無非所以為道計耳體用
既分則進道者有所歸邪正既別則志道
===
者無所惑此近思錄一書之作有功於吾
道也大矣仰惟執事先生發策秋闈下詢
承學而舉近思錄之書為言蓋以朱呂之
學望承學其嘉惠之心盛矣愚雖不敏敢
不悉心以對念昔紫陽朱子與東萊呂氏
會止寒泉精舍讀周程張子之書嘆其廣
大閎博若無津涯而懼夫初學不知所入
也因共掇取其關於大體而切於日用者
以為近思錄一編考圖書傳集之精粹遡
punctuated:
同考試官教諭許批：近思錄一書，最切於日用，而學者者所當用心者也。此篇敷答詳盡，是宜錄之。
考試官教諭俞批：考據詳悉。
考試官學正楊批：載道之文，精熟如此，於道亦庶幾矣。
對：道有體用，而著書者必由體以達乎用；道有邪正，而著書者必崇正以闢乎邪。甚矣，古人之著書，無非所以為道計耳！體用既分，則進道者有所歸；邪正既別，則志道者無所惑。此《近思錄》一書之作，有功於吾道也大矣！仰惟執事先生發策秋闈，下詢承學，而舉《近思錄》之書為言，蓋以朱呂之學望承學，其嘉惠之心盛矣！愚雖不敏，敢不悉心以對？念昔紫陽朱子與東萊呂氏會止寒泉精舍，讀周程張子之書，嘆其廣大閎博，若無津涯，而懼夫初學不知所入也。因共掇取其關於大體而切於日用者，以為《近思錄》一編，考圖書傳集之精粹，遡
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: Reflections on Things at Hand (Jinsi lu) is a book of the utmost relevance to daily practice, to which students should devote their attention [the transcription repeats 者 here]. This essay develops its replies thoroughly and fully; it deserves inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor: The examination of textual evidence is detailed and comprehensive.

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: With such refinement and mastery in writing that conveys the Way, the author must also be close to attaining the Way itself.

In reply: The Way has substance and function, and those who write books must proceed from substance to attain function. With regard to the Way, there are heterodoxy and orthodoxy, and those who write books must uphold orthodoxy to refute heterodoxy. How profound this is! The ancients wrote books solely out of concern for the Way. Once substance and function are distinguished, those advancing in the Way have a destination; once heterodoxy and orthodoxy are differentiated, those committed to the Way are free from confusion. Thus the compilation of Reflections on Things at Hand rendered a great service to our Way!

I respectfully consider how you, honored sir, have set a policy question in the autumn Provincial Examination, condescending to inquire of us students and choosing Reflections on Things at Hand as your subject. Surely you expect us students to attain the learning of Zhu and Lü. How generous your wish to benefit us! Though I am slow of understanding, how could I dare not devote my whole mind to answering?

I recall how Master Zhu of Ziyang and Master Lü of Donglai once met and stayed at the Hanquan Study Retreat. Reading the writings of Masters Zhou, Cheng, and Zhang, they marveled at their breadth and depth, seemingly without ford or shore, and feared that beginners would not know where to enter. Together, therefore, they selected passages concerning the fundamental framework and bearing closely on daily practice, compiling them into Reflections on Things at Hand. They examined the finest essence of diagrams, writings, commentaries, and collected works, and traced…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
濂洛關陝之淵源條分類別而體用以之
兼該綱舉目張而邪正以之明辨信六藝
之喉襟四子之階梯也觀其首之以求端
而論道體指性之本原以示人底止之地
明道之體統以起人嚮望之心次之以用
力而論為學旣致知以推極吾心之識復
存養以涵泳吾心之理由是而處己曰克
己曰家道曰出處義利無非處己之方也
由是而治人曰治體曰治法曰政教警戒
===
無非治人之要也至於辨異端觀聖賢其
說亦無不備載焉以辨異端言之如兼愛
為我本楊墨之道也而師也過則漸至於
兼愛商也不及則便至於為我噫過與不
及同出於儒者之為而兼愛為我實由於
末流之弊所以錄此者欲學者不可以不
察也直內方外本吾儒之事也而釋氏之
收斂虛靜敬以直內則有之其所以滅絕
倫理義以方外何有焉噫觀其心之所存
punctuated:
濂洛關陝之淵源，條分類別，而體用以之兼該；綱舉目張，而邪正以之明辨。信六藝之喉襟、四子之階梯也。觀其首之以求端而論道體，指性之本原，以示人底止之地；明道之體統，以起人嚮望之心。次之以用力而論為學，旣致知以推極吾心之識，復存養以涵泳吾心之理。由是而處己，曰克己，曰家道，曰出處義利，無非處己之方也。由是而治人，曰治體，曰治法，曰政教警戒，無非治人之要也。至於辨異端、觀聖賢，其說亦無不備載焉。
以辨異端言之，如兼愛、為我，本楊墨之道也，而師也過，則漸至於兼愛；商也不及，則便至於為我。噫！過與不及，同出於儒者之為，而兼愛、為我，實由於末流之弊。所以錄此者，欲學者不可以不察也。直內方外，本吾儒之事也，而釋氏之收斂虛靜，敬以直內則有之；其所以滅絕倫理，義以方外何有焉？噫！觀其心之所存，
translation_en:
…the profound intellectual sources in Lian, Luo, Guan, and Shan. By arranging material under headings and classifying it by subject, it encompasses both substance and function; by setting out the main principles and unfolding their particulars, it clearly distinguishes the heterodox from the orthodox. It is indeed a vital gateway to the Six Arts and a stairway to the four masters. Observe how it begins with seeking the starting point and discusses the substance of the Way: it points to the original source of human nature to show people where they should come to rest, and clarifies the coherent structure of the Way to awaken their aspiration toward it. Next, it turns to applying effort and discusses learning: one both extends knowledge to develop the understanding of one's mind to the utmost and preserves and nourishes the mind to steep oneself in its inherent principles. From this it proceeds to the conduct of oneself: overcoming the self, the way of the family, and entering or withdrawing from office, righteousness and profit—all concern methods of conducting oneself. From this it proceeds to governing others: the essential structure of government, methods of government, and political instruction and admonitions—all concern the essentials of governing others. As for distinguishing heterodox teachings and contemplating sages and worthies, their teachings on these matters are likewise fully recorded.
To speak of distinguishing heterodox teachings: universal love and acting for oneself were originally the ways of Yang Zhu and Mo Di. Yet Shi went too far and thus gradually approached universal love; Shang fell short and thus readily approached acting for oneself. Alas! Going too far and falling short both arise in the conduct of Confucian scholars, while universal love and acting for oneself actually result from the degeneration of their later followers. The purpose of recording this is to make students recognize that they must examine such matters carefully. Making oneself upright within and square without is fundamentally the work of us Confucians. In the Buddhists' inward concentration, emptiness, and stillness, there is indeed something of making oneself upright within through reverence. But since they extinguish ethical relationships, how can they possess righteousness by which to make themselves square without? Alas! When we observe what they hold in their minds…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
若相符合究其行之所檢實相悖戾所以
錄此者欲學者不可以不審也論導氣之
術則以順理窒欲為養生而闢其長生久
視之非焉論神仙之說則以保形鍊氣為
延年而闢其白日飛昇之妄焉若此者非
所以辨異端而何以觀聖賢言之論文王
不識不知似堯舜之性之也論大禹不矜
不伐似湯武之反之也論仲尼渾淪而溥
博不猶元氣之流行乎論顏孟純粹而英
===
發不猶春生秋殺之氣象乎謂荀卿才高
而過多如以人性為惡是已謂楊雄才短
而過少如以法言擬易是已以道義而陳
江都謂仲舒度越於諸子者此也以詐力
而取劉璋謂孔明未盡於王道者此也作
中說而極有格言稱王通為一隱君子也
宜矣作原道而灼有定見許韓愈為近世
豪傑也當矣周茂叔觀庭草之交翠不除
生意何充滿邪張子厚見餓莩而食便不
punctuated:
若相符合，究其行之所檢，實相悖戾。所以錄此者，欲學者不可以不審也。論導氣之術，則以順理窒欲為養生，而闢其長生久視之非焉；論神仙之說，則以保形鍊氣為延年，而闢其白日飛昇之妄焉。若此者，非所以辨異端而何？
以觀聖賢言之，論文王不識不知，似堯舜之性之也；論大禹不矜不伐，似湯武之反之也。論仲尼渾淪而溥博，不猶元氣之流行乎？論顏孟純粹而英發，不猶春生秋殺之氣象乎？謂荀卿才高而過多，如以人性為惡是已；謂楊雄才短而過少，如以《法言》擬《易》是已。以道義而陳江都，謂仲舒度越於諸子者，此也；以詐力而取劉璋，謂孔明未盡於王道者，此也。作《中說》而極有格言，稱王通為一隱君子也宜矣；作《原道》而灼有定見，許韓愈為近世豪傑也當矣。周茂叔觀庭草之交翠不除，生意何充滿邪！張子厚見餓莩而食便不
translation_en:
…seem to accord with one another; yet when one examines the restraints governing their conduct, they are actually opposed. These statements were recorded to impress upon students the necessity of careful scrutiny. In discussing techniques for guiding the vital breath, it identifies following principle and restraining desires as the means of nourishing life, while refuting the error of seeking perpetual longevity. In discussing the teachings concerning immortals, it identifies preserving the bodily form and refining the vital breath as means of prolonging one’s years, while refuting the delusion of ascending into the heavens in broad daylight. What are such passages for, if not to distinguish heterodox teachings?
As for observing the sages and worthies: its discussion of King Wen’s acting without conscious knowledge or awareness likens him to Yao and Shun, whose virtue was innate; its discussion of Yu the Great’s neither priding himself nor boasting likens him to Tang and Wu, who recovered that virtue through cultivation. In describing Zhongni as an undivided whole, vast and all-embracing, does it not liken him to the circulation of primordial vital energy? In describing Yan Hui and Mengzi as pure and brilliant in their expression, does it not liken them to the manifestations of spring’s life-giving and autumn’s life-ending energies? It says that Xun Qing possessed great talent but made many errors: his assertion that human nature is evil is one such example. It says that Yang Xiong possessed limited talent but made few errors: his modeling the Model Sayings on the Book of Changes is one such example [?]. Expounding the Way and righteousness at Jiangdu—this is why it says that Dong Zhongshu surpassed the various masters. Taking Liu Zhang’s territory through deception and force—this is why it says that Kongming fell short of fully realizing the Kingly Way. Since Wang Tong wrote the Explanations of the Mean, which contains many exemplary sayings, it is fitting to call him a gentleman living in retirement. Since Han Yu wrote Inquiry into the Way, displaying clear and settled judgments, it is appropriate to recognize him as an outstanding man of recent times. Zhou Maoshu gazed at the intermingling green grasses in his courtyard and did not remove them: how abundantly the impulse of life filled him! When Zhang Zihou saw people who had died of starvation, his food then no longer…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
美仁心何周徧邪論明道之接人温厚抱
和氣者則朱謝其徒也論伊川之師道尊
嚴立門雪者則游楊其輩也若此者非觀
聖賢而何合而言之則知近思錄之一書
規模之大而進脩有序綱領之要而節目
詳明學者誠於此而玩心焉亦足以得其
門而入矣由是以求四子之全書會其博
而反諸約則其宗廟之美百官之富庶乎
其有以進而見之矣此朱吕纂集是書之
===
微意也謹對
第四問
羅濟
同考試官教諭李批我
朝名臣之文德武功此策悉之而尤知嚮慕可嘉
考試官教諭俞批故實無遺優劣具見蓋嘗寤寐
賢豪者矣
考試官學正楊批歷述
當代名臣有若親見必平日知所景仰者歟
punctuated:
美，仁心何周徧邪！論明道之接人温厚，抱和氣者則朱、謝其徒也；論伊川之師道尊嚴，立門雪者則游、楊其輩也。若此者，非觀聖賢而何？合而言之，則知《近思錄》之一書，規模之大而進脩有序，綱領之要而節目詳明。學者誠於此而玩心焉，亦足以得其門而入矣。由是以求四子之全書，會其博而反諸約，則其宗廟之美、百官之富，庶乎其有以進而見之矣。此朱、吕纂集是書之微意也。謹對。
第四問
羅濟
同考試官教諭李批：我朝名臣之文德武功，此策悉之，而尤知嚮慕，可嘉。
考試官教諭俞批：故實無遺，優劣具見，蓋嘗寤寐賢豪者矣。
考試官學正楊批：歷述當代名臣，有若親見，必平日知所景仰者歟？
translation_en:
…no longer tasted good: how all-embracing his benevolent heart was! When discussing Mingdao’s warmth and generosity in receiving others, those who embraced his harmonious spirit were disciples such as Zhu and Xie. When discussing Yichuan’s dignity and strictness as a teacher, those who stood in the snow at his gate were men such as You and Yang. What are these examples if not the contemplation of sages and worthies? Taken together, they show that Reflections on Things at Hand (Jinsi lu) is vast in scope yet provides an orderly progression for self-cultivation; its guiding principles are essential, while its particulars are detailed and clear. If students truly ponder it with full attention, it will suffice to enable them to find the gate and enter. Proceeding from this to seek out the complete writings of the four masters, comprehending their breadth and returning to their essentials, they may then advance far enough to behold the beauty of their ancestral temples and the abundance of their officials—that is, the riches of their learning. This was the subtle intention of Zhu and Lü in compiling this book. Respectfully submitted in reply.
Fourth Question
Luo Ji 羅濟
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: This policy essay comprehensively treats the civil virtues and military achievements of our dynasty’s eminent ministers. Particularly commendable is its understanding that they should be admired and emulated.
Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: No historical particulars are omitted, and relative merits are fully apparent. Surely this is someone who has dwelt on worthies and outstanding men both waking and sleeping.
Examiner Yang, School Director, comments: He recounts in succession the eminent ministers of the present dynasty as though he had seen them in person. Surely he has long known whom to look up to and admire?

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
對誦易有雲龍風虎之喻而知君臣相與
之幾讀書有元首股肱之歌而知明良際
會之盛此上有文武之君則下必有文武
之臣感雲龍風虎於一堂會元首股肱於
一體夫豈偶然之故而已哉執事所典者
文衡所取者文士而策試諸生顧兼問乎
武豈不以鏖戰文塲之士亦有能敵愾禦
侮抜幟先登者乎而愚也非其人雖然明
問不可以虛請誦其所聞而求正焉嗟夫
===
文武之並用於世其來尚矣然必有是君
然後有是臣故有丕顯文王則有周公操
制作之文有丕承武王則有太公著鷹揚
之武由成周而至勝國上下三千年間未
甞有有是君而無是臣者也亦未甞有無
是君而有是臣者也兹欲縷數之而執事
有戒請以我
朝言之
太祖高皇帝誕膺
punctuated:
對：誦易，有雲龍風虎之喻，而知君臣相與之幾；讀書，有元首股肱之歌，而知明良際會之盛。此上有文武之君，則下必有文武之臣，感雲龍風虎於一堂，會元首股肱於一體，夫豈偶然之故而已哉？執事所典者文衡，所取者文士，而策試諸生，顧兼問乎武，豈不以鏖戰文塲之士，亦有能敵愾禦侮、抜幟先登者乎？而愚也非其人。雖然，明問不可以虛，請誦其所聞而求正焉。

嗟夫！文武之並用於世，其來尚矣。然必有是君，然後有是臣。故有丕顯文王，則有周公操制作之文；有丕承武王，則有太公著鷹揚之武。由成周而至勝國，上下三千年間，未甞有有是君而無是臣者也，亦未甞有無是君而有是臣者也。兹欲縷數之，而執事有戒，請以我朝言之。太祖高皇帝誕膺
translation_en:
In reply: Reciting the Book of Changes, I encounter the analogy of clouds following the dragon and wind following the tiger, and thus understand the subtle workings of the mutual affinity between ruler and minister. Reading the Book of Documents, I encounter the song of the head and the limbs, and thus understand the flourishing brought about when an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers meet. When above there is a ruler accomplished in civil and military affairs, below there must be ministers similarly accomplished. They respond to one another like clouds and dragon, wind and tiger, within a single hall; they unite like head and limbs in a single body. Could this possibly be merely a matter of chance? You, honored examiners, preside over the weighing of literary merit and select men of letters. Yet in testing the students with policy questions, you also inquire about military affairs. Is this not because among those who battle fiercely in the literary arena there may also be men capable of confronting the enemy, repelling aggression, seizing enemy standards, and being first to scale the walls? I, in my ignorance, am not such a man. Nevertheless, your discerning question cannot be left unanswered. Allow me to recount what I have heard and seek your correction.

Alas! The joint employment of civil and military accomplishments in the world has a long history. Yet only when there is such a ruler can there be such ministers. Thus, with the greatly illustrious King Wen came the Duke of Zhou, who exercised his civil accomplishments in establishing institutions; with King Wu, who grandly continued his predecessor’s work, came Taigong, who displayed martial prowess like a soaring hawk. From the Zhou dynasty to the former dynasty, over some three thousand years, there has never been such a ruler without such ministers, nor have there ever been such ministers without such a ruler. I would now enumerate them in detail, but you have cautioned against this; allow me therefore to speak of our own dynasty. Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, magnificently received…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
景命肇造
鴻業
天戈一揮四方響應其武一帝堯之武也
聖製諸書
天葩競發布告臣民昭回雲漢其文一帝堯
之文也
聖子神孫繼體守成
太宗文皇帝之神文聖武
仁宗昭皇帝之弘文欽武
===
宣宗章皇帝之欽文昭武
英宗睿皇帝之昭文憲武
憲宗純皇帝之崇文肅武
列聖相承文武兼備而文臣武將之中其功業
足以軒天地而昭日月銘鍾鼎而勒旂常
者夥矣茲欲泛論之而執事有命試舉其
尤者言之文臣之中若誠意伯劉基才堪
王佐而炳物幾先翼
龍以飛而運籌帷幄繼乎子房之名也為無愧
punctuated:
景命，肇造鴻業。天戈一揮，四方響應，其武一帝堯之武也。聖製諸書，天葩競發，布告臣民，昭回雲漢，其文一帝堯之文也。
聖子神孫，繼體守成。太宗文皇帝之神文聖武，仁宗昭皇帝之弘文欽武，宣宗章皇帝之欽文昭武，英宗睿皇帝之昭文憲武，憲宗純皇帝之崇文肅武，列聖相承，文武兼備，而文臣武將之中，其功業足以軒天地而昭日月，銘鍾鼎而勒旂常者夥矣。
茲欲泛論之，而執事有命，試舉其尤者言之。文臣之中，若誠意伯劉基，才堪王佐，而炳物幾先，翼龍以飛，而運籌帷幄，繼乎子房之名也，為無愧。
translation_en:
…the great Mandate, and founded the magnificent imperial enterprise. With one sweep of his heavenly spear, the four quarters responded: his martial achievement was wholly that of Emperor Yao. In the various books of his sagely authorship, heavenly blossoms vied in flowering; promulgated to officials and people, they shone like the Milky Way. His civil achievement was wholly that of Emperor Yao.
His sagely sons and divine descendants succeeded to the throne and preserved the accomplished enterprise. Emperor Wen, Taizong, possessed divine civil virtue and sagely martial prowess; Emperor Zhao, Renzong, expansive civil virtue and reverent martial prowess; Emperor Zhang, Xuanzong, reverent civil virtue and illustrious martial prowess; Emperor Rui, Yingzong, illustrious civil virtue and exemplary martial prowess; and Emperor Chun, Xianzong, exalted civil virtue and solemn martial prowess. These successive sage rulers possessed both civil and martial excellence. Among their civil officials and military commanders were many whose achievements could lift heaven and earth and rival the sun and moon in brilliance, deserving inscription on bells and tripods and engraving upon banners.
I would now discuss them broadly, but you, honored examiners, have given your instructions; let me therefore select the most outstanding for discussion. Among the civil officials was Liu Ji, Earl of Chengyi. His talents fitted him to assist a king, and he discerned the incipient workings of affairs before they unfolded. Giving wings to the dragon to take flight, he devised strategies within the command tent. He was worthy, without shame, to inherit the renown of Zifang.

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
翰林學士宋濂學本聖經而德容之粹輔
導
青宮而文名之高得於溍卿之傳也為不忝
御史中丞章溢之器宇夷曠著名臺端而
高廟以守法稱之宜也國子祭酒宋訥之雅性
持重蜚聲六館而
高廟以純德許之宜也至若文貞公楊士奇秉
節堅貞優崇館閣而匡輔
四聖恩寵始終之不渝文敏公楊榮遇事剛果
===
掌
制經綸而擁佑
三朝身名保全之不替厥功甚著而文毅公李
時勉以剛大之氣積學中秘歷陳時事危
言動
主何烈哉武將之中若武寧王徐達翊我
皇祖功高一代而反狄陰山屠城不戮比之武
惠之仁為無間開平王常遇春輔我
皇祖勇冠三軍而席卷強漢光復中土方之鄂
punctuated:
翰林學士宋濂，學本聖經，而德容之粹，輔導青宮，而文名之高，得於溍卿之傳也，為不忝。御史中丞章溢之器宇夷曠，著名臺端，而高廟以守法稱之，宜也。國子祭酒宋訥之雅性持重，蜚聲六館，而高廟以純德許之，宜也。至若文貞公楊士奇，秉節堅貞，優崇館閣，而匡輔四聖，恩寵始終之不渝。文敏公楊榮，遇事剛果，掌制經綸，而擁佑三朝，身名保全之不替。厥功甚著。而文毅公李時勉，以剛大之氣，積學中秘，歷陳時事，危言動主，何烈哉！

武將之中，若武寧王徐達，翊我皇祖，功高一代，而反狄陰山，屠城不戮，比之武惠之仁，為無間。開平王常遇春，輔我皇祖，勇冠三軍，而席卷強漢，光復中土，方之鄂
translation_en:
Song Lian, Academician of the Hanlin Academy, grounded his learning in the sages’ classics and possessed a refined moral bearing. He guided and instructed the heir apparent, and his lofty literary reputation derived from the teaching transmitted by Jin qing 溍卿 [?], to which he did no discredit. Zhang Yi, Vice Censor-in-chief, was composed and broad-minded, winning distinction in the Censorate; it was fitting that Emperor Gao praised him for upholding the law. Song Ne, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, was naturally dignified and circumspect, and his reputation spread through the six colleges; it was fitting that Emperor Gao commended his pure virtue. As for Lord Wenzhen, Yang Shiqi, he maintained firm and steadfast integrity and enjoyed high standing in the literary academies. He assisted four sage sovereigns, whose favor toward him never wavered from beginning to end. Lord Wenmin, Yang Rong, was resolute and decisive in handling affairs. He took charge of drafting imperial commands and managing affairs of state, supporting the throne through three reigns and preserving his person and reputation without decline. His achievements were most illustrious. And Lord Wenyi, Li Shimian, with his upright and expansive spirit, accumulated learning in the imperial library, set forth current affairs in detail, and moved his sovereign with forthright words. How magnificent!

Among the military commanders, Xu Da, Prince of Wuning, assisted our imperial ancestor, and his achievements surpassed those of his age. He drove the northern foes back at the Yin Mountains and stormed cities without massacring their inhabitants. In benevolence he was the equal of Wuhui. Chang Yuchun, Prince of Kaiping, assisted our imperial ancestor, and his courage surpassed that of all the armies. He swept away the powerful Han regime and restored the central lands. Comparing him with E…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
公之勇爲不殊昭靖王沐英之長於智勇
而著績平交由侯而進之公宜也平江伯
陳瑄善於任使而興利漕運由伯而進之
侯宜也若襄武王湯和之奄舉甌閩摧堅
撫順而坐收方氏海上之難以靖潁川侯
傅友德奮身戎伍間関百戰而縛取明昇
全蜀之地以平厥功甚偉而武靖王李文
忠以勲戚之貴淹貫羣籍甲囊晝赤宣威
萬里何壯哉於乎彼若而人建立於
===
天造草昧之秋遭逢於
重熙累洽之日或以文德顯或以武功著斯
皆百年之英而無容議矣執事尤以優劣
爲問草野書生何敢容喙第以文臣皆未
易及也而吾所尤景仰者誠意伯之智辨
慶雲而識
眞主則其智誠爲天下之大智矣武將皆未易
能也而吾所尤敬慕者武寧王之功殪羣
雄而翼
punctuated: 公之勇爲不殊。昭靖王沐英之長於智勇，而著績平交，由侯而進之公宜也。平江伯陳瑄善於任使，而興利漕運，由伯而進之侯宜也。若襄武王湯和之奄舉甌閩，摧堅撫順，而坐收方氏，海上之難以靖；潁川侯傅友德奮身戎伍，間関百戰，而縛取明昇，全蜀之地以平，厥功甚偉。而武靖王李文忠以勲戚之貴，淹貫羣籍，甲囊晝赤，宣威萬里，何壯哉！於乎！彼若而人建立於天造草昧之秋，遭逢於重熙累洽之日，或以文德顯，或以武功著，斯皆百年之英，而無容議矣。執事尤以優劣爲問，草野書生何敢容喙？第以文臣皆未易及也，而吾所尤景仰者，誠意伯之智，辨慶雲而識眞主，則其智誠爲天下之大智矣。武將皆未易能也，而吾所尤敬慕者，武寧王之功，殪羣雄而翼
translation_en:
…was no different in valor from the Duke of E. Mu Ying, Prince Zhaojing, excelled in wisdom and courage and won distinction in pacifying Jiao [?]; his advancement from marquis to duke was fitting. Chen Xuan, Earl of Pingjiang, was adept at carrying out his commissions and brought benefits to grain transport; his advancement from earl to marquis was fitting. Tang He, Prince Xiangwu, swiftly took Ou and Min, crushed determined resistance, and conciliated those who submitted. He thereby secured the surrender of the Fang forces, bringing the troubles at sea to an end. Fu Youde, Marquis of Yingchuan, threw himself into military service and endured the hardships of a hundred battles. He captured Ming Sheng and brought the whole territory of Shu under control: his achievements were immense. Li Wenzhong, Prince Wujing, possessed the distinction of a meritorious imperial kinsman and was deeply versed in many books. “Armor, sack, daylight, red” [?]: he made his martial might known over ten thousand li. How magnificent!

Ah! Such men established their achievements when Heaven was bringing forth a new order amid obscurity and disorder, and lived to encounter days of ever-increasing prosperity and harmony. Some became renowned for civil virtue, others distinguished themselves through military achievements. All were outstanding men of the century, beyond dispute. Yet you, sir, particularly ask about their relative merits. How could a humble scholar from the countryside dare offer an opinion? Still, although all these civil officials are difficult to equal, what I especially admire is the wisdom of the Earl of Chengyi. By discerning auspicious clouds, he recognized the true sovereign: his wisdom was indeed wisdom of the highest order under Heaven. The military commanders, too, all possessed abilities difficult to match; yet what I especially revere is the achievement of the Prince of Wuning, who slew the contending warlords and lent his support to …

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
景運則其功誠爲天下之大功矣方今
聖天子日御
經筵講求治理其文繼
祖宗之文也
皇威丕振海隅臣服其武繼
祖宗之武也而文臣之立
朝者非但辭翰之工緻而已而識見足以經
邦武將之分閫者非但弓馬之習熟而已而
驍勇足以壯
===
國斯皆一世之豪而無容訾矣執事尤以得
失爲問韋布小子何敢僭言第以明珠之
囿不能無魚目之混嘉禾之塲不能無稂
莠之雜今日郡縣之中筮仕者皆章句之
儒豈能保其悉閑於文事乎衞所之內廕
襲者皆紈綺之子豈能保其悉精於武畧
乎而鼓舞振作之者其機亦由乎上之人
何如耳愚生儲養學宮寤寐英豪久矣儻
沾一命而文事武備尚當以
punctuated: 景運，則其功誠爲天下之大功矣。方今聖天子日御經筵，講求治理，其文繼祖宗之文也；皇威丕振，海隅臣服，其武繼祖宗之武也。而文臣之立朝者，非但辭翰之工緻而已，而識見足以經邦；武將之分閫者，非但弓馬之習熟而已，而驍勇足以壯國。斯皆一世之豪，而無容訾矣。執事尤以得失爲問，韋布小子何敢僭言？第以明珠之囿，不能無魚目之混；嘉禾之塲，不能無稂莠之雜。今日郡縣之中，筮仕者皆章句之儒，豈能保其悉閑於文事乎？衞所之內，廕襲者皆紈綺之子，豈能保其悉精於武畧乎？而鼓舞振作之者，其機亦由乎上之人何如耳。愚生儲養學宮，寤寐英豪久矣。儻沾一命，而文事武備，尚當以
translation_en:
…the glorious destiny of the dynasty, then his achievements truly rank among the greatest in the realm. Today, the sagely Son of Heaven attends the Classics Colloquium daily, investigating the principles of good government: his civil accomplishments continue those of his imperial ancestors. Imperial might is greatly displayed, and even the farthest shores submit: his military accomplishments continue those of his imperial ancestors. The civil officials serving at court possess more than elegant literary skills; their understanding suffices to govern the realm. The military commanders entrusted with regional commands possess more than proficiency in archery and horsemanship; their valor suffices to strengthen the state. These are all outstanding men of their age, beyond reproach.

You have asked particularly about successes and shortcomings. How could a young commoner in plain cloth presume to speak? Yet a collection of lustrous pearls cannot be entirely free of fish eyes mixed among them, nor a field of fine grain entirely free of weeds. Those now beginning official careers in the prefectures and counties are all scholars versed in textual explication. How can one guarantee that they are all practiced in civil administration? Those inheriting posts by hereditary privilege in the guards and battalions are all sons raised in silken luxury. How can one guarantee that they are all proficient in military strategy? The key to inspiring and rousing them lies simply in the character and conduct of those above them.

I, an unworthy student, have been nurtured in the government school and have long dreamed, waking and sleeping, of outstanding men. Should I receive even an initial appointment, in civil affairs and military preparedness I would still take as my models…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
當代之諸賢是法執事與其進也幸甚
第五問
朱褒
同考試官學正蔡批此策有識見有議論非練達時
事者不能况他策皆善他日立
朝豈安於尋常尺寸者歟是宜錄出
考試官教諭俞批有敷揚有斷制其亦明體而適
用者歟
考試官學正楊批區畫時事允當人心薦之於
上殆亦有用之士也
===
議天下之事當究其源處天下之事當求
其要蓋不究其源則天下之事空言無據
不求其要則天下之事漫然無成斯二者
皆非明體適用者也范文正云士當先天
下之憂而憂顧生何人乃敢以希文自待
乎雖然明問彰彰自有不容於默默者竊
惟
朝廷大封宗藩本以親親亦以固邦本誠所
punctuated:
當代之諸賢是法，執事與其進也，幸甚。

第五問
朱褒
同考試官學正蔡批：此策有識見，有議論，非練達時事者不能。况他策皆善，他日立朝，豈安於尋常尺寸者歟？是宜錄出。
考試官教諭俞批：有敷揚，有斷制，其亦明體而適用者歟？
考試官學正楊批：區畫時事，允當人心，薦之於上，殆亦有用之士也。

議天下之事，當究其源；處天下之事，當求其要。蓋不究其源，則天下之事空言無據；不求其要，則天下之事漫然無成。斯二者，皆非明體適用者也。范文正云：「士當先天下之憂而憂。」顧生何人，乃敢以希文自待乎？雖然，明問彰彰，自有不容於默默者。竊惟朝廷大封宗藩，本以親親，亦以固邦本，誠所
translation_en:
…take the worthy men of our age as models. If you, honored examiners, approve my advancement, I shall be most fortunate.

Fifth Question
Zhu Bao

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor (xuezheng): This policy essay displays insight and reasoned argument, which only someone well versed in current affairs could produce. Moreover, his other policy essays are all good. When he takes his place at court in the future, could he be content with ordinary, minor accomplishments? This essay should therefore be selected for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor (jiaoyu): There is both exposition and decisive judgment. Is he not someone who understands fundamental principles and applies them to practical affairs?

Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor (xuezheng): His plans for current affairs accord well with people’s wishes. Recommended to the throne, he would surely prove a man of practical usefulness.

In discussing the affairs of the realm, one should investigate their origins; in managing the affairs of the realm, one should seek out what is essential. Without investigating their origins, discussion of the realm’s affairs is empty talk without foundation; without seeking out what is essential, their management is aimless and accomplishes nothing. Neither approach constitutes understanding fundamental principles and applying them to practical affairs. Fan Wenzheng said: “A scholar should worry before all others in the realm worry.” Yet who am I, a mere student, to dare measure myself against Xiwen? Nevertheless, your illuminating question is so clear that there are matters on which I cannot remain silent. I humbly consider that the court’s extensive enfeoffment of imperial clansmen as princes was intended both to show affection for its kin and to secure the foundations of the state. It is indeed something that…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
當厚也今
宗支日漸繁衍府第之興作累歲無間則農
之時不能不違莊田之
錫予頻年有加則民之産不能不去此亦勢之
必至非所敢言但緣此而董工役者假公
濟私而糜費之無筭附聲勢者以强凌弱
而兼併之無厭民之財力如之何而不竭
邪往事已固無及然
本支百世誠不可不預爲之計嗣是而後
===
宗藩之封一遵
祖宗之成憲以處之府第限常制而程其工使
董工役者不得以糜費禄秩限常數而杜
其請俾附聲勢者無由以兼併凡所以勞
民而傷財者悉爲之裁抑則上下相安湖
湘之民財力庶其少紓矣古人良法亦何
以出此邪
朝廷世襲武臣本以報功亦以脩武備誠所
當重也今武臣日習紈綺或累干
punctuated:
當厚也。今宗支日漸繁衍，府第之興作累歲無間，則農之時不能不違；莊田之錫予頻年有加，則民之産不能不去。此亦勢之必至，非所敢言。但緣此而董工役者假公濟私，而糜費之無筭；附聲勢者以强凌弱，而兼併之無厭。民之財力如之何而不竭邪？往事已固無及，然本支百世，誠不可不預爲之計。嗣是而後，宗藩之封，一遵祖宗之成憲以處之；府第限常制而程其工，使董工役者不得以糜費；禄秩限常數而杜其請，俾附聲勢者無由以兼併。凡所以勞民而傷財者，悉爲之裁抑，則上下相安，湖湘之民財力庶其少紓矣。古人良法，亦何以出此邪？
朝廷世襲武臣，本以報功，亦以脩武備，誠所當重也。今武臣日習紈綺，或累干
translation_en:
…and indeed ought to be treated generously. Now the branches of the imperial clan grow ever more numerous. Construction of their residences continues year after year without interruption, inevitably disrupting the farming seasons; grants of landed estates increase year after year, inevitably depriving the people of their property. These are also inevitable consequences of the circumstances, on which I would not presume to speak. Yet those supervising construction exploit these occasions to serve private interests under the guise of public business, squandering resources without limit; those who attach themselves to princely influence use strength to oppress the weak and insatiably engross their holdings. How could the people’s wealth and strength fail to be exhausted? What has already happened is beyond remedy. Yet plans must surely be made in advance for the main and collateral branches of the imperial house through a hundred generations. Henceforth, the enfeoffment of imperial princes should be handled in strict accordance with the established statutes of the imperial ancestors. Their residences should be confined to the prescribed standards, and the work assessed accordingly, so that construction supervisors cannot squander resources. Their stipends should be confined to the prescribed amounts, and requests for more barred, so that those attaching themselves to princely influence have no means of engrossing others’ holdings. Everything that burdens the people and depletes their wealth should be curtailed and restrained. Then those above and below would live in mutual peace, and the people of Huxiang might gain some relief in their wealth and strength. How could even the sound methods of antiquity surpass this?
The court’s institution of hereditary military office was intended both to reward merit and to maintain military preparedness; it indeed deserves great importance. Now military officials grow daily more accustomed to luxurious silks, and some repeatedly transgress…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
憲典而科尅倍常則軍固不免於逋逃或虛
冒軍功而襲廕如故則軍亦不免於私役
此亦弊之必至固不可堪况外此而更戍
瘴鄉死亡之過半守禦苗寨生全之無幾
軍之尺籍如之何而不耗邪往事已不可
追然
宗社萬年不可不重爲之慮繼今以往兵戎之
職一遵
祖宗成法以治之累犯科尅者嚴降級不敘之
條非止立功而帶俸虛冒廕襲者坐罔上
欺君之罪匪直削爵而除名凡所以更戍
而守禦者舉爲之存恤則刑賞嚴明湖湘
之軍尺籍庶其少登矣
祖宗成法烏可不謹守邪流民嘯聚嘗廑
宵旰之憂不惟
命藩臬之臣以分治而又
命臺憲大臣以總治焉綱維甚嚴可無患矣
比來鄖襄山谷之中雜聚萬計欲盡遣之
punctuated:
憲典而科尅倍常，則軍固不免於逋逃；或虛冒軍功而襲廕如故，則軍亦不免於私役。此亦弊之必至，固不可堪。况外此而更戍瘴鄉，死亡之過半；守禦苗寨，生全之無幾。軍之尺籍如之何而不耗邪？往事已不可追，然宗社萬年，不可不重爲之慮。繼今以往，兵戎之職，一遵祖宗成法以治之。累犯科尅者，嚴降級不敘之條，非止立功而帶俸；虛冒廕襲者，坐罔上欺君之罪，匪直削爵而除名。凡所以更戍而守禦者，舉爲之存恤，則刑賞嚴明，湖湘之軍尺籍庶其少登矣。祖宗成法，烏可不謹守邪？

流民嘯聚，嘗廑宵旰之憂。不惟命藩臬之臣以分治，而又命臺憲大臣以總治焉。綱維甚嚴，可無患矣。比來鄖襄山谷之中，雜聚萬計，欲盡遣之，
translation_en:
…the statutory laws, while imposing exactions at twice the customary rate, then the soldiers inevitably flee; or, if officers fraudulently claim military merit yet continue to inherit their privileges as before, then the soldiers inevitably suffer conscription into private service. These are abuses that must follow, and they are already intolerable. Moreover, of those rotated into garrison duty in pestilential regions, more than half die; of those defending stockades in Miao territory, few survive unharmed. How could the military rolls fail to shrink? What has happened cannot be undone, yet we must give serious thought to the dynasty’s enduring security. Henceforth, military offices should be governed entirely according to the established laws of the imperial ancestors. For repeated exactions, rigorously enforce the provisions for demotion and disqualification from further appointment, rather than merely requiring offenders to earn military merit while retaining their salaries. Those who fraudulently claim hereditary privileges should be convicted of deceiving their superiors and their sovereign, rather than merely being stripped of rank and struck from the rolls. Give care and relief to all those serving on rotating garrison duty and in defense. Then punishments and rewards will be strict and clear, and the numbers on the military rolls of Huxiang may increase somewhat. How could the established laws of the imperial ancestors fail to be scrupulously observed?

The gathering of displaced people into bands has previously troubled Your Majesty, keeping you anxious from before dawn until late at night. You have not only ordered officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions to exercise separate oversight, but also ordered a high censorial official to exercise overall supervision. With such stringent arrangements, there should be no cause for concern. Recently, however, people of diverse origins have gathered by the tens of thousands in the mountains and valleys of Yun and Xiang. If one wishes to send them all away…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
恐無所於歸激之而成變欲盡留之恐無
以自給釀之而成禍議者誠不能無厝火
積薪之憂也為今之計莫若仰體
當今設撫治之初意于以審其軍匠籍其姓名
編之里甲孤苦貧窮者輕徭薄賦仁以綏
之而安其懷土之念兇暴惡逆者嚴刑峻
罰義以治之而弭其不軌之心加之民牧
擇人必有如龔黃卓魯者之在郡邑如此
庶幾寬嚴相濟而撫治之意得矣苗賊刼
===
殺嘗煩
廟堂之筭不獨
命兵民之職以分守而尤
命勳舊大臣以總鎮焉備禦甚密可無虞矣
邇者永郴寶靖之地刼殺靡常欲窮追之
則魚散鳥驚依險以自匿姑少縱之則豺
噬豨勇干紀而弗馴識者誠不能無履霜
堅氷之戒也為今之計莫若兼取古人備
禦之長策于以簡其卒伍利其甲兵謹其
punctuated:
恐無所於歸，激之而成變；欲盡留之，恐無以自給，釀之而成禍。議者誠不能無厝火積薪之憂也。為今之計，莫若仰體當今設撫治之初意，于以審其軍匠，籍其姓名，編之里甲。孤苦貧窮者，輕徭薄賦，仁以綏之，而安其懷土之念；兇暴惡逆者，嚴刑峻罰，義以治之，而弭其不軌之心。加之民牧擇人，必有如龔黃卓魯者之在郡邑。如此，庶幾寬嚴相濟，而撫治之意得矣。
苗賊刼殺，嘗煩廟堂之筭。不獨命兵民之職以分守，而尤命勳舊大臣以總鎮焉。備禦甚密，可無虞矣。邇者永郴寶靖之地，刼殺靡常。欲窮追之，則魚散鳥驚，依險以自匿；姑少縱之，則豺噬豨勇，干紀而弗馴。識者誠不能無履霜堅氷之戒也。為今之計，莫若兼取古人備禦之長策，于以簡其卒伍，利其甲兵，謹其
translation_en:
…there is fear that they would have nowhere to return to, and that provoking them would bring about rebellion. Yet if all were allowed to remain, there is fear that they would lack the means to support themselves, allowing disaster to develop. Those deliberating on this matter truly cannot but worry about fire laid beneath a pile of firewood. The best course now would be respectfully to embody the present Emperor’s original intention in establishing the office of Pacification: investigate their military or artisan status, register their names, and incorporate them into the lijia household organization. For the lonely, helpless, and impoverished, lighten labor obligations and taxes; soothe them with benevolence and satisfy their desire to remain on the land. For the violent, wicked, and rebellious, impose strict punishments and severe penalties; govern them with righteousness and quell their lawless intentions. Furthermore, choose suitable men to shepherd the people, ensuring that officials like Gong, Huang, Zhuo, and Lu serve in the prefectures and counties. In this way, leniency and severity might complement one another, and the purpose of pacification would be fulfilled.
The plundering and killing by Miao bandits have troubled the court’s deliberations. Orders were given not only to military and civil officials to defend their respective jurisdictions, but also, in particular, to senior ministers of longstanding meritorious service to assume overall command. Defensive preparations were very thorough, and there should have been no cause for anxiety. Recently, however, plundering and killing have occurred unpredictably in Yong, Chen, and Baojing. If pursued relentlessly, the bandits scatter like fish and startle like birds, hiding in rugged terrain; if given even a little latitude, they bite like jackals and rage like wild boars, violating established order and refusing submission. Discerning men truly cannot fail to heed the warning that treading on frost portends solid ice. The best course now would be to draw together the effective defensive strategies of the ancients: select and review the troops, put their armor and weapons in good order, and exercise vigilance over their…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
烽堠順則戢武而懷之以恩如舜之格有
苗不咎其既往逆則奮武而震之以威如
周之伐獫狁不輕其非敵加之備邊得人
必有如韓范李趙者之在軍中如此庶幾
攻守兩得而備禦之策善矣夫湖湘之弊
固多而此其最甚究其源求其要愚生所
見似不出此惟執事進而教之
punctuated: 烽堠。順則戢武而懷之以恩，如舜之格有苗，不咎其既往；逆則奮武而震之以威，如周之伐獫狁，不輕其非敵。加之備邊得人，必有如韓范李趙者之在軍中。如此，庶幾攻守兩得，而備禦之策善矣。夫湖湘之弊固多，而此其最甚。究其源，求其要，愚生所見似不出此。惟執事進而教之。
translation_en: …the beacon watchposts. If they submit, we should lay aside arms and win them over with kindness, just as Shun brought the Youmiao to submission, without blaming them for their past offenses. If they resist, we should muster our forces and overawe them with military might, just as the Zhou attacked the Xianyun, without treating them lightly as unworthy opponents. Furthermore, frontier defense must be entrusted to capable men: the army must have men like Han, Fan, Li, and Zhao. In this way, we may attain success in both attack and defense, and our defensive strategy will be sound. The troubles of the Hu-Xiang region are certainly many, but these are the most serious. In tracing their sources and seeking the essential remedies, the views of this humble student seem to extend no further than this. I ask only that you, honored examiners, favor me with further instruction.

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
弘治戊午秋八月當天下試
士之期巡按湖廣監察御史
王恩以求賢盛事也精白一
心咨謀于藩臬重臣預聘鎧
等司校文于時諸臣工有事
塲屋者罔不夙夜勤勵胥成
===
厥事錄成鎧謹序諸後竊惟
士者之學貴於有用治己治
人而已學而不知所以用亦
奚以學為哉是故五經者天
地之心也三才之紀也道德
之源也學者幼而學壯而行
思所以治己者在是所以治
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄後序

弘治戊午秋八月，當天下試士之期，巡按湖廣監察御史王恩以求賢盛事也，精白一心，咨謀于藩臬重臣，預聘鎧等司校文。于時諸臣工有事塲屋者，罔不夙夜勤勵，胥成厥事。錄成，鎧謹序諸後。

竊惟士者之學，貴於有用，治己治人而已。學而不知所以用，亦奚以學為哉？是故五經者，天地之心也，三才之紀也，道德之源也。學者幼而學，壯而行，思所以治己者在是，所以治
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In the autumn, in the eighth month of the wuwu year of the Hongzhi reign [1498], when it was time to examine scholars throughout the realm, Wang En, Investigating Censor assigned to巡按 Huguang, regarded the search for worthy men as a momentous undertaking. With a wholly pure and single-minded purpose, he consulted the senior officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions and engaged Kai and others in advance to oversee the assessment of examination essays. At that time, all officials serving in the examination compound worked diligently day and night, together bringing the undertaking to completion. When the record was completed, I, Kai, respectfully composed this postface.

I humbly consider that what makes a scholar’s learning valuable is its practical usefulness: governing oneself and governing others, and nothing more. If one studies without knowing how to put learning to use, what is the point of studying? Thus the Five Classics are the heart of Heaven and Earth, the ordering principles of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and the source of the Way and virtue. Those who pursue learning study in youth and put it into practice in maturity. They reflect that the means of governing themselves lie herein, and that the means of governing …

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
人者在是於易得其中於詩
書得其正於禮得其文於春
秋得其斷明善誠身以立其
本篤近舉遠以達其用參天
地賛化育以極功用之全斯
為有用之學也夫舟以濟川
車以行陸榖粟以療饑布帛
===
以禦寒各效用於天地之間
者也而謂士者之學率皆空
言不能周一世之用何足尚
哉古之學以治己後世之學
以欺己古之學以治人後世
之學以驕人内欺外驕欲人
己之治難矣甚者剽竊陳言
punctuated: 人者在是。於易得其中，於詩、書得其正，於禮得其文，於春秋得其斷。明善誠身，以立其本；篤近舉遠，以達其用；參天地，賛化育，以極功用之全。斯為有用之學也。夫舟以濟川，車以行陸，榖粟以療饑，布帛以禦寒，各效用於天地之間者也。而謂士者之學率皆空言，不能周一世之用，何足尚哉？古之學以治己，後世之學以欺己；古之學以治人，後世之學以驕人。内欺外驕，欲人己之治，難矣！甚者剽竊陳言
translation_en: …the means of governing others are found here. From the Changes one gains balance; from the Odes and Documents, correctness; from the Rites, refinement; and from the Spring and Autumn Annals, discernment. By understanding goodness and making oneself sincere, one establishes the foundation; by attending earnestly to what is near and extending one's efforts to what is distant, one puts learning into practice; by participating with Heaven and Earth and assisting their transforming and nourishing work, one brings its efficacy to full realization. This is learning that has practical use. Boats serve to cross rivers, carriages to travel over land, grain to relieve hunger, and cloth and silk to ward off cold: each performs its function between Heaven and Earth. Yet if the learning of scholars is said to consist entirely of empty words, unable to meet the needs of an age, what makes it worthy of esteem? Ancient learning served to govern oneself; the learning of later ages serves to deceive oneself. Ancient learning served to govern others; the learning of later ages serves to treat others arrogantly. With self-deception within and arrogance toward others without, bringing order to oneself and others is difficult indeed! In the worst cases, scholars plagiarize stale phrases…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
以求合有司之選則既不足
以致用而適以壞之虛車虛
舟以莫不惜顧投以矢石寧
不為可太息邪蓋嘗論之欺
與驕學者之病根也病根不
去學亦不固矧望其有用乎
本草脉經聖人所以濟夭札
===
也不探病根固已茫然無下
手處乃歸罪於本草脉經之
不效豈不厚誣也哉諸士子
遭際
昌辰涵泳
清化厥惟舊矣其所以為學必
求於有用也審矣茲以明經
punctuated:
以求合有司之選，則既不足以致用，而適以壞之。虛車虛舟，以莫不惜，顧投以矢石，寧不為可太息邪？蓋嘗論之：欺與驕，學者之病根也。病根不去，學亦不固，矧望其有用乎？《本草》《脉經》，聖人所以濟夭札也。不探病根，固已茫然無下手處，乃歸罪於《本草》《脉經》之不效，豈不厚誣也哉？
諸士子遭際昌辰，涵泳清化，厥惟舊矣。其所以為學，必求於有用也，審矣。茲以明經
translation_en:
…to seek acceptance in the selection conducted by the responsible officials: such learning is already inadequate for practical application and serves only to undermine it. Empty carts and empty boats are things that everyone cherishes [?]; yet arrows and stones are cast at them. Is this not cause for a deep sigh? I have reflected on this: deceit and arrogance are the root ailments of students. Unless these roots are removed, their learning cannot even be sound; how much less can one expect it to be useful? The Materia Medica (Bencao) and the Pulse Classic (Maijing) are the means by which the sages saved people from untimely death and pestilence. Without investigating the root of the illness, one is already bewildered, with no idea where to begin treatment. Then to blame the Materia Medica and the Pulse Classic for being ineffective—is this not a gross misrepresentation?
You students have long enjoyed an auspicious age and been steeped in its pure transforming influence. It is certain that in pursuing learning you must seek to make it useful. Now, through your mastery of the classics…

title: 弘治十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
登名是錄駸駸焉有官守言
責尚益勵所學嚴諸已弘厥
施毋為情勝毋為利撓毋為
習移毋為私蔽俾所以自治
所以治人與所以為學者一
致為孝子為名臣為大儒隱
然將與五經同垂不朽矣庸
===
非是錄之光哉斯固鎧之所
深望也
浙江湖州府長興縣儒學教
諭俞鎧謹序
punctuated:
登名是錄，駸駸焉有官守言責，尚益勵所學，嚴諸已，弘厥施，毋為情勝，毋為利撓，毋為習移，毋為私蔽，俾所以自治、所以治人與所以為學者一致。為孝子，為名臣，為大儒，隱然將與五經同垂不朽矣，庸非是錄之光哉？斯固鎧之所深望也。
浙江湖州府長興縣儒學教諭俞鎧謹序。
translation_en:
…have their names entered in this record and will before long hold official duties and responsibilities of remonstrance. May they further strengthen their learning, be exacting with themselves, and extend its application broadly. Let them neither be overcome by emotion, nor diverted by profit, nor swayed by habit, nor blinded by private interests, so that their means of governing themselves, governing others, and pursuing learning may be consistent. As filial sons, distinguished ministers, and great Confucian scholars, they will surely attain an immortality enduring alongside the Five Classics. Would this not bring glory to this record? This, indeed, is what I, Kai, deeply hope for.
Preface respectfully written by Yu Kai, Instructor of the Confucian School of Changxing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.
